status: Published 466-paper shortlist with alternate sensitivity scenarios
rating_rule: Significance 5; novelty, depth and exposition each ≥4; at least one of those three =5. Proof status is informational.
topic_rule: One primary topic per paper, based on its principal theorem. Secondary topics and ambiguous classifications are noted. These are our classifications, not official conference labels.
selection_rule: Retain every paper above the target-size weighted-score cutoff. Allocate the remaining positions among equal-score papers to minimize Σ (selected_topic − N × reference_share)² / (N × reference_share), subject to eligibility and available papers. Within each topic, resolve equal-score ties by submission number.
reference_rule: Equal weight to the STOC 2026 initial accepted-paper topic proportions (212 papers) and the FOCS 2026 accepted-paper topic proportions (174 papers). No SODA data. The target proportion is a soft comparison, not an enforceable cap.
rate_basis: 28% is the user-suggested working rate, not an officially verified STOC 2026 or FOCS 2026 rate. FOCS 2025 officially reports 137/546 = 25.09%; the comparison includes that lower-rate sensitivity. A secondary STOC 2026 report of 211/752 = 28.06% remains unverified and is not used as primary evidence.
caps_finding: No numerical quantum/online/other area caps were found in the inspected official CFPs and public policy materials. Confidential committee practices are unknown.
pc_use: The STOC 2027 roster was checked for representative expertise across all fourteen categories. Coverage is nonexclusive and is not converted into quota weights or predictions of member preferences.
caveats: The 1,665-paper denominator is this catalogue snapshot, not a verified official submission total.
STOC 2026 lists 212 accepted papers but 211 final proceedings papers/talks; one complexity paper is absent from the final program, for an unknown reason.
Historical accepted-paper proportions do not establish area-specific acceptance rates; submitted-paper topic denominators are unavailable.
Scores and proof notes are reused unchanged; this pass is not a fresh quality or correctness audit.
The corpus has substantial score ties. Submission-number tie-breaking is reproducible but does not imply a quality difference.
Topic balance applies only at the score cutoff, so stronger-paper floors and eligibility shortages can prevent exact historical proportions.
Topic classifications are coarse and some cross-area assignments are uncertain. STOC-only and FOCS-only scenarios show sensitivity to benchmark choice.

papers.title: Optimal Online Stochastic Matching
papers.authors: Paul Duetting, Michal Feldman, Mathieu Molina
papers.summary: Known-law unweighted online bipartite matching has optimal competitive ratio 1-exp(1-e), approximately .8206, for Poisson and finite i.i.d. arrivals, with a polynomial-time guarantee; unknown arrival laws are strictly worse.

papers.title: Faster enumeration of primes
papers.authors: David Harvey
papers.summary: Gives prime enumeration in N(log N)^(1/2)(log log N)^(1+o(1)) deterministic bit operations and expected N(log log N)^(2+o(1)) Las Vegas time. A faster N(log log N)^(1+o(1)) variant has a conjectural success guarantee but never silently returns an incorrect list. These are multitape-Turing asymptotic results, with roughly linear space and no practical implementation claim.

papers.title: Binary code rate bounds via classical-quantum channels
papers.authors: Omar Alrabiah, Venkatesan Guruswami
papers.classification_note: Classical binary-code rate bounds are the main theorem. Quantum channels are the proof method, not quantum-code results.
papers.summary: Introduces a classical–quantum channel criterion for binary-code rate bounds, recovers the classical Plotkin/Elias–Bassalygo/MRRW bounds, and claims strict improvements over both MRRW bounds throughout 0<δ<1/2 using mixed-qubit channels.

papers.title: Two ReLU layers is all you need
papers.authors: Kilian Rueß, Florestan Brunck, Christoph Hertrich, Jack Stade, Amir Yehudayoff
papers.summary: Every continuous piecewise-linear function over any real subfield containing Q is exactly representable by a ReLU network with two hidden layers, of unrestricted finite width. In particular MAX_n has a rational two-layer representation. No polynomial-width or efficient-learning claim follows.

papers.title: Breaking the Exponential Barrier: The First Polynomial-Time Algorithm for the Győri-Lovász Theorem
papers.authors: MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Alireza Kaviani, Soheil Mohammadkhani
papers.summary: First polynomial-time algorithm claimed for Győri–Lovász connected partitions with arbitrary terminal count; extends to directed k-T-connected graphs and prescribed capacities. Maintains assignments to flow-essential terminals; a weighted implementation yields O(n k m^(2+o(1))) time.

papers.title: An FPRAS for Mixed Volumes
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu
papers.summary: Claims the first FPRAS for mixed volume of arbitrary well-presented convex bodies, with a specified extension to lower-dimensional sets. Uses a spherical Alexandrov–Fenchel Poincare inequality, smoothing, and a capacity minimization that balances bodies before common rounding.

papers.title: A PTAS for the Minimum Sum of Radii Problem
papers.authors: Fabrizio Grandoni, Anupam Gupta, Jatin Yadav
papers.summary: Randomized PTAS for minimum sum of radii in arbitrary finite metrics, with centers allowed anywhere in the input metric, time n^(2^O(1/ε)) and high probability. Consequently obtains a (2+ε)-approximation for minimum sum of diameters.

papers.title: Online Shadow Tomography Matching the Classical Bounds
papers.authors: Sitan Chen, Ryan O'Donnell, Angelos Pelecanos, John Wright
papers.summary: Online shadow tomography of arbitrary d-dimensional states attains O(sqrt(m)/epsilon^2) copies and a complementary O(sqrt(K) log(m+K)/epsilon^2) bound with K=Theta(log(d)/epsilon^2), at constant simultaneous success probability.

papers.title: Quantum algorithms for stochastic nonlinear differential equations
papers.authors: Sergey Bravyi, Adam Byrne, Mykhaylo Zayats, Sergiy Zhuk, Alexander Zlokapa
papers.summary: For succinct sparse norm- and volume-preserving homogeneous quadratic drifts, estimates linear/quadratic observables of a Gaussian-initialized and Brownian-perturbed SDE in poly(T,log N,1/ε,1/p,1/q)exp(2||Y||²/p) quantum time. Identifies bounded-initial-norm parameters where noisy estimation is BQP-complete while the noiseless problem is PP-hard.

papers.title: Get Permanent Results Faster by Counting Stars
papers.authors: Radu Curticapean
papers.summary: Computes an n×n permanent over every commutative ring with identity in O*((2−10^-40)^n) ring operations and uniformly constructs an ABP of that size with variable/0/±1 labels. Rational matrices with B-bit entries have poly(B) times the same O* bound. The fixed polynomial exponent and constants are enormous; no practical speedup is implied.

papers.title: Approximating \#BIS in $\exp(\widetilde O(n^{1/3}))$ Time
papers.authors: Jingcheng Liu, Yitong Yin
papers.summary: Randomized approximate counting and TV sampling for independent sets in arbitrary bipartite graphs in exp(O(n^(1/3)log^(4/3)n)) times polynomial accuracy overhead. Generalizes to efficiently evaluable positive log-supermodular Boolean weights with dependence on log-weight range.

papers.title: Explicit functions requiring larger than 4.5n size circuits
papers.authors: Sam McGuire, Samuel Schlesinger, Ryan Williams
papers.summary: Constructs explicit polynomial-time Boolean functions requiring more than (4.5624−epsilon)n binary fan-in-two gates, and functions whose agreement with such circuits is at most 1/2+n^{-mu}. The larger 4.6155n constant is explicitly only an unverified candidate, not a theorem.

papers.title: No Perfect Randomized Composition
papers.authors: Alex Meiburg
papers.summary: Constructs total Boolean f,g with R(f∘g)=Theta(R(f)R(g)/log R(g)), refuting constant-factor randomized composition for total functions. Outer size N=2^{Theta(n^{4/5})}, so saving is Theta(log log L) in composition length L. Also claims multiple separations among sabotage, conflict, linearized and noisy complexity and composition limits.

papers.title: The k-server conjecture is true
papers.authors: Christian Coester, Elias Koutsoupias, Marek Zbysiński
papers.summary: Proves deterministic work-function algorithm k-competitive on every metric: WFA <= k OPT + clique(C0), with stronger terminal subtraction clique(XT). Handles pseudometrics and duplicate server locations through labeled points. No polynomial-time implementation of WFA is asserted.

papers.title: Optimal XOR Lemmas for Information Complexity
papers.authors: Alexander A. Sherstov
papers.summary: Establishes optimal XOR and direct-sum laws for information complexity. For total Boolean communication problems, IC_1/3(F XOR n)=Θ(n IC_1/(3n)(F)), apart from separable XOR functions; partial problems require the paper’s split-output information complexity term.

papers.title: On the most informative Boolean function under noise
papers.authors: Dimiter Kramer, Mert Saglam
papers.summary: Proves the Courtade–Kumar most-informative Boolean-function inequality through an inductive Shannon/Tsallis interpolation. The stronger bound is I(C;X)<=rho²H(C)−(rho²−(1−h(p)))4mu(1−mu), which is at most1−h(p). The manuscript acknowledges several concurrent proofs.

papers.title: Bounded Relative Boundary Implies Narrow DNF Approximation
papers.authors: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng
papers.summary: Proves Friedgut bounded-relative-boundary conjecture: increasing f under0<p<=1/2 with resampling influence<=K admits epsilon-close monotone DNF of width exp(O((K+1)^2/epsilon^2)), independent of dimension and bias. All-bias relative-boundary version follows separately. Existential width only; no term-count or efficient-construction guarantee.

papers.title: Efficient Randomized Communication Without Large Monochromatic Rectangles
papers.authors: Haoyu Wang, Pei Wu
papers.summary: Explicit total n-bit two-party function with randomized communication Theta(log n), yet every monochromatic rectangle has relative area2^{-Omega(n)}; separates BPP from P^NP and implies P^RP is strictly weaker than BPP in communication complexity.

papers.title: Solving Linear Programs in Truly Matrix Multiplication Time
papers.authors: Gernot Zöcklein, Rasmus Kyng, Shunhua Jiang
papers.summary: Claims expected n^(omega+o(1)) log(RW/epsilon) time for weakly polynomial approximate linear programming, removing the residual exponent barrier even if omega=2.

papers.title: Nearly Tight Approximation for Vertex-Disjoint Cycle Packing
papers.authors: Madhumita Kundu, William Lochet
papers.summary: Deterministic polynomial-time vertex-disjoint cycle packing of size Omega(nu*/sqrt(log nu*)), where nu* is natural LP optimum. Improves O(log n) to O(sqrt(log n)); integrality gap matches known lower bound within loglog n.

papers.title: Quantum Separability in Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Giulio Malavolta
papers.summary: Randomized polynomial-time weak separability membership for every fixed Frobenius-distance promise gap, using additive fixed-accuracy best separable state optimization for Frobenius-bounded Hermitian objectives. Does not give inverse-polynomial precision or trace-distance membership.

papers.title: The Modular Nash-Williams Theorem
papers.authors: Amir Jafari
papers.summary: Every compatible outdegree prescription modulo q admits k-arc-connected orientation when edge connectivity>=2q+2k-2 or q+2k-1 disjoint spanning trees exist. Exact universal strong-realization criterion tau_f>q; every three-flow-critical graph has m<=3n-6, improved to3n-7 for n>=5.

papers.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
papers.authors: Jan Dreier, Nikolas Mählmann, Szymon Toruńczyk
papers.summary: One uniform FO model-checking algorithm runs in O_C,phi,epsilon(n^(3+epsilon)) on every monadically dependent graph class, without a supplied decomposition. Together with hereditary hardness this characterizes tractability under FPT!=AW*. Parameter factor need not be computable; this is not strongly uniform FPT.

papers.title: Low-Error Extractors
papers.authors: Dean Doron, Jesse Goodman
papers.summary: Constructs explicit two-source extractors for entropy C n^{1−c}, error 2^{−c n^c}, and output k, for universal constants; affine extractors reach entropy n^{4/5+α}. Proves polynomial-loss approximate duality and logarithmic-in-n/d iteration rapid mixing after sacrificing d entropy bits.

papers.title: Vector Balancing in Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Shengtao Guo, Ethan X. Fang, Junwei Lu
papers.summary: Deterministic real-RAM algorithm finds signs with infinity-norm discrepancy≤8272 for every matrix whose columns have Euclidean norm≤1, in O((mn^9+n^10)log(2+m+n)) arithmetic operations; implies constant·sqrt(t) Beck–Fiala rounding.

papers.title: Subset Sum in Almost-Linear Time
papers.authors: Ce Jin, Xiao Mao
papers.summary: Deterministic positive-integer Subset Sum search in O(n+Δ^{1+o(1)}) word-RAM time for input values ≤Δ, including binary multiplicity formulation.

papers.title: Spectrum Estimation is Almost as Hard as Tomography
papers.authors: Marco Fanizza, Ryan O'Donnell, Chirag Wadhwa
papers.summary: For every γ>0, some dimension-independent error ε_γ yields Ω(d^{2−γ}) copies for spectrum/entropy estimation and constant-fraction rank testing; joint measurements allowed.

papers.title: On the Hardness of 4-to-1 Games with Perfect Completeness
papers.authors: Yumou Fei, Dor Minzer, Shuo Wang
papers.summary: For every constant ε>0 there is a finite alphabet size r for which distinguishing value 1 from at most ε in 4-to-1 Label Cover is NP-hard. Through stated reductions this yields hardness of coloring 3-colorable graphs with any fixed number of colors, and of finding constant-density independent sets in 2-colorable 3-uniform hypergraphs.

papers.title: BQP⊆IP Does Not Relativize
papers.authors: Adam Bouland, Andrew Huang, Anand Natarajan, Itay Shalit, Avishay Tal
papers.summary: Constructs a classical oracle O with BQP^O not contained in IP^O by proving Forrelation fools polynomial-depth, polynomial-message Avg-Max circuits. Together with the separately cited relativizing BQP-in-MIP theorem, gives IP^O!=MIP^O. Does not rule out unrelativized IP or cryptographic verification.

papers.title: Sharp Phase Transition for Ellipsoid Fitting
papers.authors: Sofia de la Cerda, Aaron Potechin, Madhur Tulsiani, Jeff Xu
papers.summary: Claims the sharp Gaussian centered-ellipsoid fitting threshold: for independent d-dimensional Gaussian points, a positive semidefinite fitting matrix exists with high probability for m<=(1-epsilon_d)d^2/4 and none exists for m>=(1+epsilon_d)d^2/4, with epsilon_d=1/poly(log log d). Gives explicit primal and dual witnesses via iterated spectral transformations and graph-matrix expansions. The model permits degenerate centered ellipsoids; the asymptotic slack is not optimized.

papers.title: An exponential separation between entanglement-assisted and unassisted one-way quantum communication
papers.authors: Ryan Anselm, Srijita Kundu, Olivier Lalonde, Ashwin Nayak
papers.summary: Exhibits total Boolean functions on n-bit inputs with O(log n) entanglement-assisted one-way classical communication, but Θ(n^{1/3}) unassisted one-way quantum and randomized communication at worst-case error 1/3. The upper bound uses Θ(n) shared EPR pairs; an entanglement-assisted SMP variant also exists.

papers.title: Sounder, shorter, and simpler PCPs from HDX neighborhoods
papers.authors: Yotam Dikstein, Irit Dinur, Max Hopkins, Noah G. Singer
papers.summary: Two-query PCP/Label Cover reduction of size n(log n)^C and soundness ε>(log n)^(-a), with alphabet exp((1/ε)^C), from new fixed-dimensional neighborhood agreement tests of total length n poly(1/ε) and poly(1/ε)-size views.

papers.title: A Sharp Dynamic Haussler Lemma
papers.authors: Shihao Shao, Dacheng Tao
papers.classification_note: Sequential causal experts and online-learning dimension determine primary topic; the cover bound is combinatorial.
papers.summary: For any [0,1]-valued class F with d=sfat_(epsilon/32)(F), constructs a single global family of deterministic causal experts of size at most (C/epsilon^p)^d, covering every length-T input sequence and every target in normalized l_p error epsilon. C is universal and independent of p and T; the experts are existential, with no computational efficiency claim. A fixed countable binary class of Littlestone dimension d requires more than (1/(2^(p+1)epsilon^p))^d experts on all sufficiently long horizons, even permitting arbitrary real-valued covering vectors.

papers.title: The Multiple Unicast Conjecture is False
papers.authors: Mark Braverman, Zhongtian He
papers.summary: Refutes the undirected multiple-unicast conjecture with a causal linear code over F9: a 182-vertex subgraph of the PG(2,9) incidence graph has 735 unit-capacity edges and 157 independent sessions of rate one, while every fractional multicommodity flow has common rate at most 147/157. The code has a fixed chronological vertex order and each physical edge transmits exactly one symbol per execution, so pipelining achieves the stated rate. A prior amplification theorem gives an unbounded polylogarithmic gap. A separate 166-session construction concerns nondeterministic certificates only.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Tusnády's Problem in the Plane
papers.authors: Zhewei Wei
papers.summary: Planar axis-parallel rectangle discrepancy is Theta(log^{3/2} n): independent uniform points have, with probability >=1-exp(-An), anchored discrepancy >=c_A(log_2 n)^{3/2} for every coloring. Resolves plane only; construction is probabilistic.

papers.title: Pseudorandom Functions in NC¹ from LWE/LPN/CDH (Or: How to Build Low-Depth PRFs, Generically)
papers.authors: Youlong Ding, Aayush Jain, Ilan Komargodski
papers.summary: Generically transforms polynomially secure weak PRFs of depth d(lambda) into strong PRFs of depth O(d(lambda)), for d/log nondecreasing. Instantiations give NC1 PRFs from polynomial-ratio LWE, standard LPN and CDH via synthesizers.

papers.title: All Unitaries Have Constant Depth Quantum Circuits
papers.authors: Barak Nehoran, Joseph Slote, Henry Yuen
papers.summary: Every n-qubit unitary has a clean exact circuit of one- and two-qubit gates of depth O(n), using 2^{O(n)} ancillas and unitary-dependent arbitrary rotations. Allowing exponentially large quantum fan-out yields constant depth. A fixed synthesis algorithm uses three queries to a target-dependent diagonal phase oracle on O(N loglog(N/epsilon)) qubits (six classical queries after phase computation), N=2^n, with operator-norm approximation. These are nonuniform depth/space tradeoffs, not efficient-size compilation or black-box Hamiltonian fast-forwarding.

papers.title: Asymmetry and Complexity of Nondeterministic Computations
papers.authors: Halley Goldberg, Jinqiao Hu, Zhenjian Lu, Jingyi Lyu, Igor Oliveira
papers.summary: Develops symmetry-of-information theory for nondeterministic nKt and randomized variants. Shows average-case symmetry for polynomial-time samplable distributions; worst-case symmetry would imply strong separations and collapses. Proves unconditional exponential NTIME intersect coNTIME lower bounds for estimating nKt, corresponding randomized/AM bounds, and quantitative equivalence among rnKt symmetry, gap meta-complexity and explicit construction properties.

papers.title: Convex optimization on moment polytopes: Hadamard mirror descent and efficient algorithms for quantum functionals and other tensor parameters
papers.authors: Mahmut Levent Doğan, Keiya Sakabe, Michael Walter
papers.classification_note: General convex optimization method is primary. Quantum functionals here are applications of the mathematical optimization framework, not the principal quantum-computation model.
papers.summary: Hadamard mirror descent minimizes holonomy-invariant convex objectives over gradients with O(1/k) convergence; applications give polynomial real-arithmetic iteration bounds for quantum functionals and related moment-polytope tensor parameters. General arbitrary convex objectives are not covered.

papers.title: Rapid mixing of Potts Glauber dynamics throughout uniqueness
papers.authors: Antonio Blanca, Reza Gheissari, Heehyun Park, Xusheng Zhang
papers.summary: For fixed q, Delta and beta strictly below tree uniqueness, Potts Glauber mixes in n polylog n and Swendsen-Wang in O(log n) on almost every random Delta-regular graph. On lattice cubes/tori below beta_c, inverse spectral gap is n^{1+o(1)}, giving mixing n^{2+o(1)}. A shattering/escape dichotomy avoids uniform correlation decay under arbitrary pinnings.

papers.title: Query-Optimal and Gate-Efficient Time-Dependent Hamiltonian Simulation
papers.authors: Boyang Chen, Minbo Gao, Zhengfeng Ji, Tongyang Li, Xinzhao Wang, Shuo Zhou
papers.summary: For beta-Lipschitz H(t) with norm at most alpha and coherent sampled HAM-T block-encoding access (including the controlled/inverse calls needed for Hermitianization), simulates time-ordered evolution with O(alpha T+log(1/epsilon)/log(e+log(1/epsilon)/(alpha T))) queries. Additional gate cost is O(q[a+log(1+T(alpha+beta T)/epsilon)]), counting arbitrary one/two-qubit gates.

papers.title: An $\tilde \Omega(\log n \log m)$ Information-Theoretic Lower Bound for Randomized Online Set Cover
papers.authors: Roie Levin
papers.summary: Randomized online set cover requires Omega(log n log m/(log log n+log log m)) competitive ratio against an oblivious adversary for log^2 n<=m<=2^n. The unknown-instance model reveals incidences only as elements arrive; the bound is independent of computational limits.

papers.title: Group Action and Spin Representation Lead to a Holant* Complexity Dichotomy on Domain Size 3
papers.authors: Jin-Yi Cai, Jin Soo Ihm
papers.summary: Gives a decidable polynomial-time versus #P-hard classification for domain-three Holant* with complex-valued symmetric signatures and all unary signatures freely available; high-arity signatures and binary matrix closures require a common compatibility criterion. This is not unrestricted domain-three Holant without free unaries.

papers.title: Polynomially larger deletion codes by linear hashing of substring counts
papers.authors: Eyal En Gad
papers.summary: For every fixed t>=2 and fixed alphabet q, there exist length-n codes correcting any t insertions, deletions and substitutions with redundancy (2t-1)log_q n+O_t(log_q log_q n). The same leading coefficient holds for t bounded substring replacements; no efficient encoder/decoder is claimed.

papers.title: No Truly Sublogarithmic-Round Algorithm for Distributed MIS in the LOCAL Model
papers.authors: Seri Khoury, Aaron Schild
papers.summary: Proves randomized LOCAL MIS requires Omega(log n/log log n) rounds for any fixed positive global success probability, even with IDs [n], exact n and constant-factor maximum degree knowledge. Hard graphs blow up a degree-Theta(log n) high-girth skeleton into polynomial-size cliques joined by dense random bipartite edges.

papers.title: Online carpooling against an oblivious adversary
papers.authors: Yuhao Lei
papers.summary: For every oblivious edge sequence, a randomized online orientation algorithm has maximum prefix vertex discrepancy O((log T)^(1/3)) with high probability, with explicit tail <=12T exp(-(D/40)^3) for D>=300. The selection rule is nonconstructive; polynomial-time implementation remains open.

papers.title: Entrywise Logarithmic Matrix Algebra and Dichotomy of Planar Graph Homomorphisms
papers.authors: Jin-Yi Cai, Zhuxiao Tang
papers.summary: Classifies planar graph-homomorphism partition functions for every fixed symmetric nonnegative real matrix: general-graph tractability, planar-only tractability via holographic FKT, or planar #P-hardness. The positive full-rank core has exactly scaled tensor products of symmetric 2-by-2 Ising matrices as tractable cases; zero entries and rank defects require additional block modifications.

papers.title: Tree Equivalence of Higher-Order Recursion Schemes Is Undecidable
papers.authors: Mingkun Xiao, Yixuan Sun
papers.classification_note: Undecidability/computability theorem fits complexity; taxonomy has no separate logic/verification category.
papers.summary: Tree equality for deterministic higher-order recursion schemes is Pi^0_1-complete, already for safe productive schemes of order at most four over one nullary and one binary symbol. The lower bound reduces nonhalting of deterministic two-counter machines. The general upper bound includes nonproductive schemes with bottom labels. Related lambda-Y equivalence transfers do not claim preservation of the same order/safety restriction.

papers.title: Averaged Annealed Markov Chains Achieve the Algorithmic Threshold for Tensor PCA, Part I: Glauber Dynamics
papers.authors: Aniket Das, Tselil Schramm
papers.classification_note: Recovery of a planted tensor signal is inference; the sampler is its algorithmic method.
papers.summary: For fixed tensor order k≥3, signed-hypercube Gaussian tensor PCA at λ≥C_k N^((k−2)/4) admits polynomial-time strong recovery from uniform initialization using high-temperature Glauber trajectory averaging followed by low-temperature dynamics. Odd k uses the averaged spin vector; general k uses an augmented second moment and its top eigenvector. Averaging is polynomially long, not near-input-linear, and this does not lower the general algorithmic SNR threshold.

papers.title: A Bulow--Klemperer Theorem for Bundling and Improved Approximation Bounds for Simple Auctions
papers.authors: Yichen Huang
papers.summary: For one additive bidder with independent nonnegative regular item values of finite monopoly revenue, optimal revenue is at most the reserve-free grand-bundle second-price revenue from two iid bidders, itself at most twice optimal one-bidder bundling; factor2 is tight. For arbitrary independent items, REV<=SREV+(pi^2/6)BREV, giving factor<2.645; a separate bounded-value construction exceeds2.11. Exact recovery by the better of optimal separate/bundle auctions can require Omega(log m) bidders without regularity.

papers.title: A Counting and Sampling Lovász Local Lemma
papers.authors: Hongyang Liu, Chunyang Wang, Yitong Yin, Yiyao Zhang, Can Zhou
papers.summary: For arbitrary finite-domain CSPs with evaluation access, explicit scopes, and 4e p(D+1)²≤1, gives deterministic approximate counting in (nD/ε)^O(kD log q), randomized counting in Õ(poly(k,D,q)(n/ε)²), and exactly uniform sampling in expected Õ(n+kmD²) time with O(m) oracle evaluations. Thus fixed-local-parameter counting/sampling reaches the pD² scale, not the weaker satisfiability pD scale.

papers.title: A Better-than-e^{1/e} Approximation Algorithm for Nash Social Welfare under Additive Valuations
papers.authors: Vignesh Viswanathan
papers.classification_note: Nash social welfare allocation; aligned with #916 and historical welfare papers.
papers.summary: For unweighted Nash social welfare with additive valuations, gives a randomized polynomial-time approximation e^(1/e)-c for an absolute c>0. The manuscript estimates c only around 10^-80 and explicitly does not optimize it; this is a barrier-breaking asymptotic improvement, not a practically substantial constant reduction.

papers.title: A Unified Complexity Framework for Quantum Property Testing
papers.authors: Qisheng Wang
papers.summary: Gives a moment-matching master lower bound for spectral functionals L_phi(rho)=tr(phi(d rho))/d, with copies Omega(d^2/M^2) under explicit concentration and Lipschitz hypotheses. Applies it to entropy, spectrum, purity, distances and Renyi functionals, and transfers sample bounds to purified-access query bounds. Claimed tight entropy complexity uses an upper bound from a separate cited work.

papers.title: $\ell_{\infty}$ norm SVP in $\widetilde{O}(3^n)$
papers.authors: Yiming Gao
papers.summary: Claims an exact infinity-norm shortest-vector randomized algorithm using O-tilde(3^n) time and space on rational full-rank lattices, with worst-case resource caps and success at least 2/3. Also yields bounded-integer subset balancing in O-tilde(3^n), improving meet-in-the-middle for d>=5.

papers.title: Algebraic-Geometric Parvaresh--Vardy Subspace Designs and Rank Condensers
papers.authors: Gil Cohen, Dean Doron, Noam Goldgraber
papers.classification_note: Subspace-design/rank-condenser construction is pseudorandomness; coding is a major method overlap.
papers.summary: Constructs explicit strong subspace designs over every finite field with codimension r, A=O(q^3 r k/gamma^5), and average intersection at most (1/q+gamma) times test-subspace dimension. Obtains rank condensers with constant field size, constant output entropy rate and optimal linear ambient-dimension dependence; construction time is polynomial in q, not log q.

papers.title: LOCAL LLL in poly(loglog n) Rounds
papers.authors: Maxime Flin, Mohsen Ghaffari, Magnus M. Halldorsson, Yannic Maus, Alexandre Nolin
papers.summary: Solves the variable LLL in randomized poly(log log n) LOCAL rounds with arbitrary inverse-polynomial failure probability under p*d^1000<1. Nodes know polynomial size, degree and probability upper bounds; message size and local computation are unrestricted.

papers.title: From Degree Three to Degree Two: Statistical Randomized Encodings for All Functions
papers.authors: Emmanuela Orsini, Arpita Patra
papers.summary: Every Boolean function has statistical randomized encodings of degree two jointly in original input and independent uniform random bits, with correctness and privacy errors <=2^-lambda and complexity polynomial in mod-2 branching-program size plus lambda. Locality-three decomposable encodings and locality-three OWFs from uniform-NC1 OWFs follow. Multiparty effective-degree-two encodings protect every static semi-honest coalition, allowing arbitrary local preprocessing. This permits negligible correctness error; it is not a perfectly correct statistical encoding nor unconditional polynomial overhead in circuit size.

papers.title: UPPcc is Not Closed Under Intersection
papers.authors: Mark Bun, Mandar Juvekar
papers.summary: Constructs explicit bounded-integer-halfspace matrices with sign rank Θ(d) whose disjoint-input two-fold conjunction has sign rank 2^Θ(d), with 2^Θ(d²) rows/columns. Consequently O(log n) unbounded-error communication can rise to Ω(√n), proving UPP^cc is not intersection-closed. This does not contradict intersection closure of PP or PP^cc.

papers.title: Quantum Lazy Sampling and Path Recording for Any Group
papers.authors: Ben Foxman, Alex Lombardi, Fermi Ma, Barak Nehoran, John Wright
papers.summary: Develops exact path-recording simulation for Haar-random elements of any compact group represented in U(N), with O(t log N) recording qubits after t queries. Efficient updates require efficient compatible representation-theoretic transforms; the general formula alone is not an efficient algorithm. Applies the framework to permutation-times-Clifford pseudorandom unitaries.

papers.title: QMA has perfect completeness
papers.authors: Sabee Grewal, Dorian Rudolph
papers.summary: Proves QMA=QMA₁ with exact Hadamard–Toffoli verification. A polynomial-bit rational diagonal entry of a power of the acceptance operator closes a finite nonunitary history into an exact cycle; a global kernel test gives perfect completeness and constant soundness. The construction depends on verifier arithmetic and does not relativize to arbitrary quantum oracles.

papers.title: Directed Global Minimum Cut in Almost-Linear Time
papers.authors: Henry Fleischmann, Jason Li, Thatchaphol Saranurak, Benyu Wang
papers.summary: Computes directed global minimum cut with high probability using maximum-flow instances of total size O-tilde(m), plus O-tilde(m) additional time. For polynomially bounded positive integral weights this gives m^(1+o(1)) time. The key is marginal contraction of a random arborescence without constructing an approximate arborescence packing.

papers.title: The Polynomial-Time Low-Degree Conjecture is False
papers.authors: Songtao Mao
papers.summary: For every fixed r>=3, constructs vertex-permutation-invariant simple-graph distributions P_n matching G(n,1/2) exactly on every set of Theta((log n)^(r-1)) edges, yet a uniform deterministic O(n^2)-time rank test strongly distinguishes after any fixed resampling rate epsilon in [0,epsilon_r], for some sufficiently small positive epsilon_r. The sampler is nonuniform with polynomial advice; uniform polynomial-time sampling remains open. Thus the stated symmetric, uniform-null, noisy polynomial-time low-degree conjecture fails without an additional hypothesis.

papers.title: A Proof of the Most Informative Boolean Function Conjecture
papers.authors: Zijie Chen, Amin Gohari, Adel Javanmard, Honghao Lin, Vahab Mirrokni, Chandra Nair, David Woodruff
papers.classification_note: Mutual-information inequality for Boolean functions/channels, rather than a circuit or communication lower bound.
papers.summary: Claims a computer-assisted proof of the full Courtade–Kumar most-informative Boolean function conjecture: I(g(X);Y) <= 1-H_2(p), in every dimension for every Boolean function and crossover probability. A hybrid Bellman inequality handles biased functions, with analytic boundary arguments and certified compact-region inequalities.

papers.title: Second-Best Trade Is Half Efficient in Multidimensional Markets
papers.authors: Dirk Bergemann, Yang Cai, Kangning Wang, Jinzhao Wu, Renzhe Xu
papers.summary: For finite-support additive multidimensional buyers and sellers with independent agents but arbitrary within-agent correlation and arbitrary downward-closed trade feasibility, proves existence of a Bayesian-IC, interim-IR, reportwise strongly budget-balanced mechanism attaining at least half of first-best gains from trade.

papers.title: Optimal $e^{(\gamma+o(1))n}$-Approximation of the Permanent of Positive Semidefinite Matrices
papers.authors: Nima Anari, Farzam Ebrahimnejad
papers.summary: For rational Hermitian positive-semidefinite A, gives a deterministic polynomial-time exp((γ+ε)n)-approximation to per(A), where γ is Euler’s constant and ε>0. The exact real-arithmetic relaxation satisfies exp(−γn) exp Φ(A)≤per(A)≤exp Φ(A), with Φ maximizing Σlog(vᵢ†Xvᵢ)+log det X−tr X+d over positive-definite X for A=VV†. Entries may be complex; no entrywise nonnegativity assumption.

papers.title: Catalytic Tree Evaluation from Matching Vectors
papers.authors: Alexandra Henzinger, Edward Pyne, Seyoon Ragavan
papers.summary: For every fixed ε>0, solves TreeEval in O(log n) free space, 2^O((log n)^ε) catalytic space and polynomial time. A generic matching-vector/decoder construction gives additional tradeoffs and a multitape-time-T simulation using O(√T) free space, 2^O(T^ε) catalytic space and 2^O(√T) time.

papers.title: Solving $p$-norm regression in matrix multiplication time
papers.authors: Deeksha Adil, Brian Bullins, Liam O'Carroll, Aaron Sidford
papers.summary: Randomized high-accuracy ℓp regression in soft-O_p(nd^(ω−1)) for fixed p≥2 and soft-O_p(nnz(A)+d^ω) for fixed 1<p≤2; for p=∞ obtains soft-O(nd^(ω−1)poly(1/ε)). For n≈d this is matrix-multiplication time for every ω. The dependence near p=1 is exponential in 1/(p−1).

papers.title: Tight Approximation Bounds for Clock Auctions
papers.authors: Mahyar Afshinmehr, Josh Ascher, Arash Ashuri, Vasilis Gkatzelis, Pouria Mahmoudkhan, Aviad Rubinstein, Daniel Schoepflin
papers.summary: Establishes tight Θ(log n/log log n) worst-case welfare approximation for randomized clock auctions on arbitrary downward-closed single-parameter feasibility, with matching Θ(log log d/log log log d) overlap dependence. The lower bound holds for known i.i.d. priors and extends to OSP mechanisms with no negative transfers and ex-post IR; disjoint maximal sets admit a prior-free 32-approximation.

papers.title: Breaking the Parity Barrier for Constant-Depth Circuits
papers.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Xin Li, Ivan Mihajlin, Yan Zhong
papers.summary: For every fixed depth d≥3, proves 2^Ω((n log n)^(1/(d−1))) AND/OR circuit size for a standard trilinear Toeplitz function and inverse trace over F_(2^n). Gives stronger-than-parity average-case bounds in explicit size ranges and restricted-fan-in depth-three bounds answering a cited longstanding question.

papers.title: Algorithmic List Decoding of Reed–Solomon Codes up to Capacity
papers.authors: Joshua Brakensiek, Yeyuan Chen, Aaron Putterman, Zihan Zhang, Kai Zhe Zheng
papers.summary: Gives polynomial-time list decoding of Reed–Solomon codes up to capacity over prime fields with arbitrary evaluation points and sufficiently large linear-in-blocklength field size. The low-rate derivative-interpolation theorem combines with a rate reduction to obtain constant-rate guarantees.

papers.title: Hitting sets From Derivations: Waring Rank and Noncommutative ABPs
papers.authors: Shubham Bhardwaj, Foram Lakhani, Partha Mukhopadhyay, Ramprasad Saptharishi, Pratik Shastri, Amit Sinhababu
papers.summary: Constructs polynomial-size hitting sets in characteristic zero for polynomials with bounded partial-derivative dimension, including powering circuits, and for noncommutative algebraic branching programs using matrix substitutions. The generator uses truncated logarithms and a formal-derivation Wronskian.

papers.title: Testing Implies Distance Estimation with Polynomial Loss
papers.authors: Gaia Carenini, Cameron Seth
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Every isomorphism-closed dense graph property with q(ε)-query testing admits additive-ε distance estimation using poly(max{1,q(cε)},1/ε) queries, for an absolute c>0. The tester may be adaptive/two-sided; computation can be exhaustive and the original input size remains available to the sampled predicate.

papers.title: The Entire Quantum Computer on a Classical Leash
papers.authors: Yael Kalai, Dakshita Khurana, Justin Raizes
papers.summary: Assuming post-quantum LWE, a classical client and one quantum server can securely evaluate general real quantum circuits with abort and ε-simulation, preserving private quantum state across sequential computations. Applications obtain negligible computational error for sampling verification and negligible loss in falsifiable RSP games; general simulation itself remains ε-dependent.

papers.title: Reed–Solomon Codes Beyond Johnson: Efficient Decoding and Smaller Cryptographic Proofs
papers.authors: Quang Dao, Scott Kominers, Justin Thaler
papers.summary: For Reed–Solomon codes on arbitrary prescribed evaluation points, gives an explicit first-hidden-derivative agreement curve below Johnson, list size Oρ(n/η²), and line-MCA exceptional count Oρ(n²/η⁴), subject to sufficiently large characteristic. Deterministic decoding is soft-O(n³ log q) at fixed rate/gap beyond this curve and polynomial in n,log q at fixed gap from capacity. Above Johnson, improves MCA gap dependence from η^−5 to η^−3 in every characteristic.

papers.title: Factor Closure in Noncommutative Algebraic Complexity
papers.authors: V. Arvind, Pushkar S Joglekar
papers.classification_note: Factor closure for arithmetic circuit/formula complexity classes, rather than a numerical arithmetic algorithm.
papers.summary: Over every field, every specified one-sided factor of a degree-D polynomial computed by a size-s noncommutative circuit has size O(sD³), and every factor in f=agb has size O(sD⁶). Formulas have O(s²)/O(s⁴) factor bounds; VP_nc and VNP_nc are factor-closed. Constants are arbitrary field elements at unit arithmetic cost; the construction requires cofactor-word/suffix-coefficient data.

papers.title: Cube-Root Soundness Is Optimal for the Line–versus–Point Test
papers.authors: Quang Dao, Scott Kominers, Justin Thaler, Kai Zhe Zheng
papers.summary: The line-versus-point test over every finite field and dimension m≥2 guarantees degree-d global agreement at least acceptance−O((d/q)^{1/3}). Explicit cubic-extension examples show the exponent 1/3 is optimal, including fixed degree; higher-degree construction is given in dimension ≥3.

papers.title: A classical oracle separation between QMA and QMA(2)
papers.authors: Sabee Grewal, Saachi Mutreja, Kabir Tomer
papers.summary: Constructs a classical oracle relative to which QMA differs from QMA(2), using signed-permutation access to a separable Hamiltonian problem. YES has a zero-energy product state; NO has entangled zero-energy states but constant energy for every product state.

papers.title: A Walk from Free Probability to Matrix Discrepancy I: Matrix Spencer
papers.authors: Tarun Kathuria
papers.summary: Claims the full Matrix Spencer bound: for real symmetric m×m matrices A_i with ‖A_i‖≤1, finds signs with discrepancy at most 4000√(n·max{1,1+log(2m/n)}). A randomized algorithm has polynomial real-arithmetic time and failure ≤2^−b; polynomial bit complexity is explicitly not claimed.

papers.title: Matrix Lewis Weights: Solving Semidefinite Programs in Square Root Constraints Iterations
papers.authors: Jonathan Kelner, Shunhua Jiang, Aaron Sidford, Lichen Zhang
papers.summary: Introduces a matrix Lewis barrier for semidefinite programming with approximately square-root(m) path-following iterations, replacing the log-determinant barrier's square-root(n) dependence when constraints m are smaller than matrix order n. Gives a randomized sketched implementation and explicit running-time improvement regimes.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Polylogarithmic Quantum Shadow Tomography
papers.authors: Fernando Jeronimo, Qizhao Huang, Lenny Liu
papers.summary: Claims dimension-independent shadow tomography using O(epsilon^(-2) log M log(M/delta)) state copies. A minimax reduction to finite ensembles is paired with an observable-independent recovery-label measurement and simultaneous estimation guarantees.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial Trace Reconstruction
papers.authors: Arnav Burudgunte, Paul Valiant, Hongao Wang
papers.classification_note: Deletion-channel trace reconstruction sample complexity is classical information theory; learning is an overlap.
papers.summary: Reconstructs every unknown n-bit string from exp(p^(−7/3)(log₂n)^c) deletion-channel traces for an absolute c and retention p>0. This is quasipolynomial sample complexity when p is inverse-polylogarithmic or larger. Pairwise distinguishing is quasipolynomial time, but unrestricted reconstruction uses exponential candidate enumeration in this paper.

papers.title: A Linear Lower Bound for Convex Body Chasing in Every Norm
papers.authors: Nicolas Christianson
papers.summary: Proves a universal Ω(d) competitive-ratio lower bound for convex body chasing in every norm on R^d, including randomized algorithms and compact convex requests. Matches the known O(d) upper bound; the construction is nonnested.

papers.title: Sublinear Metric Distortion for Matching
papers.authors: Moses Charikar, Alireza Haqi, Jabari Hastings, Yichen Huang, Prasanna Ramakrishnan
papers.classification_note: Ordinal social-choice distortion and mechanism comparisons determine economics, even though the new matching rule is not asserted truthful.
papers.summary: Using only each agent’s ordinal ranking of n items in an unknown common metric, constructs a randomized one-sided perfect matching with expected distortion O(n^{log_4 3}), the first sublinear bound. Also claims RSD lower bound Ω(n/√log n), PS distortion Θ((√10/3)^n), and new truthful-mechanism lower bounds. The new sublinear mechanism is not asserted truthful; deterministic soft-O(n^{log_4 3}) follows from an external derandomization result.

papers.title: A Better-than-2 Approximation for k-Median
papers.authors: Rares-Darius Buhai, Vincent Cohen-Addad, Henry Fleischmann, Anupam Gupta, Antoni Jubés Monforte, Madhusudhan Reddy Pittu, Miltiadis Stouras, Ola Svensson, Lukas Vogl
papers.summary: Claims a randomized polynomial-time 1.95-approximation for general-metric k-median, combining a stronger facility-location pseudo-approximation with an improved stable-instance algorithm. The final solution respects the k-center budget.

papers.title: On Brouwer's Laplacian conjecture
papers.authors: Pravesh Kothari, Stefan Tudose
papers.summary: Proves Brouwer’s Laplacian conjecture for every finite simple graph: the sum of the largest k Laplacian eigenvalues is at most m+binom(k+1,2). Establishes an implication cycle with the Grone–Merris–Bai majorization theorem through centered split-graph nuclear norms and a projection routing inequality.

papers.title: A deterministic $(1+\varepsilon)^n$ approximation for the permanent of a nonnegative matrix
papers.authors: Vishesh Jain, Dingding Dong
papers.summary: For every fixed ε>0, a deterministic algorithm approximates any nonnegative n×n permanent within (1+ε)^n in n^{O(ε^{-2} log³(2/ε))} arithmetic operations. Rational inputs have polynomially bounded intermediate bit lengths. This is exponential-factor approximation, not an FPTAS.

papers.title: The Sharp Dimension Bound in the Johnson--Lindenstrauss Lemma
papers.authors: Vishesh Jain
papers.summary: Proves every n-point subset of R^d admits a linear (1+epsilon)-distortion embedding into O(min{d,n-1,epsilon^-2 log(2+epsilon^2 n)}) dimensions, resolving the full-range Johnson–Lindenstrauss dimension conjecture. The new central lemma halves PSD rank while controlling m quadratic forms with error O(sqrt(log(2+m/r^2)/r)).

papers.title: Superlattice methods for the shortest vector problem and discrete Gaussian sampling
papers.authors: Minki Hhan, Jiseung Kim, Sunyeop Kim, Thijs Laarhoven
papers.classification_note: Classical SVP and lattice sampling are primary; quantum tradeoffs are secondary.
papers.summary: Claims worst-case exact SVP in 2^{0.4385n+o(n)} time and 2^{0.3015n+o(n)} space, with further time-space and quantum tradeoffs. Also gives arbitrary-width centered discrete Gaussian sampling in (3/2)^{n/2+o(n)} time and space with exponentially small statistical error; this does not claim equally fast shifted sampling.

papers.title: An $\widetilde{O}(n^3)$-time FPRAS for the Permanent
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Heng Guo, Eric Vigoda, Xiongxin Yang
papers.summary: An FPRAS for the permanent of arbitrary n by n 0/1 matrices uses O(n^3 epsilon^-2 log^6(n/epsilon)) arithmetic operations and O(n^3 epsilon^-2 log^8(n/epsilon)) bit operations. Nonnegative matrices have the same strongly polynomial arithmetic-operation bound, in the unit-cost model.

papers.title: Quadratic Probing Insertions Are $\epsilon^{-(1+o(1))}$ Time
papers.authors: Yang S. Hu, William Kuszmaul, Jingxun Liang, Stefan Walzer, Huacheng Yu, Renfei Zhou
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Quadratic probing with independent uniform key hashes, prime table size n, insertion-only workload and ε>1/√log n has expected next-insertion cost ε^{-(1+o(1))} at load 1−ε. A fallback scans the table after the quadratic sequence. The result does not establish the exact O(1/ε) conjecture or a bounded-independence implementation.

papers.title: $0/1$-Polytopes with Exponentially Small Edge Expansion
papers.authors: Xiongxin Yang
papers.summary: Constructs full-dimensional 0/1-polytopes in dimension 4n+1 whose graph edge expansion is at most 4n β^n/(1−β^n), where β=(1+√6)²/12<1. Thus general 0/1-polytopes can have exponentially small expansion, disproving both the Mihail–Vazirani bound h≥1 and any universal inverse-polynomial lower bound.

papers.title: Counting Linear Extensions Faster than $2^n$
papers.authors: Keigo Oka
papers.classification_note: Exact counting algorithm classified counting_sampling, despite exact-exponential discrete-algorithm methods.
papers.summary: Deterministically counts linear extensions of an arbitrary n-element poset in O*(33^{n/6})<O*(1.791^n) time and space. There are no width, height or dimension assumptions; exponential space remains necessary for the presented algorithm.

papers.title: Exponential Separation of Sign-Rank and Margin Complexity
papers.authors: Gabriel Hart, Kaave Hosseini
papers.summary: For k≥1 and equality bit length n≥10k2^k, proves 2^k≤sign-rank(OR_k∘EQ_n)≤2^(k+1)−1 while margin complexity is at most 2k+1. Produces explicit N×N sign matrices with margin complexity O(log log N) and sign-rank Ω(log N/(log log N)²), an exponential separation in the margin parameter.

papers.title: Reed--Muller Codes are Optimal Binary Linear 3-Query LCCs
papers.authors: Oliver Janzer, Peter Manohar
papers.summary: Proves that a binary linear (3,δ,ε)-locally correctable code with ε<1/2 has block length n≥2^(Ω(δ⁷√k)). Thus constant-radius binary linear 3-query LCCs match the Reed–Muller exponent up to constants; the theorem does not cover nonlinear codes or merely locally decodable codes.

papers.title: Single-Variable Connectivity in Random $k$-SAT
papers.authors: Chunyang Wang, Yitong Yin, Yixiao Yu, Yiyao Zhang
papers.classification_note: Random-CSP solution geometry/connectivity and threshold structure are primary; no general SAT algorithm claimed.
papers.summary: For sufficiently large fixed k, proves typical-solution single-bit connectivity up to density (2^k/k)(ln k+ln ln k+γ*−o_k(1)), γ*≈0.871, and locates first reconstruction onset at the matching +o_k(1) scale. Looseness persists to the higher constant-1 threshold; shattering with linear energy barriers is proved from ln(34/13)≈0.9614. These are high-probability random-formula/typical-solution results, not connectivity of every solution.

papers.title: An Explicit and Optimal Separation of BPP from NP in Number-on-Forehead Communication Complexity
papers.authors: Haoyu Wang, Yimeng Wang, Pei Wu
papers.summary: For every fixed k≥3 constructs explicit polynomial-time computable total Boolean functions with O_k(1) public-coin one-sided-error NOF communication and Ω_k(n) nondeterministic communication, hence also linear deterministic communication. Constants depend on k; this is a communication-class separation, not ordinary BPP versus NP.

papers.title: Random-Walk Cuckoo Hashing is Efficient up to the Critical Load Threshold
papers.authors: Yang S. Hu, William Kuszmaul, Jingxun Liang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Proves near-linear dependence on inverse threshold slack for random-walk d-ary cuckoo insertions: expected insertion time (ε−ε*_d)^(−1−O(1/√(d log d))) for sufficiently large fixed d, conditioned on a hash-only event of probability 1−O(1/n). For each fixed d≥3 it gives polynomial inverse-slack dependence, and away from the critical window obtains O(1/ε). Parameters d and positive slack are fixed before taking sufficiently large n.

papers.title: Sharp Bounds for Truthful-in-Expectation Scheduling
papers.authors: Yunpeng Li
papers.classification_note: Truthful mechanism performance is primary, so economics rather than online or generic scheduling.
papers.summary: Claims the optimal truthful-in-expectation expected-makespan ratio (n+1)/2 for n≥7 unrelated strategic machines. The lower bound allows unrestricted computation and correlated jobs but assumes finite expected payments and one approximation ratio uniformly over all finite job counts. A correlated Bounded-Square mechanism is expected-polynomial bit-time on rational reports; n=4,5,6 have separate nonmatching upper bounds.

papers.title: Nearly Linear Private Learning of Littlestone Classes
papers.authors: Shay Moran, Chao Yan
papers.summary: Gives an approximate-DP realizable PAC learner for every nonempty binary class of Littlestone dimension d≥1 using O((d log(d/(αεδ))+log(1/β))/(αε)) samples. This is O(d log d) for fixed parameters and does not assert computational efficiency or properness for general classes. Subspace indicators admit a proper learner with linear d dependence, independent of ambient dimension.

papers.title: An $O(1)$ Bound for the KLS Constant
papers.authors: Zhao Song, Xinzhi Zhang
papers.summary: Claims a dimension-independent Poincare constant for every isotropic log-concave probability measure, and hence a constant reciprocal Cheeger bound resolving KLS, including nonsmooth and bounded-support measures.

papers.title: Semi-Streaming Reachability and Shortest Paths in $n^{1/3+o(1)}$ Passes
papers.authors: Gary Hoppenworth, George Z. Li, Sepideh Mahabadi, Jakub Tarnawski
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Computes exact directed SSSP with high probability in n^(1/3+o(1)) passes and soft-O(n) space for nonnegative polynomially bounded integer weights. Also gives improved directed reachability and work-depth tradeoffs. Implicit shortcuts/hopsets store block descriptions rather than all closure edges.

papers.title: A Tale of Two Walks: From Kac to KMP and Back
papers.authors: Qian Chen, Jingcheng Liu, Minglong Qin, Leonard J. Schulman, Fang Song, Penghui Yao, Mingnan Zhao
papers.classification_note: Classical KMP and coordinate-Hit-and-Run mixing are primary; quantum Kac-twirling consequences form an important overlap.
papers.summary: On every connected d-vertex graph, bounds the t-particle KMP mixing time within O(log d) of single-particle mixing uniformly over t. Coordinate hit-and-run on the standard n-simplex mixes in O(n(log n+log(1/ε))) from any initial distribution. Parallel Kac twirling converges in trace norm after O(log d+log(1/ε)) steps for every t, restricted to symmetric-subspace input states.

papers.title: High-Multiplicity Bin Packing is FPT
papers.authors: Tomohiro Koana, Soh Kumabe
papers.classification_note: Exact integer/bin-packing optimization is primary, despite fixed-parameter formulation.
papers.summary: Decides high-multiplicity Bin Packing deterministically in 2^{d^{O(d)}} times a polynomial of fixed exponent in the binary input length, parameterized solely by d distinct sizes. Both sizes and multiplicities are binary. The result is exact decision, with no additive bin allowance.

papers.title: Time/Space Hardness from Lattice Problems
papers.authors: Damiano Abram, Giulio Malavolta, Lawrence Roy
papers.classification_note: Topic classification only: this does not override the unresolved audit status caused by essential imported proof sources being unavailable.
papers.summary: From the specified Decomposed SIS hardness assumption constructs correlation-intractable functions yielding average-case memory hardness and sequentiality, hence P!=L, P!=NC, and a proper uniform NC hierarchy. The assumption is a structured/extended SIS variant with parameter-specific extension width and short-solution bound beta<q; it is not claimed from ordinary SIS or ordinary worst-case SVP. Homomorphic lattice encodings support iteration without fixing a depth cap or bootstrapping.

papers.title: A Full Complexity Dichotomy for Complex-Valued Boolean Holant Problems
papers.authors: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng, Juqiu Wang
papers.summary: Claims a complete FP versus #P-hard dichotomy under polynomial-time Turing reductions for every fixed finite set of exact algebraic complex-valued Boolean signatures on general graphs. A separately decidable seven-form tractability criterion is inherited from prior work; the new contribution is hardness for the unrestricted all-even case.

papers.title: Breaking the $2^n$ barrier for directed hamiltonicity
papers.authors: Tomohiro Koana, Soh Kumabe
papers.summary: One-sided randomized O(1.9133^n)-time algorithm for Directed Hamiltonian Cycle on unrestricted n-vertex digraphs, using exponential space; does not give the analogous sub-2^k directed k-Path algorithm.

papers.title: On the Quantum Chromatic Gap II
papers.authors: Lorenzo Ciardo, Antoine Mottet
papers.summary: For every d≥4, ε>0 and context radius k, constructs a d-to-1 game of classical value<ε with a perfect finite-dimensional k-compatible quantum strategy. Via the cited quantum-complete coloring reductions, this yields graphs with quantum chromatic number3 and arbitrarily large classical chromatic number.

papers.title: Splay trees are almost dynamically optimal
papers.authors: Petr Chmel, Bernhard Haeupler, Richard Hladík, Michal Koucký, Antti Roeyskoe, Václav Rozhoň, Ondřej Sladký, Robert E. Tarjan
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: BST dynamic-optimality theorem belongs to data structures by shared rule, even though the guarantee is competitive against offline optimum.
papers.summary: Proves splay-tree access cost O((OPT+n)*log log n*(log log log n)^2) from any initial splay tree, against the offline dynamic BST optimum. Also proves the split conjecture within the same polyloglog factor. This is a first sublogarithmic competitive bound for splay trees, not constant-factor dynamic optimality; the additive n factor is essential for arbitrary initialization.

papers.title: Primal/Dual Method for the Grothendieck Constant
papers.authors: Steven Heilman, Chris Jones, Giulio Malavolta
papers.classification_note: Grothendieck constant and its functional-analytic characterization are primary; approximation-algorithm rounding is the method/application overlap.
papers.summary: Claims the real Grothendieck constant lies in [1.773,1.7799], with a separate heuristic estimate near1.779. Gives a Gaussian primal/dual characterization linking Hermite projection games and Krivine rounding distributions; the numerical endpoints depend on large rigorous certificates.

papers.title: A Quadratic Lower Bound for Noncommutative Circuits
papers.authors: Sophus Valentin Willumsgaard, Pratik Shastri
papers.summary: Proves an optimal Omega(n*d) product-gate lower bound for arbitrary fan-in-two noncommutative circuits computing the degree-2d palindrome polynomial in 2n variables, without homogeneity or syntactic-degree restrictions. Thus d=n gives a quadratic lower bound. The same argument applies to any degree-2d polynomial in n variables whose middle coefficient matrix has full rank. A functional-ring corollary additionally invokes a transfer theorem.

papers.title: A polynomial scaling window for random k-SAT and a proof of the satisfiability conjecture
papers.authors: Gaia Carenini
papers.classification_note: Random-SAT threshold existence and scaling-window geometry, without a SAT algorithm, is classified combinatorics_geometry.
papers.summary: For every fixed k≥3, the random signed k-SAT unsatisfiability hitting time has variance O_k(n^(1+2/k)), giving O_k,η(n^(1/2+1/k)) scaling windows and existence of a limiting threshold density α_k. Does not identify the numerical threshold or give an efficient SAT algorithm.

papers.title: Undirected Multiple-Unicast Network Coding and Faster External-Memory Integer Sorting
papers.authors: Baochun Li, Zongpeng Li, Sirui Liu
papers.classification_note: Undirected network-coding advantage is primary; external-memory integer sorting is a consequence.
papers.summary: Claims a strict coding advantage over fractional routing for undirected multiple-unicast networks, and derives a deterministic external-memory integer-sorting bound improving comparison sorting in some parameter regimes.

papers.title: Extending Tardos's Theorem to Separable Convex Quadratic Programming
papers.authors: Bin Cui, Hanqing Li, Xupeng Miao
papers.summary: Extends Tardos operation bounds to continuous separable convex quadratic programs Ax=b,x≥0 with integer A and arbitrary rational linear costs and nonnegative diagonal quadratic weights. Exact primal–dual optimum or infeasibility/unboundedness certificates use poly(r,m,encoding(A)) rational operations, independent of b,c,q lengths, with polynomial intermediate encodings.

papers.title: Incremental All-Pairs Effective Resistance in Almost-Linear Time
papers.authors: Gernot Zöcklein, Rasmus Kyng, Maximilian Probst Gutenberg, Gramoz Goranci, Yibin Zhao
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Maintains(1±ε) effective resistances and energies of polylog-sparse component-balanced demands in an initially empty undirected graph under edge insertions. For O(m) operations, total time m·(1/ε)^{O(sqrt(log n log log n))}, with high probability against an oblivious adversary and polynomial capacity ratio.

papers.title: Nearly Optimal Hardness for CVP and NCP with Preprocessing
papers.authors: Guy Weissenberg, Giacomo Fenzi
papers.classification_note: Joint CVP/NCP preprocessing hardness; complexity primary, with lattice/coding secondary.
papers.summary: Unless NP⊆P/poly, polynomial-size arbitrary preprocessing and polynomial online time cannot approximate NCP over any fixed finite field within M^(1−ε), or CVP in fixedℓ_p within M^(1/min{p,2}−ε). Covers search and gap formulations. The code/lattice depends only on input length; the target carries the instance.

papers.title: Resolving the Worst-Case Complexity of Linear Secret Sharing
papers.authors: Oded Nir
papers.summary: Every n-party monotone access structure has linear secret sharing over any finite field with maximum share 2^{ceil(n/2)−1}+1 field elements. Also claims nonlinear exponent0.494, quadratic exponent0.4994 and an almost-all 2^{n/2−o(n)} monotone-span-program lower bound simultaneously over every field.

papers.title: Contextual Search and Bilateral Trade with a Trace-Square-Root Potential
papers.authors: Romain Cosson, Federico Fusco, Anupam Gupta, Stefano Leonardi, Renato Paes Leme, Matteo Russo
papers.summary: Tight horizon-independent O(sqrt(d)) expected total loss for contextual search and one-bit contextual bilateral trade with fixed unknown unit-ball vectors and adaptive unit contexts. Known-prior counterparts are bounded by trace-square-root covariance, allowing dependent seller/buyer priors with finite second moments. Search has explicit O(d^2) arithmetic and memory per round; worst-case trade uses an existential finite minimax lottery.

papers.title: Quantum Advantage for Distributed Symmetry Breaking
papers.authors: Maxime Flin, Longcheng Li, Jukka Suomela
papers.summary: Gives a one-round one-way quantum-LOCAL algorithm for directed cycles with20,000 colors and arbitrary local errorε using O(log1/ε) qubits. With known n and ε=n^{-10}, classical reductions yield four-round3-coloring and constant-round bounded-degree coloring, MIS and maximal matching with high probability, and collapse classical O(log*n)-round LCLs to quantum O(1).

papers.title: The Price of Capacities for Clustering Coresets
papers.authors: Milind Prabu, Chris Schwiegelshohn, Sudarshan Shyam
papers.summary: For k>=2, capacitated Euclidean k-median coresets have optimal size soft-Theta(k*epsilon^-2*min(sqrt(k),epsilon^-1)), and k-means soft-Theta(k*epsilon^-2*min(k,epsilon^-2)). Also closes unconstrained small-epsilon lower bounds at soft-Theta(min(k^(4/3)*epsilon^-2,k*epsilon^-3)) and soft-Theta(min(k^(3/2)*epsilon^-2,k*epsilon^-4)). Capacities are free up to logs for bounded doubling or distance pseudodimension in stated lower-bound parameter ranges. Coresets preserve fractional exact-load transportation costs for every center tuple/load vector.

papers.title: Dynamic Optimality to within O(log log log n)
papers.authors: Daniel Čech, Bernhard Haeupler, Antti Roeyskoe, Václav Rozhoň, Robert Tarjan, Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Introduces online Cha-cha BSTs with total cost O((OPT(X)+n) log log log n), using two levels of preferred paths, and proves independent-rectangle bound tight up to the same factor. Balanced auxiliary trees and splay auxiliary variants are implemented; this is not constant dynamic optimality or a bound for ordinary splay itself.

papers.title: The Space Complexity of Property Testing
papers.authors: Clément Canonne, Xi Chen, William Pires, Toniann Pitassi, Rocco A. Servedio
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Property-testing space bounds; data/sublinear primary, space-complexity method secondary.
papers.summary: Introduces a clockless randomized finite-state query model with unlimited time and long-run average acceptance. For fixed small distance, space isΘ(n) for linearity,softΘ(sqrt n) for monotonicity,Θ(k logn) for k-juntas(k≤n^{.99}), andΘ(logn) for symmetry and LTFs. Finite-halting upper-bound variants also exist.

papers.title: Optimal Pattern-Avoidance Bounds for Binary Search Trees
papers.authors: Anita Dürr, Arturo Merino, Karol Węgrzycki, Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: A pattern-agnostic online BST serves every π-avoiding access sequence of length m≥n in O(m(1+log s_π)) total cost and time, where s_π is the Stanley–Wilf limit. Includes online-insertion sorting and a constant-factor offline approximation in 2^poly(s_π)n time. Allows input-independent O(n) initialization; it does not prove dynamic optimality for arbitrary sequences or that splay/Greedy has this bound.

papers.title: Tight Analysis of Randomized Truthful Scheduling: An $(m+1)/2$ Lower Bound
papers.authors: Wenqian Wang, Chenyang Xu, Yuhao Zhang
papers.summary: Proves a claimed (m+1)/2 lower bound for truthful-in-expectation randomized unrelated-machine makespan mechanisms; applies to all universally truthful mechanisms without discrete-support restriction. More generally the bound holds for truthful fractional mechanisms measured against integral optimum, matching that fractional model exactly; TIE upper (m+5)/2 leaves additive gap2.

papers.title: Partially Dynamic Single-Source Shortest Paths in Almost-Linear Time
papers.authors: Bin Cui, Hanqing Li, Xupeng Miao, Haoze Wang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Claims deterministic(1+ε)-approximate SSSP in directed positive-integer-weight graphs under insertions or deletions with totalm^{1+o(1)}ε^{-1}logW update time and constant-time explicit distance queries. Incremental version additionally reports simple approximate paths in output-linear time; decremental version maintains distances only.

papers.title: Square-Root Regret for Adversarial Multiplayer Bandits without Collision Information or Shared Randomness
papers.authors: Chenyu Gan
papers.summary: Claims O(m^(3/2)*sqrt(KT)*log²(KmT)) regret for m labeled players, K>m arms, synchronous known horizon, oblivious reward matrices and reward-only collision-obscured feedback, without shared random seed. Fixed public table is known to the adversary; coordinator privately selects and communicates a row. Polynomial exact-arithmetic implementation uses a very large table (soft-O(T^(9/2)) cells) and soft-O(T³) play operations in stated regime.

papers.title: Correlated Forest Rounding for Unweighted Nash Social Welfare
papers.authors: Yuda Feng, Yang Hu, Shi Li, Ruilong Zhang
papers.classification_note: Welfare guarantee in a fair-allocation model; economics primary despite rounding method.
papers.summary: For unweighted Nash social welfare, gives randomized polynomial-time ratios(4(e/(e−1))³)^{1/4}+ε<1.9949+ε for submodular value oracles,2.89+ε for XOS demand/XOS oracles and35.6+ε for subadditive demand oracles. Matching-rematching framework lower bounds match the submodular ratio, not unrestricted algorithms.

papers.title: Approximating two-terminal network reliability
papers.authors: Weiming Feng, Yucheng Fu, Heng Guo
papers.summary: Gives the first FPRAS for two-terminal reliability on general directed and undirected graphs, with further near-nm and near-quadratic running-time claims respectively; complementary unreliability is shown #BIS-hard.

papers.title: Inside the Critical Window of Random 2-SAT
papers.authors: Vlady Ravelomanana
papers.summary: Claims a locally uniform explicit Airy-series limiting satisfiability profile for random2-SAT at m=n+xn^{2/3}, matching the independent-clause model, together with conditional backbone and unconditional spine laws on then^{2/3} scale and cubic-kernel/path-length geometry.

papers.title: Counting over Unbreakable Decompositions: A Single-Exponential Parameterized Algorithm for Minimum Bisection
papers.authors: Aditya Anand, Evangelos Kipouridis, Karol Węgrzycki
papers.summary: Deterministic 2^{O(k)} n^{O(1)} algorithm counts every vertex subset by size and edge-cut size j≤k, yielding minimum bisection in single-exponential parameter time. Builds a compact decomposition with adhesions ≤2k and (3k,k)-edge-unbreakable bags inside each subtree; this does not provide lean vertex-separation decompositions.

papers.title: Planted Dense Subgraph Conjectures Are Equivalent
papers.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Nobutaka Shimizu
papers.summary: For each fixed rational 0<q<p≤1, polynomial-time conjectures for planted dense subgraphs are equivalent across fixed/binomial planted size, search/decision, and inverse-polynomial through exponentially-high success. Decision advantage only a constant factor above edge counting suffices. The exponent α in k=N^(1/2−α) may change across reductions.

papers.title: Learning Positive Linear Combinations of ReLUs in Fully Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Ilias Diakonikolas, Jelena Diakonikolas, Puqian Wang, Nikos Zarifis
papers.summary: First claimed poly(d,k,1/ε)-time and sample PAC learner for positive combinations of k arbitrary ReLUs under standard Gaussian inputs, with relative L2 error and no weight-conditioning assumption. Improper hypothesis is a linear function plus ≤k positive absolute-value terms; realizable labels are the main theorem.

papers.title: As Easy as Rank One: Optimal Algorithms for Matroid Secretary and Single-Sample Matroid Prophet
papers.authors: Hamed Abdi, Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Zhiyi Huang, Danny Mittal, Sahil Singla
papers.summary: Gives fully checked 4-competitive matroid secretary and optimal 2-competitive single-sample matroid prophet algorithms. The manuscript additionally claims optimal e-competitive secretary and exact accepted-set distribution guarantees; those longer arguments remain unaudited under the explicit large-proof exception.

papers.title: Stochastic Matching with Polynomial Degree
papers.authors: Soheil Behnezhad
papers.summary: Shows a (1-epsilon)-preserving stochastic-matching sparsifier with degree O(log(1/epsilon)/(p epsilon^4)), resolving the polynomial-degree conjecture via a marginal-preserving low-total-covariance matching distribution.

papers.title: Faster Algorithms for Minimum Degree Spanning Tree
papers.authors: Sayan Bhattacharya, Ermiya Farokhnejad, Thatchaphol Saranurak, Haoze Wang
papers.summary: Deterministic MDST algorithms achieve maximum degree Δ*+1 in m n^(1/2+o(1)) time and ceil((1+ε)Δ*)+1 in soft-O(m/ε³) time on general connected graphs.

papers.title: Glauber Dynamics for Sampling Colorings: Rapid Mixing above $(1+1/\mathrm{e})\Delta$ via Hidden Hard-Core Models
papers.authors: Xiongxin Yang
papers.summary: For every fixed γ>0 and sufficiently large Δ, heat-bath Glauber dynamics for proper q-colorings of any maximum-degree-Δ graph has spectral gap Ωγ(1/n) when q≥(1+1/e+γ)Δ, and mixing Oγ(n(n log q+log 1/ε)). Uniform in growing Δ,q; no girth assumption.

papers.title: Anticoncentration of the Permanent in Ginibre Ensembles
papers.authors: Frederic Koehler, Pui Kuen Leung
papers.classification_note: Principal theorem is anticoncentration of random permanents; quantum sampling is an application.
papers.summary: Proves Gaussian permanent anticoncentration, including the Aaronson–Arkhipov conjecture: for a complex iid Gaussian n-by-n matrix, the normalized permanent has density at most n/pi, hence every epsilon-radius disk has probability at most n epsilon squared. Real and row-ordered quaternionic analogues and independent additive perturbations are also treated.

papers.title: $K_h$-Minor-Free Graphs Have Balanced Separators of Size $O(h\sqrt{n})$
papers.authors: Jonathan Conroy, Hung Le, Jack Spalding-Jamieson
papers.summary: Every n-vertex K_h-minor-free graph has a 3/4-balanced vertex separator of size at most 16h√n, resolving the 1990 Alon–Seymour–Thomas conjecture. The new ingredient is a walk of length <13k/ψ hitting k possibly overlapping sets of size at least n/k in a vertex expander. The presented separator procedure is existential/exponential, not a polynomial-time construction.

papers.title: The Complexity of Correlated Equilibria Beyond Normal-Form Games
papers.authors: Ioannis Anagnostides, Constantinos Daskalakis, Gabriele Farina, Noah Golowich, Tuomas Sandholm, Brian Hu Zhang
papers.summary: For any prescribed polynomial support bound, inverse-polynomial approximate fixed sets are PPAD-hard; this gives unconditional CE hardness for two-player concave games quadratic in each player’s own strategy. Explicit multilinear polytope games are hard at exponential precision, and inverse-polynomial precision there is conditional on PCP-for-PPAD. Also gives swap-regret lower bounds and tractable restricted-deviation equilibria.

papers.title: Marton's conjecture in polynomial time
papers.authors: Srinivasan Arunachalam, Arkopal Dutt, Sabee Grewal, Aparna Gupte
papers.summary: Given uniform sampling and membership access to A in F_2^n with doubling at most K, outputs a basis for a subspace V of size at most |A| whose polynomially many translates cover A, in poly(n,K,log(1/delta)) resources. Applications include quadratic Goldreich–Levin and stabilizer-learning tasks.

papers.title: A Little Derandomization Goes a Long Way: Unconditional Circuit Lower Bounds using Low-Degree PIT
papers.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Karthik Gajulapalli, Alexander Golovnev, Ivan Mihajlin
papers.summary: Unconditionally, either NE has languages outside SIZE[2^n/(2n)] or constant-free VP_Z^0 differs from VNP_Z^0. Refines PIT-to-lower-bound tradeoffs; gives O_d(s t^(d−1)) fixed-finite-field constant-degree PIT and faster integer syntactically set-multilinear tests with an explicit intermediate coefficient-bound promise.

papers.title: Polynomial Interpolation for Sherali-Adams Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Nathan Acheampong, Ben Davis, Robert Robere
papers.summary: Polynomial interpolation yields an exponential Res(2)-versus-Sherali-Adams separation and proves that size-automating Sherali-Adams is NP-hard.

papers.title: Solving Linear Systems in $\tilde{O}(m n \log \frac{\kappa}{\epsilon})$ Bit Operations
papers.authors: Jonathan Kelner
papers.summary: Deterministically solves a nonsingular sparse linear system to relative residual epsilon in near O(mn log(kappa/epsilon)) bit operations for logarithmically encoded inputs. General floating-point input cost is accounted for separately, and the output uses short integer significands with one encoded exponent; no condition-number bound is required.

papers.title: An Exponential Succinctness Gap between Three-Variable Logic and the Calculus of Relations
papers.authors: Yuya Uezato, Yoshiki Nakamura
papers.summary: An O(k)-size positive FO3 binary query requires at least 2^(k-1) relation-composition gates in any equivalent calculus-of-relations circuit, even with sharing, arbitrary Boolean operations/converse and agreement only on finite structures. No named vertices/order or vertex-dependent constants are free. Additional claims give tight 2^Theta(m/log m) fixed-single-relation circuit succinctness, FO2/tree and Boolean/tropical matrix-query bounds.

papers.title: The Hyperclique Hypothesis is False
papers.authors: Nick Fischer
papers.summary: An explicit signed recursive algorithm counts k-cliques in h-uniform hypergraphs in n^((1-epsilon_h)k) time for fixed k>h, refuting the stated Hyperclique Hypothesis. The elementary 3-uniform 4-clique bound is n^3.99999.

papers.title: Polynomial Lower Bounds for Steiner Shortcuts via Test Functions
papers.authors: Aaron Bernstein, Henry Fleischmann, Bernhard Haeupler, Gary Hoppenworth, Thatchaphol Saranurak
papers.summary: Constructs directed graphs for which even Steiner shortcut augmentations with m^(1+epsilon) edges require diameter n^(1/56-O(epsilon)); extends to exact undirected Steiner hopsets and monotone circuit depth reduction.

papers.title: Top-Down Lower Bounds for All Depths
papers.authors: Oliver Korten
papers.summary: Gives completely top-down communication-adversary proofs that depth-d De Morgan circuits for parity need exp(ε_d n^(1/(d−1))) wires for every fixed d≥2. Central new light-pattern estimate uses harmonic-mean coefficients of random projections of high-min-entropy distributions.

papers.title: QPTAS for Max Weight Independent Set in Graphs with Strongly Edge-Sublinear Separators
papers.authors: Édouard Bonnet, Yeonsu Chang
papers.summary: Every hereditary class whose m-edge graphs have balanced separators O(m^b), for fixed b<1, admits a deterministic QPTAS for rational-weight maximum independent set. No geometric representation or separator oracle is supplied. This includes graphs excluding any fixed induced minor, using the cited separator theorem.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Strong Roberson Conjecture
papers.authors: Arnar Kristjánsson
papers.summary: Refutes the Strong Roberson Conjecture and its weak-immersion analogue: explicit connected graphs H have hom(H,·) determined by counts from graphs excluding H as a minor or immersion. A concrete minor witness is the 91-vertex circulant with jumps 1 and 5; its 182-vertex cubic bipartite split handles immersion. Failure occurs even for a minor-closed source class of pathwidth at most ten.

papers.title: Mortality Is Undecidable for 2 × 2 Integer Matrices
papers.authors: Thanin Quartz, Ivan O. Shevchenko, Hans De Sterck, Jun Liu
papers.summary: Claims undecidability of mortality for 2×2 integer matrices, even for exactly 5,799 distinct matrices with 5,798 fixed nonsingular generators of determinant ±p and one variable rank-one matrix with fixed image. The construction encodes a universal arithmetic program in rational projective points; a p-adic error set is intended to prevent invalid products from returning to valid configurations.

papers.title: NP-hardness for Bipartite Colorings up to the Maximum Degree
papers.authors: Andreas Galanis, Heng Guo, Yuchen He, Daniel Stefankovic, Eric Vigoda
papers.summary: For every fixed odd q>=5 and Delta>q, and for q=3 with Delta>=5, approximating the number of proper q-colorings of bipartite maximum-degree-Delta graphs within exp(cn) is NP-hard. Without a degree restriction, every fixed q>=3 has no FPRAS unless NP=RP. Even-q bounded-degree and (q,Delta)=(3,4) are deferred to a future full version.

papers.title: The Stretch Factor of Planar Delaunay Triangulations Is Nearly Determined
papers.authors: Guanlin Mo, Kangke Cheng, Hu Ding
papers.summary: Claims every planar Delaunay triangulation has stretch at most 1.5949, versus the known lower bound 1.5932. Reduces arbitrary disk chains to local potential inequalities, then a four-parameter differential/interval verification. The chain reduction can introduce slack, so this does not identify the exact optimum.

papers.title: Semi-Streaming Matching in a Single Pass II: Greedy is Optimal
papers.authors: Sepehr Assadi, Max Jiang, Mars Xiang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Proves that a single adversarial-order pass with O(n polylog n) space cannot approximate maximum matching by any fixed factor greater than 1/2 with constant success probability, even for bipartite graphs with a perfect matching. Also states the optimal 1/2 competitive ratio for preemptive online matching. The theorem does not cover random-order or multipass streams.

papers.title: Randomized Greedy MIS is Fast at Every Node
