papers.authors: Mina Dalirrooyfard, Konstantin Makarychev, Slobodan Mitrović, Srikkanth Ramachandran
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: For every vertex fixed before random ranks are sampled, memoized rank-ordered pruned greedy MIS makes at most CΔ^90(1+h) fresh calls except with probability e^(−h). Expected fresh calls are O(Δ^90); total calls incur an additional Δ factor. This is not a simultaneous all-vertices bound or an arbitrary neighbor-scan order guarantee.

papers.title: Square-root queries can help
papers.authors: Eric Ma, Ewin Tang
papers.summary: Shows that efficient square roots for every efficiently implementable unitary would imply BQP=PSPACE, and gives an Omega(N) versus O(log N) black-box separation between ordinary and arbitrary square-root queries.

papers.title: Bellman-Ford in Almost-Linear Time
papers.authors: Isaac M Hair, George Z. Li, Jason Li, Junkai Zhang
papers.summary: Gives a Las Vegas randomized m^(1+o(1))-time algorithm for single-source shortest paths in directed graphs with arbitrary real edge weights, with high-probability running time. Improves betweenness reduction and adds a shortcut-unfolding invariant to prevent recursive graph densification. The result is in the real-weight arithmetic model, not a bit-complexity bound independent of weight representation.

papers.title: Gibbs Sampling in the Shattered Phase by Decoded Quantum Interferometry
papers.authors: Leo Zhou, Noah Shutty, Mark Sellke, Stephen Jordan
papers.summary: For random signed k-uniform XORSAT with fixed large k and average degree D≥k, proves shattering and failure of stable samplers for (1+ε)√(2 log k/D)≤β≤√(k/(2D)), yet gives polynomial-time DQI+USD and classical Prange samplers whenever D tanh β<K*(k), with K*(k)/k→1. At D=3k, β=1/4 both samplers achieve vanishing expected total-variation error while Glauber mixing is exponential. This is not a quantum advantage over all classical algorithms.

papers.title: Multivariate Resultants: Complexity and Applications to Real Feasibility
papers.authors: Gorav Jindal, Bhargav C S, Himanshu Shukla, Radu Curticapean
papers.summary: Proves existential real feasibility belongs to the counting hierarchy, using compact coefficient access to resultants, finite critical-point witnesses and short partial Thom encodings. Separately proves polynomial-size quadratic resultant circuits imply VP=VNP, modular evaluation is #P-hard, addressed absolute-value bits are PP-hard, and signs are parity-P-hard even for nonzero sparse symmetric cubic tensor determinants.

papers.title: New Lower and Upper Bounds for the Grothendieck Constant
papers.authors: Rahul Saha, Alan Li, Anton Xue, Swarat Chaudhuri, Adam Klivans, Pravesh K. Kothari, Raghu Meka
papers.classification_note: Bounds on the Grothendieck constant; aligned with #820. Approximation applications are secondary.
papers.summary: Claims new bounds 6π/11≤KG≤π/(2 log(1+√2))−3.47×10⁻⁴ for the real Grothendieck constant. The lower bound follows from a universal affine constraint on Krivine correlation coefficients plus asymptotic optimality of mixed Krivine schemes; the upper bound uses a high-dimensional cubic–quintic limiting scheme and rigorous numerical certification.

papers.title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten–Stigum
papers.authors: Ferenc Bencs, Brice Huang, Daniel Lee, Kuikui Liu, Guus Regts
papers.summary: For fixed d>=3 and fixed delta>0, deterministically estimates the zero-field antiferromagnetic Ising partition function on a uniformly random d-regular graph in (n/epsilon)^C(d,delta) time, with high probability over the graph, for beta<=(1-delta) beta_KS(d), beta_KS=2 arctanh(1/sqrt(d-1)). Proves high-probability zero-freeness in a constant-width complex strip. Does not supply a sampling algorithm or efficiently testable success certificate.

papers.title: Optimal Sub-Gaussian Mean Estimation in Low Dimensions
papers.authors: Jasper C.H. Lee, Suraj Mathashery, Paul Valiant, Kun Wang
papers.summary: Claims a polynomial-time scale/shift/rotation-equivariant estimator for arbitrary finite unknown covariance achieving (1+o(1))*sqrt(2||Sigma||op log(1/delta)/n) Euclidean error in constant or slowly growing dimension, with o(1) uniform over the distribution when log(1/delta)/n and d^2 loglog(1/delta)/log(1/delta) tend to zero. Uses an SDP trimming rule and a computer-assisted quantified inequality.

papers.title: Bipartite Matching is in NC
papers.authors: Abhranil Chatterjee, Sumanta Ghosh, Rohit Gurjar, Roshan Raj, Thomas Thierauf
papers.summary: Claims deterministic NC algorithms for bipartite matching, weighted linear matroid intersection and noncommutative rank. The weighted matching theorem explicitly assumes polynomially bounded edge weights; search is obtained through weighted-decision reductions. The construction replaces graph entries by folded Vandermonde blocks and encodes weight through polynomial degrees.

papers.title: Adaptive Data Analysis and Adversarial Robustness on Insertion-Deletion Streams
papers.authors: Elena Gribelyuk, Honghao Lin, Xin Lyu, Mahbod Majid, David P. Woodruff, Huacheng Yu, Samson Zhou
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Answers k adaptive [0,1]-valued statistical queries over arbitrary finite domains using soft-O(sqrt(k)/alpha+1/alpha^2) samples; combines this with a fixed linear F2 sketch and stateful decoder and a recursive streaming construction to obtain epsilon^-2 polylog(n) bits for adversarial turnstile F2 throughout polynomial-length streams with polynomially bounded integer frequencies.

papers.title: Asymptotically Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes
papers.authors: William Gay, Fernando Jeronimo
papers.summary: Constructs polynomial-time explicit binary CSS quantum LDPC families with constant rate, constant relative distance, bounded check/qubit degrees and constant all-state local-test soundness H >= (sigma/N)D_Q. Instantiates a cubical cosheaf framework using arithmetic tree-product quotients, Frobenius-twisted equivariant Reed-Solomon codes and uniform product expansion on distinct norm-one grids.

papers.title: Existence of the Core in Approval-Based Committee Elections
papers.authors: Patrick Becker, Matthias Greger, Dominik Peters
papers.summary: Proves that every approval-based committee election has a core-stable committee, in fact one robust to the paper’s fractional core+ deviations, and gives a polynomial-time algorithm for finding one at the Hare quota. Uses a harmonic-entropy payment objective and approximate single-candidate local optimality. Computing its global optimum is a distinct, harder problem.

papers.title: Quasipolynomial 3-Coloring of Diameter-2 Graphs via Domain Reduction from Nogoods
papers.authors: Philip Whittington
papers.summary: Deterministically solves decision, search and exact counting for 3-Coloring and fixed-palette List-3-Coloring on diameter-at-most-two graphs in 2^(O(log³n)) time. Does not give a polynomial algorithm; NP-hardness would imply NP⊆QP.

papers.title: Pretty good shadow tomography
papers.authors: Sabee Grewal, Angelos Pelecanos, Jack Spilecki, Ewin Tang, John Wright
papers.summary: For any known collection of m>=2 bounded observables and arbitrary unknown d-dimensional mixed state, collective measurements achieve simultaneous epsilon-accurate estimates with failure delta using O(log(m) log(m/delta)/epsilon^2) copies, independent of d. This is an information-theoretic offline result; it does not give efficient implementation or an observable-independent classical shadow.

papers.title: Beyond the Bochner Method: Optimal Spectral Gaps for Block Dynamics of Spin Systems like the O(N) Model
papers.authors: Jonathan Leake, Anqi Li
papers.summary: Sharp matrix-valued local-to-global spectral bounds for block Glauber dynamics after arbitrary marginalization; applications give O(N) gap (1-||J_abs||/N)/n with arbitrary fields and weighted forest pair correlation at most 4/3 times the product.

papers.title: A Tight $ \widetilde\Omega (\sqrt m) $ Information-theoretic Lower Bound for Randomized Online Set Cover
papers.authors: Ilan Doron-Arad, Joseph (Seffi) Naor
papers.summary: Unweighted known-instance online set cover has randomized oblivious-adversary competitive ratio Omega(sqrt(m)), with unrestricted computation; additional random-order Omega(m^(1/3)) and polynomial-memory Omega(m/log m) bounds.

papers.title: Algorithmic List Decoding at Capacity and Optimal Proximity Gaps for Reed--Solomon Codes
papers.authors: Fernando Granha Jeronimo
papers.summary: For every fixed slack gamma>0 and bounded input-list size, every evaluation set of an ordinary Reed–Solomon code over a prime field q>=n has deterministic capacity-slack list recovery in q^{O_gamma(1)} field operations and n^{O_gamma(1)} output list size independent of q. Also claims polynomial-exception-budget mutual correlated agreement along fixed-degree received-word curves at the same radius.

papers.title: An FPRAS for Counting Common Bases of Two Matroids
papers.authors: Xiaoyu Chen, Kuikui Liu
papers.summary: Gives an FPRAS for counting common bases of two arbitrary independence-oracle matroids. More generally, develops a soft-intersection and convex-programming framework for counting coefficients of products of log-concave measures.

papers.title: Large Growth Happens: Gaussian Elimination with Partial Pivoting on Random Matrices
papers.authors: Daniel Spielman, Xifan Yu
papers.summary: For iid Gaussian n-by-n matrices, exact-arithmetic partial-pivoting elimination has growth >=rho with probability at least exp(-710 log^2(rho/sqrt(n)) log n), over the explicit range from 100 sqrt(n) log n up to exponential growth.

papers.title: Polytope Sampling at the Speed of Isoperimetry
papers.authors: Anming Gu, Bobby Shi, Kevin Tian, Hubert Yang
papers.summary: Samples the uniform law on an m-facet n-dimensional polytope to TV error delta in O(m^2 n^(omega-1) log^3(m/delta)) time plus an explicit analytic-center term; no warm start is assumed, but a feasible point and inner/outer radius bounds are supplied.

papers.title: Algorithmic Principles For Multiclass Learning Are Hard To Come By: Limits of Regularization and Proper Learning
papers.authors: Julian Asilis, Shaddin Dughmi, Vatsal Sharan, Alec Sun, Shanghua Teng, Chang Wang
papers.summary: Constructs a realizable multiclass PAC-learnable class contained in no properly learnable envelope; additional separations show proper learning can require sublinear training error and regularization templates do not capture all learnable classes.

papers.title: Quadratic Extractors
papers.authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Jesse Goodman, David Zuckerman
papers.summary: Explicit extractors for quadratic sources over F₂ with polylogarithmic min-entropy, using a derivative-entropy structure theorem, quadratic correlation breaking and explicit rank combiners.

papers.title: Near-Cubic Gate and Near-Quartic Wire Lower Bounds for SYM ◦THR Circuits
papers.authors: Dev Nag
papers.summary: Claims an ENP language with constant average-case hardness against SYM∘THR circuits of nearly n⁴ wires and nearly n³ gates, for every sufficiently large n. Top integer weights are charged by absolute multiplicity; this is not arbitrary-real-weight THR∘THR hardness.

papers.title: Finding Hypercliques Faster Than Brute Force
papers.authors: Josh Alman, Baitian Li, Neha Pant, Kevin Pratt, Ryan Williams
papers.summary: For every fixed k≥3, uniformly constructs Z[1/2] arithmetic circuits of size O(n^{k−εk}) for the k-hyperclique polynomial, with εk=2^{-Θ(2^k)}. Gives exact counting, faster Max-Degree-kCSP and subquadratic fixed-length AP detection.

papers.title: Kadison--Singer in Deterministic Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Ekene Ezeunala, Haotian Jiang
papers.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial-time signing of rational Hermitian rank-at-most-one matrices with norm at most 13||sum H_i^2||^(1/2), implying Weaver KS2 with constant 13/2.

papers.title: Quadratic Statistical Randomized Encoding for All Functions
papers.authors: Benny Applebaum
papers.summary: Claims statistical randomized encodings of degree 2 and locality 3 for every finite function, with efficient encodings for NC¹ and specified log-space classes, resolving the degree-two universality question with negligible error.

papers.title: An Explicit 4n−O(log(n)) Size Lower Bound against General Boolean Circuits
papers.authors: Om Swostik Mishra, Rahul Santhanam
papers.summary: An explicit polynomial-time Boolean function requires general fan-in-two Boolean circuits of size at least 4n−O(log n). More generally a dimension-d affine disperser has circuit complexity at least 4n−10d, with a deterministic poly(n,2^d) refuter.

papers.title: The Optimal Sample Complexity of Multiclass and List Learning
papers.authors: Chirag Pabbaraju
papers.summary: Proves maximal shifted ℓ-density of every one-inclusion hypergraph is at most its ℓ-DS dimension. Consequently obtains realizable ℓ-list PAC sample complexity O((d_DS^ℓ+log(1/δ))/ε), including arbitrary label sets. Matching list lower bounds require the stated label-richness condition; multiclass is ℓ=1. Also gives agnostic, compression and universal-learning consequences with separate qualifications.

papers.title: TFNP in the Random Oracle Model
papers.authors: Noah Fleming, Mika Göös, Ziyi Guan, Oliver Korten, Daniel Mitropolsky, Toniann Pitassi, Artur Riazanov, Dmitry Sokolov, Tianqi Yang, Weiqiang Yuan
papers.summary: Average-case PPAD hardness in the random-oracle model, contrasted with polynomial-query UEoPL solvability by computationally unbounded solvers, plus separations from PLS under public-coin reductions.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Junta Testing
papers.authors: Jinge Bao, Minbo Gao, Penghui Yao
papers.summary: Determines junta-testing query complexity in four models: Boolean functions Θ(sqrt(k/ε)); unitaries with forward and inverse queries Θ(sqrt(k)/ε); forward-only unitaries and channels Θ(k/(ε² log k)). The common stated window is sufficiently large k, n≥2k and 2^{−k/16}≤ε≤1/16. Distances are uniform Boolean distance, phase-invariant normalized Hilbert–Schmidt unitary distance and normalized Choi Hilbert–Schmidt channel distance, not diamond distance. Forward upper testers use product inputs and single-qubit measurements without ancillas.

papers.title: Optimal LCA and Sublinear Estimation for Bipartite Matching in $\Delta^{O(1/\varepsilon)}$ Queries
papers.authors: Edith Cohen, Mohammad Roghani
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Bipartite matching LCA gives a globally consistent always-feasible matching with (1−ε) value with probability .9 using (2Δ)^{O(1/ε)} worst-case queries per mate query; additive εn size estimation has the same exponent. General graphs receive half-integral fractional matching, not integral near-optimal matching.

papers.title: A Complete Characterization of Central String Queries in Compact Space
papers.authors: Dominik Kempa, Tomasz Kociumaka
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Gives constant-factor-preserving equivalences between central compact string queries and simpler prefix operations, preserving alphabet and all four space/time measures. Constructs the PLCP bitvector deterministically in O(n min{1,log σ/√log n}) time, with O(n log σ) working bits and O(n)-bit/O(1)-query final indexing.

papers.title: Counterexamples to EFX for Submodular and Subadditive Valuations
papers.authors: Hannaneh Akrami, Simon Mackenzie, Alexander Mayorov, Kurt Mehlhorn, Shreyas Srinivas, Mashbat Suzuki, Christoph Weidenbach
papers.summary: Constructs three-agent eight-good monotone valuations with no complete EFX allocation and transfers the counterexample, with the same agents/goods, to weighted coverage. Extends to n>=3,m>=n+5. Separately claims existence for three agents <=7 goods, subadditive approximation obstruction alpha>2^{-1/6}, and a weighted-coverage obstruction near .957455; these further results were not audited. EFX quantifies every removed good, including zero marginal ones; the result does not settle additive valuations.

papers.title: Low-Temperature Sampling via Equilibrium Disagreements
papers.authors: Andreas Galanis, Daniel Stefankovic
papers.summary: Develops equilibrium-disagreement canonical paths yielding phase Glauber convergence in n^{3/2+o(1)} steps on random regular graphs throughout fixed-parameter low-temperature regimes for hard-core, Ising, and real-q>2 random-cluster models. An n^{2+o(1)} sampler combines phases without high-accuracy partition-function estimation.

papers.title: On the Composition Theorem for Approximate Degree, Randomized and Exact Quantum Query Complexity
papers.authors: Samruddhi Pednekar, Supartha Podder
papers.classification_note: Composition results span classical and quantum query models; approximate-degree/randomized bounds primary.
papers.summary: Claims constant-factor multiplicative composition for approximate degree of all total Boolean functions, a randomized-query composition lower bound R(f)R(g)/log(n+1) for partial functions, and a polynomial failure of multiplicative composition for exact quantum queries.

papers.title: A Quasipolynomial Algorithm for $\ell_\infty$ Contractions
papers.authors: Ashkan Soleymani, Gabriele Farina
papers.summary: Gives a deterministic log(1/(γε))^{O(log² d)} exact-arithmetic/oracle algorithm for an ε-near fixed point of any d-dimensional (1−γ) ℓ∞ contraction, and corresponding approximate fixed points of nonexpansions.

papers.title: Hardness of Approximation for Semialgebraic CSPs: Every Geometric Semialgebraic CSP is Approximation Resistant
papers.authors: Dionysis Arvanitakis, Vaggos Chatziafratis, Konstantin Makarychev
papers.summary: Assuming UGC, any satisfiable fixed-dimensional semialgebraic predicate invariant under common translation and positive scaling, with open accepting set and best iid biased acceptance alpha*<1, is approximation resistant: near-satisfiable versus at most alpha*+epsilon. Includes strict ordinal-distance/orientation constraints; excludes equality predicates and origin-dependent MAX-CUT.

papers.title: Efficient classical simulation of Fermi-Hubbard models with Kramers symmetry
papers.authors: Chaithanya Rayudu, Jun Takahashi, Ojas Parekh, Andrew Zhao
papers.summary: Gives a classical randomized relative approximation to Tr exp(−βH) in poly(N,r,β,Λ,1/ε) time for the attractive Kramers Hamiltonian class H=a†ha−ΣU_i n(v_i)n(Θv_i), with Θ²=−I, ΘhΘ⁻¹=h and U_i≥0.

papers.title: Nearly Optimal Submodular Sparsification, with and without Cardinality Constraints
papers.authors: Zhengting Bao, Dongrun Cai, Xue Chen, Yuchen He, Chihao Zhang
papers.summary: For sums of arbitrary nonnegative submodular functions, constructs component reweightings of size O(n² log n/epsilon²) preserving every subset query, without monotonicity or symmetry. Also claims O(nk log n/epsilon²) for |S|<=k, with matching Omega(nk) scale. Weights computed by nested submodular minimization then independent component sampling.

papers.title: $(1+\epsilon)$-Distortion Spanning Tree Covers of Minor-Free Graphs with Size $O(\log \log n)$
papers.authors: Willem Fletcher, Arnold Filtser, Ellis Hershkowitz, Lazar Milenković
papers.summary: Constructs (1+ε)-distortion spanning-subgraph tree covers of size f(ε,r) log log n for K_r-minor-free graphs, with new strong sparse partitions and separated strong neighborhood covers; derives compact routing and path-reporting oracles.

papers.title: Counting and Sampling by Local Repair: From the Lovász Local Lemma to Random k-SAT
papers.authors: Dimitris Achlioptas
papers.summary: Claims perfect sampling at the pD² local-lemma scale and a stronger Sampling Local Lemma using connected simultaneous-event probabilities. Applications include independent-transversal FPRAS/perfect sampling at block size at least 9Δ and random k-SAT counting/almost-uniform sampling up to density c·2^k/k².

papers.title: Truthful-in-Expectation Mechanism with Constant Maximin-Share Guarantee
papers.authors: Mengfan Ma, Biaoshuai TAO, Fangxiao WANG
papers.summary: For nonnegative additive goods, gives a truthful-in-expectation and ex-ante envy-free mechanism with at least1/6 TPS, hence1/6 MMS, for every agent in every realized allocation. Rational-input implementation is polynomial time with an explicit lottery over at most m(n−1)+1 complete allocations.

papers.title: Depth-$1$ expanders on the unitary group and applications
papers.authors: Anurag Anshu, Shankar Balasubramanian, Jonas Haferkamp, Aram Harrow, Xinyu Tan
papers.summary: Constructs constant-degree, constant-gap quantum expanders with depth-one Clifford/CNOT/Pauli circuits, and a dimension-uniform unitary-group expander using such generators plus one T gate and its inverse. Applications include a frustration-free 1D entanglement–gap construction with S=Θ(Δ^(−1/2)) and streaming tests of volume-law states.

papers.title: Combinatorial Boolean matrix Multiplation in n^3/2^{\Omega(\sqrt{\log n})} Time
papers.authors: Piaoyang Cui, Yiming Liu, David P. Woodruff
papers.summary: Claims deterministic combinatorial BMM and triangle detection in n³/2^{Ω(√log n)} time via a 2^{O(d²)}-piece grid-regularity decomposition with a bounded fractional density-weighted volume.

papers.title: Iterative Rounding for Determinant Maximization and Real Stable Polynomials
papers.authors: Nikhil Bansal, Wenzheng Li, Mohit Singh, Yuze Xu
papers.summary: Deterministic polynomial-time e^(14d+ε)-approximation producing a matroid base for determinant maximization in dimension d and rank r≥d. Extends to degree-d homogeneous multiaffine real stable polynomials with a value oracle; coefficient-oracle access additionally requires a support-matroid oracle and yields a randomized guarantee.

papers.title: Algorithmic Wave-Particle Duality: Pathfinding in Welded Trees is Hard
papers.authors: Joseph Carolan, Andrew Childs, Matthew Coudron, Amin Shiraz Gilani, David Miloschewsky, Supartha Podder
papers.summary: For a distribution over single-cycle welded trees of height n, any unrestricted quantum adjacency/colored-neighbor query algorithm finding any entrance–exit path has success O(q/2^(n/3)+nq³/2^n); consequently soft-Theta(2^(n/3)) queries are needed and sufficient. Exit finding alone remains polynomial-query.

papers.title: Four Ways to Stream: Exponential Separations from Random Order and Quantum Memory
papers.authors: Nadezhda Voronova
papers.summary: Separates random-order quantum streaming exponentially from both random-order classical and data-first quantum streaming, via repeated Hidden Matching. Establishes linear multiple-request quantum communication bounds and quantum random-order Noisy Gap Cycle lower bounds.

papers.title: A Quantum Lower Bound for Triangle Finding
papers.authors: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Xingyu Zhou
papers.summary: Claims the first superlinear quantum adjacency-matrix query lower bound for triangle finding, Omega(N^(13/12)), with detection consequences for fixed connected nonbipartite graphs.

papers.title: Optimal Robust Community Detection
papers.authors: Samuel B. Hopkins, Yiding Hua, Sidhanth Mohanty, Amit Rajaraman, David Steurer
papers.summary: For fixed sparse two-community SBM parameters and ε>0, a nearly-linear-time estimator attains uncorrupted information-theoretic optimal correlation minus ε while tolerating ηn arbitrary edge changes, for a sufficiently small parameter-dependent η>0. Also proves spectral nonbacktracking initialization of belief propagation is asymptotically optimal.

papers.title: Non-Interactive Cryptography over Noisy Channels from Indistinguishability Obfuscation
papers.authors: Yuval Ishai, George Lu, Liav Zafar
papers.summary: Assuming iO and OWFs, arbitrary finite-alphabet computational wiretap coding is possible exactly when receiver channel is not a stochastic degradation of eavesdropper channel, with negligible error. Every nontrivial finite channel supports one-way randomized sender-input computation with prescribed inverse-polynomial simulation error, not negligible error. Multi-receiver independently noisy product channels are characterized by noise preservation; receiver outputs use independent private coins.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Quantum Lower Bounds for Convex Optimization via Fourier Rank
papers.authors: Brandon Augustino, Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Enrico Fontana, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul, Nadezhda Voronova
papers.summary: Claims linear quantum membership-query lower bounds for high-accuracy convex optimization over ellipsoids, an n/2 continuous matrix phase-query determinant lower bound, and optimal-up-to-log strongly convex gradient-query bounds.

papers.title: Sparse Hamiltonian simulation with optimal dependence on the maximum column Euclidean norm
papers.authors: Zecheng Li, Chunhao Wang
papers.summary: For d-sparse Hermitian H with known column-Euclidean bound Λ and entry bound Λmax≤Λ, simulates exp(−itH) to clean-isometry operator error ε using O(tΛ sqrt(d)+sqrt(tdΛmax log(2/ε))+log(2/ε)) sparse queries. Leading scale is optimal when d>1 and tΛ≥log(2/ε), with dimension allowed to grow; joint optimality outside that regime is not claimed. Applications include constant-error Theta(sqrt(N)) black-box unitary implementation.

papers.title: Deterministic Parameterized Inapproximability of the Shortest Vector and Minimum Distance Problems
papers.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Bingkai Lin, Yuwei Liu, Kazuki Ogitsuka
papers.summary: Deterministic FPT reductions establish W[1]-hardness of gamma-approximate SVP in every computable finite lp norm for gamma<2^(1/p), and of constant-factor MDP over every finite field.

papers.title: Subquadratic Time Matrix Multiplication Data Structures Beyond the Dual Exponent, with Applications
papers.authors: Josh Alman, Jakob Nogler, Virginia Vassilevska Williams
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Matrix-product data structure/query tradeoff is primary; arithmetic algorithms secondary.
papers.summary: Preprocess two N×N matrices in N^(2−γ) field operations to answer selected-entry product queries in D^(1−ε) time for D up to N^0.501215..., with a √N-query example using preprocessing N^1.999733... and query N^0.499733.... This is a data-structure tradeoff, not an improvement to the square matrix-multiplication exponent.

papers.title: Shortest Disjoint Paths in Planar Graphs
papers.authors: Srijan Chakraborty, Anish Mukherjee
papers.summary: Randomized n^O(k) algorithm for minimum-total-length k vertex-disjoint paths at arbitrary terminal positions in undirected planar graphs; more precise 4^k n^O(f) for terminals assigned to f faces. Extends to bounded genus and fixed-pattern minimum-weight minors/subdivisions. Costs are nonnegative polynomially bounded integers; arbitrary binary weights incur poly(W), not a strongly polynomial guarantee.

papers.title: Tight Bounds on the Menu-Size Complexity of Approximately Optimal Auctions with Two Items
papers.authors: Hau Chan, Mingyu Guo, Nguyen Thach
papers.summary: Claims a tight Theta(epsilon^(-2)) worst-distribution menu size for additive-epsilon optimal revenue with one additive buyer and two bounded-value items, plus an n-item upper bound.

papers.title: Binary Huffman Coding with Unequal Letter Costs Is NP-Complete
papers.authors: L. Sunil Chandran, Rishikesh Gajjala
papers.summary: Binary unequal-letter-cost prefix coding is NP-complete even for consecutive costs (M,M+1) when M, frequencies and threshold are binary-encoded inputs. Also claims hardness of minimizing weighted ones among all ordinary minimum-length codes. Does not prove strong NP-hardness or settle an FPTAS.

papers.title: Inapproximability of Euclidean Steiner Tree
papers.authors: Simon Bartlmae
papers.summary: Claims APX-hardness of continuous Euclidean Steiner tree in O(log n) dimensions, no PTAS in O(log log n) dimensions under NP not contained in SUBEXP, and nearly tight fixed-dimension accuracy dependence under a stated weaker-than-ETH running-time assumption.

papers.title: Adaptive Matrix Sparsification with Applications to Empirical Risk Minimization and Computational Geometry
papers.authors: Yang Liu, Richard Peng, Colin Tang, Albert Weng, Junzhao Yang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Adaptive insertion/deletion leverage-score data structure is the core theorem; optimization applications secondary.
papers.summary: Adaptive row-insertion/deletion leverage-score maintenance in total soft-O(nd+Q d^6), with spectrally bounded Gram matrices and O(n) total rows, yields high-accuracy constant-block ERM in soft-O(nd+d^6 sqrt(n)); also minimum-enclosing-ball and ellipsoid applications. Near-linear input time requires n sufficiently larger than the polynomial d term.

papers.title: The Honeycomb Framework for Code Bounds
papers.authors: William Gay, Fernando Granha Jeronimo, Lenny Liu
papers.summary: Unifies moving-projection and classical–quantum channel code bounds using a honeycomb of compatible representations, strengthens specified bounds, and introduces finite and asymptotic hierarchies.

papers.title: Round-Optimal Statistical Verifiable Secret Sharing with Polynomial Complexity
papers.authors: Chen-Da Liu-Zhang, Elisaweta Masserova
papers.summary: Claims polynomial-communication, polynomial-computation statistical VSS with three sharing rounds and one reconstruction round for t<n/2, against static rushing corruption.

papers.title: A Constant-Rate Compiler for Continual Memory Leakage
papers.authors: Rajeev Raghunath, Shweta Agrawal, Anuja Modi
papers.summary: A universal compiler for deterministic secret-key computations tolerates a constant leakage fraction relative to each compiled persistent share across adaptive invocations, using two separately leaking components and inputless leakage-free correlation samplers. Packed extension-field configurations keep live register count and physical-encoding lifetime constant. Sampler removal needs additional iO/LWE setup assumptions.

papers.title: Almost Tight Hardness of Approximation for 0-Extension
papers.authors: Qingyun Chen, Weihao Zhu
papers.summary: Constructs Ω(log^(1−ε)k) earthmover-LP integrality gaps for 0-Extension for every fixed ε>0 and arbitrarily large k. Via MNRS08 this yields matching-scale hardness conditional on UGC; manuscript states NP-hardness using a separately claimed recent UGC proof.

papers.title: Minimum-Cost $k$-Arborescence Packing in $\tilde O(km+k^4 n)$ Time
papers.authors: Zhaienhe Zhou
papers.summary: Deterministic strongly polynomial minimum-cost packing of k arc-disjoint rooted arborescences in soft-O(km+k^4 n) for arbitrary real costs, hence near-linear for fixed k. Extension gives minimum-cost maximum-cardinality k-forest packing in soft-O(k m^(1+o(1))+k^5 n), using bounded-integer min-cost flow as a subroutine.

papers.title: Faster Isomorphism for Groups of Class 2
papers.authors: Xiaorui Sun
papers.summary: Tests Cayley-table isomorphism of arbitrary class-2 groups of order N in N^O((log N)^(25/26)loglog N), including 2-groups of unrestricted exponent.

papers.title: 3SUM Made Simpler (Without Matrix Multiplication), $k$-SUM Hypothesis Refuted for Odd $k$, and Real 3SUM/APSP Derandomized
papers.authors: Timothy M. Chan, Reina Itakura, Zhiyuan Ma, Yuancheng Yu
papers.summary: Gives a matrix-multiplication-free randomized truly subquadratic integer 3SUM algorithm, refutes the integer k-SUM hypothesis for every odd constant k, and derandomizes real 3SUM/APSP reductions to selected-entry matrix multiplication.

papers.title: The log log jam in Gaussian state tomography
papers.authors: Sitan Chen, Weiyuan Gong, Qi Ye, Zhihan Zhang
papers.summary: Adaptive entangled Gaussian measurements require Ω(loglog E+1/ε²) copies to learn pure Gaussian states. Provides bounded-adaptivity energy tradeoffs and non-Gaussian entangled tomography of n-mode pure states using O((n²+log(1/δ))/ε²) copies independent of energy.

papers.title: SVP Is NP-Hard for Some Rank-2 Cyclotomic Modules
papers.authors: Jiaqi Liu, Yansong Feng, Yanbin Pan
papers.summary: Deterministic many-one NP-completeness of exact Euclidean SVP on full-rank free rank-two modules over Z[ζ_q] for variable odd primes q, in the canonical norm; does not assert average-case or power-of-two cyclotomic hardness.

papers.title: Low-Degree Learning from Localization Schemes
papers.authors: Gautam Chandrasekaran, Jason Gaitonde, Ankur Moitra, Arsen Vasilyan
papers.summary: Pinned Poincaré inequalities imply rapid decay under coordinate-erasure conditional resampling for functions orthogonal to low-degree polynomials. Extra bounded-width/degree or specified mean-field assumptions give optimal degree-linear decay and transfer broad product-distribution learning bounds to high-temperature Ising models.

papers.title: The 3-Uniform Hyperclique Hypothesis is False
papers.authors: Timothy M. Chan, Reina Itakura, Zhiyuan Ma, Yuancheng Yu
papers.summary: Two algebraic algorithms reduce 3-uniform 4-hyperclique counting to rectangular matrix products. Using the cited Uznański2026 characteristic-zero exponent theorem, the first yields n^3.957 deterministic time and a Max-3-SAT 2^0.99n consequence. The numerical subquartic conclusion depends essentially on that recent external theorem.

papers.title: A Near-Optimal Generalized Sorting Algorithm
papers.authors: Sanjeev Khanna, Aaron Putterman, Junkai Song
papers.summary: Reduces randomized generalized-sorting query complexity from soft-O(n^(3/2)) to O(n log^4 n) in expectation, assuming the allowed-comparison graph contains the hidden order's consecutive pairs.

papers.title: Bootstrap, Recolor, Verify: Hierarchical Integrality Gap Instance for 0-extension
papers.authors: Konstantin Makarychev
papers.classification_note: Integrality-gap construction; approximation category, rather than an unconditional computational-hardness theorem.
papers.summary: Proves an Omega(log k/(log log k)^5) integrality gap for the metric relaxation of 0-Extension. For each fixed r an initial construction yields Omega_r(log^{r/(r+1)} k). This is not a hardness theorem or a gap for the earthmover relaxation.

papers.title: Exact Counting and Sampling of Labeled Graphs of Bounded Treewidth with MSO Properties
papers.authors: KunCheng Zou, Yuanhong Wang, Yi Chang, Yuyi Wang, Ondřej Kuželka
papers.summary: Claims polynomial-time exact counting and weighted uniform sampling of labeled bounded-treewidth graphs satisfying fixed MSO2 properties, with f(theta)O(n²) arithmetic operations.

papers.title: No linear stretching of single-copy quantum pseudorandomness
papers.authors: Boyang Chen, Andrea Coladangelo, Yao-Ting Lin, Nikos Skoumios, Justin Tysdal, Yiming Wang
papers.summary: For every 1<γ<δ, constructs a unitary oracle with γn-output-qubit single-copy pseudorandom states but no δn-output 1PRS, even with controlled/inverse/conjugate oracle access. Rules out corresponding fully black-box stretching, not all non-black-box constructions.

papers.title: Optimal Vertex Sampling for Constraint Satisfaction Problems
papers.authors: Kehua Chang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: For fixed arity r and alphabet q, uniform k-vertex sampling estimates bounded-payoff dense-CSP optimum with optimal k=Theta(epsilon^-2) for constant confidence. Gives a real-valued coefficient-norm bound, sparse Max-Cut sampling estimates, and matching dense sampling lower bounds. Confidence amplification in the direct concentration statement costs log^2(1/delta).

papers.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy
papers.authors: Atul Mantri
papers.summary: Constructs a classical oracle with an exactly quantum-polynomial-time unary language outside PH that nevertheless has public-coin classical verification with an efficient quantum honest prover; message complexity must grow.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum Algorithms for Ordered Search
papers.authors: Joseph Carolan, Andrew Childs
papers.summary: Exact ordered search uses (ln n)/π+o(log n) worst-case queries, matching the established adversary leading constant; a separate zero-error continuum construction attains the same expected leading constant.

papers.title: Quasilinear Encoding at the Quadratic Alphabet Scale via Short Cartier Bases
papers.authors: Zemin Chao, Dongli Liu, Yixuan Li, Hengzhao Ma, Hongzhi Wang
papers.summary: Constructs exact-length, exact-dimension F_{q^2}-linear codes with q least power of two >=5/epsilon and distance >=N−K−epsilon N. Strongly explicit deterministic encoding, systematic inversion, membership and transposes use N poly(1/epsilon) log^4(N+2) bit work and O(N log(2+1/epsilon)) live bits. The added randomized mixed error/erasure decoder has quadratic K dependence and is quasilinear only at low dimension.

papers.title: When quantum thermal states look classical
papers.authors: Jordan Cotler, Harald Putterman, Alexander Zlokapa
papers.summary: Proves high-temperature classicality thresholds for Pauli Hamiltonians: separability at scale 1/(sk), and zero-free/phase-transition bounds at scale 1/max{s,sqrt(Jsk)}, with nearly commuting improvements, sampling and thermodynamic algorithms. Here s is local strength, k locality and J the largest Pauli coefficient; the distinctions between these normalizations matter.

papers.title: Compressed Permutation Oracles Revisited
papers.authors: Joseph Carolan, Christian Majenz
papers.summary: Improves soundness of the existing compressed permutation oracle from N^{1/12} to the tight square-root query scale, allowing coherent forward/inverse queries and ideal-cipher key superpositions. Explicit advantage is <=120q/sqrt(N−q+1)+q(q+1)/(N−2q+1) when 3q−1<=N. Applications give concrete sponge and Davies–Meyer search bounds.

papers.title: Seed Recycling: Explicit Codes for Mixed Synchronization Errors Matching the Leading Term of the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound
papers.authors: Quan D. Bui, Manabu Hagiwara, Shuche Wang, Van Khu Vu
papers.summary: For each fixed t, constructs explicit binary codes correcting t mixed insertions, deletions, substitutions and adjacent transpositions, with redundancy 2t log n + 2t log log n + O_t(log log log n) and polynomial-time encoding/decoding. Seeds are used to carry payload bits, so choosing collision-free hashes does not pay their full description length.

papers.title: Tight Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Continual Counting
papers.authors: Charlie Harrison‎, Ethan Leeman
papers.summary: For eta=max(epsilon,delta), L=log(n eta), U=1+min{L,log(eta/delta)}, proves unrestricted binary prefix-sum error Omega(L^{3/2}sqrt(U)/eta) in expected l_infinity and Omega(L^2 U/eta^2) in mean/max-coordinate expected square loss, for n eta sufficiently large, epsilon<=1,delta<=1/4. Blocked Laplace/Gaussian tree mechanisms match; high-privacy errors saturate at n and n^2.

papers.title: Zero-Freeness for Random Regular Graphs up to the Replica Symmetry Breaking Threshold
papers.authors: Zejia Chen, Chunyang Wang, Xinyuan Zhang
papers.summary: Claims whp zero-free regions and deterministic polynomial-time partition approximation on random fixed-degree regular graphs throughout the interior of replica symmetry, including hardcore occupation up to (2log d−2loglog d+2−2log2+o(1))/d and proper-coloring degree up to (2q−1)logq−2log2+o(1).

papers.title: Settling the Complexity of Hylland--Zeckhauser Equilibria
papers.authors: Zhengyang Liu, Yixin Tao, Yonglei Yan
papers.summary: Exact Hylland–Zeckhauser equilibrium is claimed FIXP-complete even when only an allocation is requested. For rational utilities in [0,1], a polynomial-time algorithm in input size and 1/δ obtains additive budget/utility error 0.0755211+δ; the stated constant PPAD hardness is conditional.

papers.title: Near-Linear Lower Bounds for Testing Directed Acyclicity
papers.authors: Artur Czumaj, Pan Peng, Yuyang Wang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: For each fixed η>0, some εη>0 makes adaptive randomized two-sided testing of directed acyclicity require Ω(n^(1−η)) outgoing-neighbor queries, even for simple graphs with both indegree and outdegree at most any fixed d≥2. Incoming edges are not queryable.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Approximate EFX for Chores via Flow and Matching
papers.authors: Genjie Qin, Qizhi Fang, Minming Li, Wenjing Liu, Xin Chen
papers.summary: Polynomial-time (3+epsilon)-EFX for arbitrary nonnegative additive rational chores; more generally (2+1/k+epsilon)-EFkX. Gives exact EFkX for m<=2kn and (2−1/k)-EFkX for m<=(3k−1)n. Four-agent ten-chore instance rules out gamma-EFX for gamma below approximately1.102578.

papers.title: Balanced Fair Division and Generalized Kneser Graphs
papers.authors: Sharareh Slipour, Amir Jafari
papers.summary: Proves chi(KG(2n,n,2))=6, resolving the Jafari–Alipour conjecture, and chi(KG(2n,n,3))>=10. Consequently five agents always admit balanced EF1 across two prescribed groups, sharply, and nine admit balanced EF2 for arbitrary monotone valuations.

papers.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
papers.authors: Ivan O. Shevchenko, Jun Liu, Xinzhi Liu
papers.summary: Claims that GAS for rational homogeneous polynomial vector fields of each fixed odd degree d≥3 is recursively enumerable complete in every sufficiently large fixed dimension. It supplies a degree-reduction construction and separate Lyapunov-stability consequences.

papers.title: On efficient global updates in first-order logic
papers.authors: Tuukka Korhonen, Marek Sokołowski
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: For fixed relational signature, bounded formula length and bounded-treedepth promise after every operation, supports FO global relation reinterpretations, local tuple updates and sentence queries in total O((n+T)alpha(n)) time and linear space. OVH rules out polynomial preprocessing plus strongly sublinear amortized operations on any subgraph-closed unbounded-treedepth class. Inverse-Ackermann lower bound already holds on star forests.

papers.title: How to Round Spiky Balls into Submission; And Faster Algorithms For The Closest Vector Problem
papers.authors: Divesh Aggarwal, Aditya Morolia
papers.summary: For each fixed 1<p<2, randomized exact CVP in full-rank rational lattices runs in expected 2^O_p(n) poly(input bits) time, with amplification to failure δ. Related exact SVP results include 1≤p<2.

papers.title: Learning Fourier-Sparse Signals and Multiband Signals
papers.authors: Dongrun Cai, Xue Chen, Xiaowei Shao, Yile Wang
papers.summary: For arbitrary clustered real frequencies within a bandlimit, gives an improper Haar–Fourier reconstruction from Õ(k/ε²) noisy samples and time, with squared L2 error O(ε)||x||²+O(1)||noise||². Frequency-list coverage is O(k) for the precisely recoverable part, not every frequency; proper k-term learning takes Õ(k)^O(k) time.

papers.title: Breaking the quantum barriers for Graph Collision
papers.authors: Arjan Cornelissen, Amin Shiraz Gilani, Shiva Kintali, François Le Gall, Subhasree Patro, Xingyu Zhou
papers.summary: For any known n-vertex graph, decides whether queried vertex marks contain an edge using soft-O(n^(11/17)) quantum queries; also claims Ω(√(n log n)) lower bounds on finite-field incidence graphs. Extends to positive-certificate-size-two functions over q symbols in soft-O((nq)^(11/17)).

papers.title: On the Computation of Sparse Equilibria in Normal-Form Games
papers.authors: Fan Chen, Constantinos Daskalakis, Gabriele Farina, Noah Golowich, Charalampos Platanos
papers.summary: For every fixed T, inverse-polynomial-accuracy T-product-mixture CCE in three-player games is PPAD-complete; analogous two-player CE hardness assumes PCP-for-PPAD. Two-player epsilon-CCE has O(1/epsilon) mixture components in polynomial time; constant-epsilon CE has action-count-independent sparsity with a tower-height O(1/epsilon) dependence.

papers.title: Distributional Quantum Query Complexity
papers.authors: Shalev Ben-David, M. H. Ebtehaj
papers.summary: Distribution-respecting composition, direct-sum and strong direct-product lower bounds for quantum queries, including search problems. Composition uses a new Shaltiel-free inner-function measure rather than ordinary distributional Q; direct product at success ((1+α)/2)^k costs Ω(k(1−α)Q^μ_(1−α)(f)).

papers.title: Sharp Spectral Bounds for Kikuchi Matrices: \\ The Hypergraph Moore Bound and Optimal Trade-offs for $k$XOR
papers.authors: Alexander Schmidhuber, Matthew Hastings
papers.summary: Claims Feige's hypergraph Moore bound without a density logarithm and sharp level-versus-density tradeoffs for random/planted kXOR. Normalized Kikuchi matrices yield even covers of size O(ell log(en/ell)) above C n^(k/2)/ell^(k/2−1), with absolute constants in the combinatorial theorem.

papers.title: Asymptotically good large-alphabet LDCs with polylogarithmic query complexity
papers.authors: Tal Yankovitz
papers.summary: Constructs constant-information-rate large-alphabet LDCs with polylogarithmic symbol queries and log alphabet subpolynomial in message size for chosen constant exponent. The stronger blockwise LCC corrects a specified field symbol by reading entire large blocks; this is not a binary constant-rate polylog-query code.

papers.title: Private Information Retrieval from Two Entangled Servers
papers.authors: Atul Mantri
papers.summary: Two entangled servers support information-theoretic PIR with a classical client and 2m+poly(log N,lambda) communication, private against one malicious server while the other is honest. The client forwards prescribed messages; server entanglement/work can be quasipolynomial, with a polynomial-resource alternative at higher communication.

papers.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Number-on-Forehead Communication
papers.authors: Haoyu Wang, Pei Wu, Guangxu Yang
papers.summary: An explicit partial Boolean Interleaved Unitary Product problem separates O(log n) quantum from soft-Ω(n^(1/32)) randomized communication in unrestricted interactive three-party number-on-forehead protocols; one clean qubit per constant-gap run suffices.

papers.title: A Constructive FPT Algorithm for Integer Cone Optimization with Convex Costs
papers.authors: Klaus Jansen, Felix Ohnesorge, Björn Schumacher
papers.summary: Deterministic2^{tau log(tau+1)2^{O(d)}}poly(input) algorithm for mixed integer-cone optimization over tau bounded rational generator polytopes, convex dense-encoded rational-polynomial costs on integer blocks, arbitrary linear aggregate/count constraints and unbounded number k of continuous coordinates. Returns<=2^{2d+1} generators/type or infeasible/unbounded.

papers.title: A Polynomial Kernel for Planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set
papers.authors: Zimo Sheng, Mingyu Xiao
papers.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial kernel for planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set with O(k^66 log²k) vertices/arcs. Compresses a dual grouped strong-connectivity augmentation instance by truncated distance records, then returns to planar vertex deletion.

papers.title: Streaming Weighted Set Cover Requires (Nearly) Linear Space
papers.authors: Ali Vakilian
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: For weighted set cover on n elements and m sets, p-pass alpha-estimation requires pS=Omega(mk^2/n) under M=m/2>=Ck^2 and v=n/2>=6alpha exp(27alpha)k ln(2M+1), v=o(k^2). Gives near-input-linear space for polylog passes and constant or O(loglog n) approximation, already for weights1,k.

papers.title: Tight Query Lower Bounds for Quantum Sampling, with an Application to Certified Randomness
papers.authors: Keshav Bhateja, Mehdi Esmaili, Atul Mantri
papers.summary: Claims Θ(N^(1/3)) queries to beat the honest expected XEB score by a constant for random Boolean Fourier sampling and Haar state access. For Fourier and canonical Haar oracles, near-ideal scores by poly(log N)-query devices imply almost log N bits of smooth private min-entropy, even with prior entanglement and later oracle disclosure. These are ideal oracle results, not guarantees for arbitrary circuits.

papers.title: A Dichotomy for MIP* in the Presence of Unital Noise
papers.authors: Yangjing Dong, Zhenyu Jiang, Minglong Qin, Penghui Yao, Haigang Zhou
papers.summary: For any fixed polynomial-time computable two-qubit state with maximally mixed marginals, sharing arbitrarily many copies yields MIPψ[poly,poly]=NEXP if separable or maximal correlation<1, and RE if entangled with maximal correlation=1. No additional shared quantum resource is allowed.

papers.title: Parameterized Tractability of Euclidean k-Steiner Tree
papers.authors: Sujoy Bhore, Sándor Kisfaludi-Bak, Dániel Marx, Saeed Odak
papers.summary: Discrete Euclidean k-Steiner Tree is deterministic FPT in each fixed dimension with 2^O_d(k log k)n^O(1) time. Continuous planar instances on an L×L integer grid admit 2^O(k log k)(n+L)^O(1), while unrestricted rational planar continuous instances and logarithmic-dimensional discrete instances are W[1]-hard.

papers.title: A Dichotomy for Terminal Cyclability
papers.authors: Matthias Bentert, Dario Giuliano Cavallaro, Sebastian Wiederrecht
papers.classification_note: Algorithmic tractability dichotomy for graph classes; structural graph theory secondary.
papers.summary: Terminal Cyclability is polynomial on every red-minor-closed annotated-graph class excluding an annotated planar graph, and NP-complete otherwise. Algorithm n^{2^{poly(b)}} uses terminal bidimensionality b and weak irrelevant vertices down to treewidth2^{poly(b)}log n.

papers.title: An Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Multidimensional Subset Sum
papers.authors: Lin Chen, Yuchen Mao, Guochuan Zhang
papers.summary: Claims deterministic O_{d,epsilon}(n+N^(d+epsilon)) time for fixed-dimensional subset sum with coordinates bounded by N, including a near-linear-in-maximum-item one-dimensional algorithm, and improved fixed-row integer-program feasibility.

papers.title: Beyond Gomory-Hu: All-Pairs $\times$ All-Pairs Mincuts in $O(n)$ Space
papers.authors: Koustav Bhanja, Merav Parter, Asaf Petruschka
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Compact mincut representation and failure oracle; data structures primary.
papers.summary: An O(n)-space representation recovers the mincut-unit ordering for any terminal pair in O(n) time, then answers whether a mincut separates a second pair in O(1), yielding an optimal-space single-edge-failure mincut oracle.

papers.title: Online Metric Problems via Randomly Perturbed Work Functions
papers.authors: Christian Coester, Danish Kashaev
papers.summary: A randomized perturbed-work-function framework gives O(log² n) metric allocation and k-taxi on n-point metrics, and ln k+ln ln k+O(1) weighted paging with a matching lower bound up to an additive constant. Other applications recover known matching/HST-server bounds.

papers.title: Max Independent Set Remains NP-hard when Excluding a Planar Induced Minor (and More)
papers.authors: Édouard Bonnet, Yeonsu Chang
papers.summary: Maximum Independent Set is NP-hard on graphs excluding the 5×5 grid as an induced minor. Also proves subexponential lower bounds under a weak ETH variant and hardness of coloring, feedback vertex set and domination on weakly sparse classes with restricted induced-subgraph components/twin-width.

papers.title: Quasi-polynomial-sized vertex multicut-mimicking networks and kernelization for Vertex Multiway Cut
papers.authors: Eduard Eiben, Roohani Sharma, Magnus Wahlström
papers.summary: Deterministic polynomial-time vertex multicut mimickers with |T|^7 c^{O(log c)} vertices preserving every terminal-partition optimum up to c, allowing terminal deletion. Exact case c=|T| yields quasi-polynomial kernels for Vertex Multiway Cut, request-sensitive Vertex Multicut and finite-group Feedback Vertex Set; hyperedge mimickers remove rank dependence.

papers.title: Constant Approximation of Fréchet Distance in Near-Linear Time
papers.authors: Haoqiang Huang, Zihe Wang, Shuo Zhang
papers.summary: Gives deterministic O(n^(1+epsilon)) time constant-factor approximation for continuous and discrete Fréchet distance in every fixed dimension, with a constant depending doubly exponentially on 1/epsilon.

papers.title: Efficient Private and Robust Statistics
papers.authors: Anming Gu, Arun Jambulapati, Syamantak Kumar, Argyris Mouzakis, Kevin Tian, Chutong Yang
papers.summary: Nearly input-linear algorithms simultaneously achieve differential privacy and contamination robustness for high-dimensional mean estimation, with near-optimal sample complexity, plus PCA and well-conditioned regression extensions.

papers.title: Pure Differentially Private Query Release via Laplace Input Smoothing
papers.authors: Zongrui Zou
papers.summary: A sparse Laplace perturbation followed by selection-only multiplicative weights achieves pure-DP statistical query release at the square-root error scale, in polynomially many idealized real-arithmetic/sampling operations.

papers.title: Hitting time for loose Hamilton cycles in the random hypergraph process
papers.authors: Jared León, Xizhi Liu
papers.summary: For even n, the random 3-uniform hypergraph process acquires a loose Hamilton cycle exactly when its last isolated vertex disappears, with high probability. Higher-uniformity and counting extensions are stated separately, with graph Hamiltonicity corresponding to minimum degree two.

papers.title: Accelerated Parallel Algorithms for Packing Linear Programming
papers.authors: Jiale Chen, Li Chen, Andrei Graur, Aaron Sidford
papers.summary: Deterministic width-independent packing LP algorithm with soft-O(1/epsilon) parallel depth and soft-O(nnz(A)/epsilon) work for arbitrary nonnegative A and inverse accuracy polynomial in dimension.

papers.title: List Decoding, Linear Hashing, and Furstenberg over $\mathbb{F}_q$
papers.authors: Vinayak M. Kumar, Geoffrey Mon
papers.summary: A multiplicity-gap polynomial method gives dimension-independent finite-field Furstenberg bounds, optimal-order maximum load for linear hashing over each fixed field, and random-linear-code list sizes uniformly controlled even near the maximal error rate.

papers.title: The Existence of Maximin Share Allocations is $\Delta_2^P$-complete
papers.authors: Sushmita Gupta, Sanjay Seetharaman
papers.summary: Existence of exact maximin-share allocations for additive goods is Delta_2^P-complete already for five agents; also weak coNP-hardness for three agents, strong coNP-hardness for variable agents, approximation and chores consequences.

papers.title: A Constant Approximation for Min-sum k-Clustering
papers.authors: Aditya Anand, Moses Charikar, Ruiquan Gao, Fabrizio Grandoni, Euiwoong Lee, Amatya Sharma, Ernest van Wijland
papers.summary: Randomized polynomial-time (2.16×10^9+ε)-approximation for metric min-sum k-clustering with exactly k clusters, via 2×10^7 LMP and factor108 bipoint rounding.

papers.title: Strong Backdoor to Forests is FPT: Tight Linear-Time FPT for Essentially General SAT
papers.authors: Olesia Bilyk, Aidar Munduzbaev, Roohani Sharma, Mamnoon Siam
papers.summary: Finds an exact size-k strong backdoor to incidence forests in 2^(2^O(k))|ϕ| time for non-tautological CNF; proves W[1]-hardness for every fixed target treewidth t≥2 even on non-tautological 3-CNF. A sub-double-exponential dependence would give 2^o(n/log n)-time 3-SAT.

papers.title: Sublinear Time Clustering: Taming Random Walks in Arbitrary Noise
papers.authors: Michael Kapralov, Ekaterina Kochetkova
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Neighbor-query pair classifier in d-regular graphs with induced φ-expanders and ε-sparse boundaries, arbitrary external noise and cluster sizes. Outside a fixed small bad set, expected time is r^{1/2+O(loglog(φ²/ε)/log(φ²/ε))} times polynomial ε^−1,φ^−1; no guarantee for two noise endpoints.

papers.title: A Circuit Complexity Trichotomy For Regular Languages
papers.authors: Stefan Göller, Amaldev
papers.summary: Regular languages under nonuniform unbounded-fanin AND/OR non-input-gate size and subset encoding have constant, almost-logarithmic [Omega(log n),O(log n loglog n)] or linear complexity. Omega is infinitely-often Hardy-Littlewood. Sublinear class has algebraic/logical/congruence characterizations and PSPACE-complete NFA membership.

papers.title: The Limits of Posted Prices in Random-Order Combinatorial Auctions
papers.authors: Frederick Qiu, Aviad Rubinstein
papers.summary: Random-order XOS combinatorial auctions admit no constant-factor truthful posted-item-price mechanism, even with unlimited computation and full revelation of previous valuations: the lower bound is Ω(log log log m). For one clause/demand-style query per bidder it strengthens to Ω(log log m).

papers.title: Synchronization Strings over a Ternary Alphabet
papers.authors: Huibo Xu, Shi Fu, Youming Qiao, Dacheng Tao
papers.summary: Constructs ternary synchronization strings of every length with ε=2001/2002, settling minimum alphabet size three. A computer-assisted stronger range ε>215/216 supports expected O(n²log³n) Las Vegas and O(nlog⁴n) Monte Carlo constructions; further counting/circle extensions are given.

papers.title: A unifying framework for Graph Minor Structure Theorems with polynomial bounds
papers.authors: Maximilian Gorsky, Evangelos Protopapas, Sebastian Wiederrecht
papers.summary: Polynomial-parameter homogeneous local/global graph minor structure framework using colour explorers; obtains tight a−1 major apices for excluding a-apex H, polynomial half-integral Erdős–Pósa bounds for fixed H and related colorful/coarse results.

papers.title: First Near-Additive All-Pairs Approximate Shortest Paths in Decremental Weighted Graphs
papers.authors: Eden Koveshi, Liam Roditty, Ariel Sapir
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Randomized decremental weighted undirected APASP against an oblivious adversary: (1+ε,2W2) in expected Õ(n^(3/2+o(1))sqrt(m)) total update time; (1+ε,2W1+2W2) in Õ(ε^-9 n^(7/3)); further k-dependent weighted/unweighted tradeoffs. Wi is local to the pair’s current shortest path.

papers.title: Word Length and Diameter in Permutation Groups
papers.authors: Markus Lohrey, Alexander Thumm
papers.summary: Binary-encoded diameter of explicitly generated permutation groups is PSPACE-complete, even solvable derived-length3; binary word length jumps from NP-complete for class2 nilpotent to PSPACE-complete for class3 nilpotent metabelian groups. Unary diameter is Pi2P-complete for full symmetric groups.

papers.title: Monadically Dependent Graph Classes Have Almost Bounded Merge-Width
papers.authors: Jan Dreier, Nikolas Mählmann, Michał Pilipczuk, Szymon Toruńczyk
papers.summary: Every monadically dependent graph class has radius-r merge-width n^{o(1)} for every fixed r, with witnessing sequences computable in n^{3+o(1)} class/r-dependent time. FO model-checking consequence needs a companion paper.

papers.title: Optimal Private Gaussian Multi-sampling
papers.authors: Raoof Zare Moayedi, Mohammad Hossein Yassaee, Javad B. Ebrahimi
papers.summary: For arbitrary unknown nonsingular d-dimensional Gaussian input, an approximate-DP mechanism uses Õ(m+d sqrt(m)/ε) samples and O(n³) operations to output exactly independent draws from QP=(1−α/(2m))P+α/(2m)N(0,I), jointly α-close to P^m. Matching bounds extend to dependent outputs and wider privacy ranges.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Brooks Coloring
papers.authors: Gopinath Mishra, Anish Mukherjee
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Fully dynamic explicit Δ-coloring for graphs whose maximum degree remains ≤Δ≥3 and which contain no K_(Δ+1): polylogarithmic amortized update time against an oblivious adversary after polynomial initialization; O(Δ log_Δ n) per update with high probability against adaptive adversaries. Color queries take O(1).

papers.title: Greedy BST is O(log log n)-competitive
papers.authors: Moshe Lewenstein
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Online geometric Greedy BST has cost O(n+OPT_n(X)loglog n) for arbitrary initial tree, refined to loglog k for k distinct requested keys. Initial comparator tree is free; O(n) initialization is necessary.

papers.title: An LP Algorithm for Counting Eulerian Orientations Through the Lens of Promise Polymorphisms
papers.authors: Jincheng Guan, Shuai Shao, Ke Shi
papers.classification_note: FP/#P classification is the main consequence; counting algorithm supplies tractability.
papers.summary: Polynomial-time algorithm for weighted Eulerian-orientation signatures in the former FP^NP tractable class, removing the NP oracle and obtaining an FP/#P dichotomy; associated complex Holant consequence with a nonzero odd-arity signature.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for the Weisfeiler-Leman Algorithm via Implicit Parity Systems
papers.authors: Radu Curticapean, Mingjun Liu, Daniel Neuen, Tim Seppelt
papers.summary: For fixed k≥3, k-WL distinguishing has unconditional n^(k−1−ε) deterministic multitape-Turing-machine lower bounds; variable-k distinguishing is EXPTIME/XP complete. Also Ω(n^(k−1)) iteration lower bounds and exp(Ω(n^(k−1))) bounded-treewidth homomorphism witness size.

papers.title: Mean-only Prophet Inequalities
papers.authors: Yilong Feng, Yaonan Jin, Xiaowei Wu, Xinyue Xiang
papers.summary: Knowing only n and E[max Xi], nonadaptive threshold algorithms attain0.7419 for iid prophet selection and0.6916 for prophet secretary at every n. IID full-information optimum remains higher around0.7454; mean-only randomized adaptive algorithms have a strict gap below it.

papers.title: Toward an Optimal Quantum Algorithm for Geometrically Local Hamiltonian Simulation
papers.authors: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Penghui Yao, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang
papers.summary: For fixed-dimensional finite-range normalized lattice Hamiltonians, simulates full time-T evolution with nearest-neighbor depth O(T log(nT/ε)), O(nT log(nT/ε)) gates and O(n) ancillas; at fixed suitable T and small constant error, uniform XXZ needs Ω(log n/log log n) depth.

papers.title: Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing: Below Half Threshold Rate
papers.authors: Hai H. Nguyen
papers.summary: For arbitrary nonzero evaluation points over any prime field p>n, Shamir sharing with threshold k≥(1/2−10^−14)n is exponentially resilient to arbitrary one-bit local leakage from every share. For k≥(1/2+δ)n, tolerates floor((δ/24)log₂n) leaked bits per share with stretched-exponential security.

papers.title: Subexponential Approximation of the Permanent in Deterministic Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Sergei Kudria, Jason Luo, Mahbod Majid
papers.summary: Deterministic polynomial-bit-time bounds L≤per(A)≤U for nonnegative rational matrices, with log(U/L)=O(n (loglog n)^2/log n); zero permanent is detected separately.

papers.title: Exact $\ell_p$-CVP via Euclidean SVP in Polynomial Space
papers.authors: Jiseung Kim, Minkyu Kim, Hyung Tae Lee
papers.summary: Randomized rank-preserving reduction from exact ℓp closest vector, for integer p≥2 and rational full-rank inputs, to exact Euclidean shortest vector using (Cp)^N poly(p,ℓ) time/calls and polynomial space outside the oracle. Provides exact arbitrary-target algorithms and enumeration of all closest vectors.

papers.title: Optimal Average Distortion for Non-Expansive Embeddings of Euclidean Metrics into the Line: With applications to cut-matching games and vertex expansion
papers.authors: Jack Spalding-Jamieson
papers.summary: Every n-point Euclidean metric has a non-expansive line embedding with average distortion O(sqrt(log n/log log n)), matching the known lower bound. Applications give O(log²n/log log n) cut-matching rounds for Ω(log n) spectral expansion and a sqrt(log n/log log n) reweighted-eigenvalue vertex-expansion loss.

papers.title: Optimal Separations Between Randomized and Quantum Query Complexity under Permutation Symmetry
papers.authors: Yunqi Huang, Lvzhou Li, Zekun Ye, Shenggen Zheng
papers.summary: For position-permutation-invariant partial functions over any finite alphabet, proves R_ε=O(Q_ε²), uniformly for 1/6≤ε<1/2. Graph properties satisfy R=O(Q⁴), fixed-k hypergraph properties O_k(Q^(2k)), with explicit promise families nearly attaining exponent 2k.

papers.title: Hardness of Unique Shortest Vectors and Bounded Distance Decoding
papers.authors: Sergei Kudria, Jason Luo
papers.summary: Randomized NP-hardness of constant-factor unique-SVP and BDD at every fixed radius fraction below 1/2 for each fixed computable ℓp norm, 1≤p<∞, including search. Finite-field code BDD below half distance is deterministically equivalent to UniqueCircuitSAT. Polynomial uniqueness/radius gaps are obtained for rational p>2 and p=∞.

papers.title: Rounded Potentials Certify Exact Maximum Flow
papers.authors: Ohad Trabelsi
papers.summary: An exact directed max-flow value has a certificate of n rounded vertex potentials of O(log(nW)) bits, verified in O(n+m) operations; applications include near-cubic MA all-pairs verification, near-linear online annotation and small distributed labels.

papers.title: Coupling Independence Implies Zero-Freeness
papers.authors: Shuai Shao, Ke Shi
papers.summary: Transfers coupling independence to a size-uniform complex zero-free neighborhood of [0,1] for bounded-degree Potts models; gives q≥11Δ/6, and q≥1.809Δ for Δ≥125 with stronger estimates. Also treats independent color fields and selected log-concave Boolean Holant problems.

papers.title: PIT and Reconstruction for Sums of High Powers
papers.authors: Amir Shpilka, Nimrod Kaplan, Yann Tal
papers.summary: For sums of r powers of inner degree-Δ polynomials, lifts an inner interpolating set of size s to a hitting set of size (s−1)Δd+1 when d+1≥(r−1)², in characteristic zero or sufficiently large characteristic. Proper reconstruction at d>(r+1)^4Δ and an individual-degree variant yield deterministic reconstruction and PIT for several sparse, roABP and shallow-circuit families.

papers.title: Constant-Factor Approximation for Generalized Max–Min Degree Arborescence in Quasi-Polynomial Time
papers.authors: Wenzheng Li
papers.summary: Rounds a generalized weighted path LP of degree K to value at least K/2^17−δ, where δ is the largest edge weight. Gives a 2^19-approximation for unweighted MMDA/GMMDA in expected n^{O(log n)} time and a constant expected-polynomial approximation for restricted submodular Santa Claus.

papers.title: Interior Point Methods Solve Random LPs in polylog(n) iterations
papers.authors: Shunhua Jiang, Daniel Dadush, Rasmus Kyng, Haoyuan Ma
papers.summary: An interior-point method solves min{1^T x:Ax=A1,x≥0} for Gaussian d×n matrices with cn≤d≤(1−c)n in O(log^{6.5} n) linear-system iterations with high probability, returning exact primal/dual optima in the real-RAM model.

papers.title: Adaptive Data Analysis Beyond the Privacy Barrier
papers.authors: Florian E. Dorner, Moritz Hardt
papers.summary: A deterministic leaderboard mechanism achieves O((log m)^(3/2)√(log(2kn/β)/n)) error, m=min(k,n)+1. A shifted-model reduction answers Ω(√n/log²n) adaptive statistical queries with O(log²n/√n) population error, separating population accuracy from simultaneous empirical accuracy.

papers.title: Tight bounds for fractional and randomized truthful scheduling
papers.authors: Georgios Anastasiadis, George Christodoulou, Elias Koutsoupias, Annamaria Kovacs, Conrad Schecker
papers.summary: Every truthful fractional mechanism on n unrelated machines has ratio at least (n+1)/2 against integral makespan, hence so does every truthful-in-expectation mechanism. A universally truthful mechanism attains (n+1)/2+O(√(n log n)). Arbitrarily many finite tasks are allowed.

papers.title: A Nearly Linear-Time FPRAS for Counting Knapsack
papers.authors: Ce Jin, Jaewoo Park, Barna Saha
papers.summary: FPRAS for counting nonnegative-weight subsets below a threshold in soft-O(n/ε²) word-RAM time, with word length O(log(n/ε)+log T), success probability at least2/3.

papers.title: A polynomial-time classical sampler for noisy quantum circuits from statistical mechanics
papers.authors: Jon Nelson, Joel Rajakumar, Chao Yin, Yifan (Frank) Zhang, Michael Gullans
papers.summary: For fixed lattice dimension and fixed depolarizing strength p>0, arbitrary local two-qubit unital circuits of depth exceeding O(p^-1 log(1/p)) have a polynomial-time classical sampler, including inverse-polynomial TV error; also gives relative approximation of arbitrary marginals. Runtime dependence on p is not polynomial uniformly as p→0.

papers.title: When Do Gradients Suffice? A Characterization of First-Order Convex Optimization
papers.authors: Noga Alon, Tomer Koren, Roi Livni, Shay Moran
papers.summary: Characterizes Banach unit balls admitting first-order convex optimization with query complexity depending only on accuracy: bounded margin-shattered trees, polynomial sequential Rademacher decay, nontrivial dual martingale type and a bounded uniformly convex regularizer are equivalent. Thus suitable Mirror Descent suffices whenever any first-order algorithm does.

papers.title: Quantum Interactive Proofs of Proximity
papers.authors: Kenan Wood
papers.summary: Every logspace-uniform NC property has a public-coin QCIPP with query, communication and verifier time Õ(n^(2/5)), even at proximity n^(-3/5). Gives conditional Ω(n^(1/3)) total-complexity obstructions, parity tradeoff connections, and tight linear lower bounds for almost all fixed-rate properties.

papers.title: Classical Tensor Codes and Quantum Tanner Codes Achieve Capacity on Erasure Channels
papers.authors: Henry D. Pfister, Oscar Sprumont, Gilles Zémor
papers.classification_note: Both classical and quantum codes; classified quantum because quantum erasure-capacity theorem is a central result.
papers.summary: Tensor products of capacity-achieving classical code families retain erasure capacity under error-decay/minimum-distance conditions. Builds binary quantum Tanner codes of rate ≥1−2ρ−ε for ρ<1/2, bounded checks and degree, linear distance, linear-time erasure decoding and exponentially small failure for fixed ρ,ε.

papers.title: Improved Steiner Forest Approximation via Cut Spaces
papers.authors: Shayan Cheshm Jahan, Alireza Keshavarz Hedayati, Ali Safari, AmirMohammad Shahrezaei
papers.summary: Deterministic polynomial-time 1.94295-approximation for undirected nonnegative-weight Steiner Forest.

papers.title: Optimal (Randomized) Compact Routing Schemes
papers.authors: Gur Lifshitz, Shiri Chechik, Avi Kadria, Liam Roditty
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Labeled compact routing achieves expected stretch 2k−1 with Õ(n^(1/k)) average local storage, Õ(k)-word labels and Õ(1)-word headers; only routing is randomized. Also improves deterministic, worst-case-storage and name-independent tradeoffs, including (8k/3+6,4k/9) expected stretch for unweighted worst-case storage.

papers.title: Breaking the Graph-Size Barrier for Tree Vertex Sparsifiers in Near-Linear Time
papers.authors: Daniel Agassy, Dani Dorfman, Haim Kaplan
papers.summary: Randomized near-linear-time construction of an O(k)-vertex hierarchical tree preserving every terminal cut within O(log²k log log k), hence all terminal multicommodity congestion within O(log³k log log k), for arbitrary capacitated undirected graphs.

papers.title: Pure privacy for structured problems in polynomial time
papers.authors: Hongjie Chen, Deepak Narayanan Sridharan, David Steurer
papers.summary: Gives polynomial-time pure-DP algorithms whose privacy cost reflects intrinsic structure: balanced SBM weak recovery at every fixed parameter above Kesten–Stigum and every fixed ε>0; low-threshold-rank MaxCut; sparse Gaussian mean estimation; and list-decodable means.

papers.title: Online Graph Coloring: Competitive Ratios Separating Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms
papers.authors: Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda
papers.summary: Separates randomized and deterministic online vertex coloring: deterministic competitive ratio Ω(n/log n), randomized O(n(log log n)²/log²n) against oblivious inputs, and deterministic upper O(n/(log log n)^(2−ε)).

papers.title: The Contraction Lemma Beyond ETH: Algorithms and Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Karthik Gajulapalli
papers.classification_note: Complexity and simulation consequences; audit qualifications remain unchanged.
papers.summary: Conditional on the stated, unaudited subexponential exact tensor-contraction lemma, develops new counting and simulation reductions; the checked fixed-algebraic-gate quantum simulation costs poly(input)·2^O((s+q)/sqrt(log(s+q))). The manuscript also claims search and hierarchy consequences and supplies a long contraction appendix. This review does not verify that appendix, an unconditional subexponential SAT algorithm, or an ETH refutation.

papers.title: Fitting Ultrametrics under any $\ell_p$ Objective
papers.authors: Moses Charikar, Ruiquan Gao
papers.summary: An O(p)-approximation for ultrametric and tree fitting in every fixed ℓp norm p>1; the same LP merging algorithm gives 12.091 for ℓ1 ultrametric fitting.

papers.title: Nearly Tight Cell-Probe Lower Bounds for Querying on Tree via Talagrand Inequality
papers.authors: Zihao Liang, Mingmou Liu
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Deterministic exact static cell-probe redundancy n/w^{O(t)} above Catalan entropy for bracket matching, RMQ and specified tree-navigation/excess interfaces; common position-only findopen/findclose convention is explicit.

papers.title: PAC Learning with Multiple Correct Answers
papers.authors: Steve Hanneke, Farnam Mansouri, Alireza F. Pour, Amirreza Shaeiri, Kun Wang
papers.summary: Characterizes PAC learning when each target gives at most ℓ acceptable labels. For finite labels, full-set and bandit learnability are governed by generalized Natarajan dimension, while demonstrations are governed by intersections of at most ℓ+1 hypotheses and may require ε^{−ℓ} samples. A packed dimension handles countable labels; agnostic demonstrations require additional compatibility.

papers.title: A Dichotomy for Exact Quantum Circuit Amplitudes
papers.authors: Chenghua Liu, Boning Meng
papers.summary: Exact computational-basis amplitudes for any fixed finite qubit unitary library are in FP for monomial, product-preserving or common diagonal-Clifford-frame libraries, and otherwise #P-hard under polynomial-time Turing reductions; gates may act on arbitrary ordered distinct wires.

papers.title: A Fast Algorithm for Subspace Convolution
papers.authors: Shlomo Perles, Omri Weinstein
papers.summary: Computes subspace zeta/Möbius transforms, transposes and span convolution in O_q(N log N) ring operations for fixed q=p^m when p is invertible in the coefficient ring. Rank-restricted incidence transforms are quasi-linear in input/output table size; applications include Grassmann kernels and rank-decomposition graph colouring.

papers.title: Path Decompositions of Sparse Graphs via Gaussian Sweeps and Faster Exponential Algorithms
papers.authors: Serge Gaspers
papers.summary: For all simple maximum-degree-three graphs, claims pathwidth, cutwidth and bisection width ≤(3/(4π))acos(5/6)n+o(n)≈.13982n; degree-four pathwidth≈.24577n and general per-edge 7m/48+o(n), with polynomial-time constructions and faster exact algorithms.

papers.title: Approximating the Euclidean Ball by Polytopes: Surprising Rates in High Dimensions
papers.authors: Yegor Gorodzha, Steven Hoehner, Gil Kur
papers.summary: Unrestricted-vertex approximation of the Euclidean ball in relative symmetric-difference volume has log vertex budget Θ(d log(1+1/(εsqrt(d)))) for sufficiently small ε; fixed-error budget exp(Θ(sqrt(d))), while cube and facet complexities remain exponential in d.

papers.title: A Proof of the Matrix Spencer Conjecture
papers.authors: Emrullah Akbas, Suvrit Sra
papers.summary: Claims full Matrix Spencer bound O(sqrt(n·max{1,log(d/n)})) for n symmetric d×d contractions, with a randomized polynomial-time coloring algorithm.

papers.title: Improved Bounds for Certifying Injective Norm of Sparse Random Tensors
papers.authors: Pravesh Kothari, Anand Louis, Rameesh Paul, Prasad Raghavendra
papers.summary: Polynomial-time universal injective-norm certificates have high-probability utility O_k(√p n^{k/4}+(log n)^{k/4}) on sparse Rademacher tensors; yields degree-2k SoS independence bounds O_k(√n/p^{1/k}) and quiet-planting low-degree lower bounds.

papers.title: Claw-free perfect graphs are chromatic-choosable.
papers.authors: Umesh Shankar, Suchismita Mishra, Narayanan N
papers.summary: Every claw-free perfect graph is chromatic-choosable; any proper precoloring of a clique of simplicial vertices extends from lists of size k≥ω(G). Gives polynomial elementary-graph and parameterized general algorithms.

papers.title: Optimal Black-Box Hardness Amplification for Integer Sums
papers.authors: Farhan Ali, Weiqiang Yuan
papers.summary: Integer summation amplifies δ-hardness to success ε using k=O(1/(δε²)) copies and multiplicative circuit loss O(ε^−2 log(1/δ)) independent of output range; claims matching adaptive black-box query lower bound and range-free inimitability regularity.

papers.title: Recovering Planted Subgraphs in Smoothed Models
papers.authors: Pravesh Kothari, Anand Louis, Rameesh Paul, Prasad Raghavendra
papers.summary: Recovers near-satisfiable planted induced 2-CSPs in smoothed Feige–Kilian variants. For flipped FK, achieves approximate recovery at the square-root scale with quadratic planted corruption budget; for FK gives near-square-root list recovery in n^{O(1/ε)} time with explicit smoothing-density and noise restrictions.

papers.title: A Sharp Rigidity Law for Effective Resistance
papers.authors: Tianlang Chen
papers.classification_note: Structural resistance-sparsifier lower bound, rather than an algorithmic construction.
papers.summary: Sharp spread-versus-edge law ε≥(N−1−d)/((N−1)(d−1)) for arbitrary positive-conductance graphs; implies Ω(N/η) resistance sparsifier edges already for K_N. Also proves exact missing-edge extremality, degree limits and separation between new-edge and subgraph output models.

papers.title: The Margin Complexity of Maxima of Linear Functionals
papers.authors: Tianlang Chen
papers.summary: The audited central fixed-margin theorem separates Θ(r log r) from O(r) fat-shattering growth for maxima of r homogeneous unit-norm linear functionals, at 1/(3√3) with witnesses and 1/7 at zero witnesses. The lower bound takes a supremum over ambient dimension. Critical-window refinements, unequal-radius entropy laws and multi-head retrieval results remain unchecked under the large-proof exception.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Classical and Quantum Simulation of Quantum Impurity Models
papers.authors: Jiaqing Jiang, Nathan Ju, Ojas Parekh, Chaithanya Rayudu, Andrew Zhao
papers.summary: Claims classical polynomial-time approximation of ground energy and thermal properties for fixed-size fermionic impurity models, while nonequilibrium Green's-function simulation captures quantum computation.

papers.title: The Price of Partial Information with Switching Costs: A Complete Characterization for Feedback Graphs
