papers.authors: Nicolò Cesa-Bianchi, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni, Emmanuel Esposito, Federico Fusco, Tomer Koren
papers.summary: Characterizes switching-cost regret for directed feedback graphs: square-root T up to logs for strongly revealing graphs, min(T,gamma^{1/3}T^{2/3}) otherwise when observable, and linear regret when unobservable.

papers.title: Progress on AC0[2]-Frege Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Yaroslav Alekseev, Svyatoslav Gryaznov, Toniann Pitassi, Robert Robere, Alexander Shekhovtsov, Iddo Tzameret
papers.summary: Majority lifting extends syntactic Res(PC_r) lower bounds to degree (log n)^(3/2), leading to superpolynomial depth-3.5 AC0[2]-Frege lower bounds when bottom degree b=o(sqrt(log n)).

papers.title: Pattern Matching with Edits in $\tilde{O}(n+k^3 \cdot n/m)$ Time
papers.authors: Tomasz Kociumaka
papers.summary: Claims an O(n+k^3 log^2(k) ceil(n/m)) algorithm for edit-distance pattern matching, resolving the Cole–Hariharan cubic-parameter conjecture up to logarithms and extending through the PILLAR model.

papers.title: Multiplying matrices via polynomials: operational asymptotic spectrum barrier
papers.authors: Alimzhan Amanov, Maxim van den Berg, Jeroen Zuiddam
papers.summary: Defines a formal operational preorder generated by specified polynomial-multiplication degenerations, direct/partial sums and tensor products. Proves these ingredients cannot yield square exponent below 9/4 or improve the stated piecewise rectangular bound, even after asymptotic closure. Also recovers existing any-field upper bounds.

papers.title: Settling the Approximability of Submodular Facility Location
papers.authors: Adam N. Elmachtoub, Bento Natura, Meike Neuwohner
papers.summary: Proves the Θ(log log |C|) approximation threshold for homogeneous metric submodular facility location in the value-oracle model, even for matroid-rank facility costs, together with a matching-order configuration-LP gap. Separate computational hardness is also claimed under NP≠RP.

papers.title: Linear-size $\ell_1$ sparsifiers
papers.authors: Victor Reis, Thomas Rothvoss
papers.summary: Every real m×n matrix admits a nonnegative diagonal row rescaling with O(n/ε²) nonzero entries preserving its ℓ₁ norm on every vector within 1±ε. Equivalently, every n-dimensional zonotope has such a linear-size segment sparsifier. The ℓ₁ construction takes 2^m times polynomial time, not polynomial time.

papers.title: Parallel Repetition for k-Player XOR Games
papers.authors: Mark Braverman, Dor Minzer
papers.summary: Every fixed k-player XOR game over a prime field with classical value below one has exponentially decaying n-fold repeated value, with a game-dependent exponent and no restriction on the question distribution. States extension to all finite Abelian groups.

papers.title: Is Randomness Necessary for Adaptive Data Analysis?
papers.authors: Edith Cohen, Haim Kaplan, Yishay Mansour, Shay Sapir, Uri Stemmer, Eliad Tsfadia
papers.classification_note: Adaptive statistical query accuracy is classified as learning/statistics, not regret-based online learning.
papers.summary: Every deterministic, even unbounded, mechanism on a domain of size 2^{O(n^2 log n)} is defeated with probability >=.9 by O(n log n) adaptive Boolean queries of error >.1 for a distribution uniform on 20n points. With b private random bits, O(n log n+b) queries suffice on a correspondingly larger domain. Analyst depends on mechanism.

papers.title: Strong Lower Bounds for Weak Epsilon-Nets
papers.authors: Sujoy Bhore, Reilly Browne, Da Wei Zheng
papers.summary: Proves f_3(r)=Omega(r^(3/2)) for weak 1/r nets of convex sets, and f_d(r)=Omega(r^gamma_d), gamma_d=0.5 floor((sqrt(8d+25)−1)/2), via shifted grid quadratic lifts. Gives corresponding fractional-piercing gaps and Hadwiger–Debrunner lower bounds.

papers.title: The Exact Communication Threshold for Parallel Repetition
papers.authors: Daiki Suruga
papers.summary: For every finite total two-player relation and arbitrary fixed input distribution, any worst-case communication rate strictly below zero-error internal information complexity yields exponentially small success on all n independent instances. Claims matching global-error amortized rates for distributional and randomized communication, with unrestricted rounds.

papers.title: The Greedy Superstring Conjecture Is False
papers.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Rishikesh Gajjala, Juha Harviainen, Alexander S. Kulikov, Ivan Mihajlin, Hiroki Shibata, Alexander V. Smal
papers.classification_note: Greedy approximation guarantees/counterexample are primary, rather than exact string algorithms.
papers.summary: Claims a binary-string family with greedy superstring ratio tending to 12/5, refuting the factor-two Greedy Conjecture; also improves the greedy upper bound to three and proves sharp or improved bounds for fixed-length strings.

papers.title: 4-Block Integer Programming is in FPT
papers.authors: Martin Koutecký, Alexandra Lassota, Koen Ligthart
papers.classification_note: Integer optimization algorithm is primary, despite fixed-parameter formulation.
papers.summary: General 4-block integer programming is FPT in small-block dimensions and coefficients, with near-linear dependence on number of local variables and polynomial logarithmic dependence on box diameter. Allows arbitrary coefficients in the few global columns and separable convex comparison-oracle objectives; complexity counts arithmetic operations and oracle calls.

papers.title: Tarski Fixed Points in Quasi-FPT Queries
papers.authors: Xi Chen, Ruiquan Gao, Yuhao Li, Aviad Rubinstein, Mihalis Yannakakis
papers.classification_note: Oracle query upper/lower bounds for a total fixed-point search problem; borderline with discrete/optimization algorithms, classified complexity.
papers.summary: For monotone functions on [n]^k, gives deterministic O(5^k (log n)^ceil(log2 k)) query upper bound and Las Vegas worst-case expected lower bound Omega((log n/polylog k)^floor(log4(6k+4))), even for unique fixed points. Arbitrary computation between oracle queries is free.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Randomized Generalized k-Server on Uniform Metrics
papers.authors: Junho Hwang
papers.summary: Randomized generalized k-server on uniform metrics has tight Theta(k log k) competitive ratio against oblivious inputs, and weighted uniform metrics have exp(Theta(k)) ratio via a 20^k algorithm. Unit-weight upper bound is (k+1)ln(2k) with no additive term, even for infinite spaces.

papers.title: Settling the Sample Complexity of Rényi Entropy Estimation
papers.authors: Qisheng Wang
papers.summary: Determines, for fixed noninteger alpha>0, sufficiently large alphabet d and sufficiently small error epsilon, Renyi-entropy sample complexity Theta(d^max(1/alpha,1)/(epsilon^(1/alpha) log d)+d^abs(1-1/alpha)/epsilon^2). Constants depend on alpha and are not uniform near integer orders.

papers.title: Almost-Linear Modular Composition over Arbitrary Commutative Rings
papers.authors: yang zhou, Mingsheng Wang
papers.summary: Claims a deterministic division-free algorithm computing g(a) mod monic f of degree n over every commutative ring with identity in n·2^O(√log n) ring operations, including preprocessing. General arbitrary monic moduli and arbitrary inputs are covered; finite-field bit complexity and special modulus X^n were already almost linear.

papers.title: Byzantine Broadcast in $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$ Communication
papers.authors: Yuval Efron, Jovan Komatovic, Ling Ren
papers.summary: Deterministic synchronous authenticated single-bit Byzantine broadcast tolerating any t<n adaptive corruptions with O(n² log⁴n·λ) communication by correct parties and O(t) rounds, using a PKI, signatures and binding vector commitments with λ>log n. Cryptographic primitives are idealized; this is not unauthenticated broadcast or a long-message amortization theorem.

papers.title: Combinatorial limitations of list-decoding Reed-Solomon codes
papers.authors: Omar Alrabiah, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami
papers.summary: For full-length RS codes over F_{q^{4t}}, rates q^{-2} and (1−q^{-1})² admit n^{Ω_q(log n)} lists at radius 1−√R+O_q(n^{-1/4}). Over infinitely many prime fields, explicit words have n nearby codewords at constant rate about 2/(3m) and radius about 1−1/m for m≡2 mod3; amplification gives arbitrary fixed polynomial list sizes at rate Θ(1/ℓ), constant gap Ω(1/ℓ²) below capacity. Thus prime-field constant-list capacity conjectures fail, while polynomial-list capacity remains compatible.

papers.title: Code Swendsen-Wang Dynamics
papers.authors: Dominik Hangleiter, Nathan Ju, Umesh Vazirani
papers.classification_note: The quantum stabilizer Hamiltonian/4D toric-code mixing result supplies the quantum-specific main contribution; classical-code chains are a substantial overlap.
papers.summary: Introduces Code Swendsen–Wang updates for classical parity-check and quantum stabilizer-code Hamiltonians. Proves mixing 2^O(Δ)poly(n,β) for approximately graphic/cographic codes, yielding polynomial mixing for the 4D toric code at every finite temperature, including criticality; also gives torpid mixing at a first-order transition in a 3-spin Curie–Weiss model.

papers.title: Optimal partition rank bounds for the determinant and other multilinear polynomials
papers.authors: Neil Krishnan, Guy Moshkovitz
papers.classification_note: Tensor partition-rank lower bounds are placed with algebraic complexity; this is a coarse boundary with algebraic/combinatorial mathematics.
papers.summary: Over every field, an n-variable-block set-multilinear polynomial whose permutation monomials all have nonzero coefficients has partition rank at least n for odd n and n−1 for even n. These bounds are attained by the determinant. Also gives characteristic-two elementary-multisymmetric examples with partition rank d or d−1 but bounded analytic rank.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Preprocessing Attacks on Quantum Cryptography
papers.authors: Fangqi Dong, Alex Lombardi
papers.summary: For K≤N binary-phase states in an N-dimensional Hilbert space, a T-query adversary with S qubits of oracle-dependent advice recovers the sampled key from one copy with probability O((1+T²+√(S(T+1)))/K). Classical advice improves the last term to S(T+1)/(KN). Also improves post-quantum PRG security and extends one-query unitary-synthesis lower bounds when random-oracle queries are allowed.

papers.title: Succinct Interactive Commitments and Arguments for NP from Exponentially Hard Injective One-Way Functions
papers.authors: Jesko Dujmovic, Daniel Wichs
papers.summary: Exponentially hard injective one-way functions yield public-coin interactive NP arguments with communication/rounds O-tilde(T^theta) and verifier time O-tilde(|x|+T^theta), for an assumption-dependent theta<1. Interactive vector commitments recursively amplify constant-factor compression. This is neither polylogarithmic succinctness nor a construction from ordinary polynomial-hardness OWFs.

papers.title: Optimal Quantum de Finetti Theorems via Argmax Rounding
papers.authors: Fernando Granha Jeronimo, Pei Wu, Haochen Xu
papers.summary: Improves two-site bosonic trace-norm de Finetti error from O(d/N) to O(sqrt(d)/N), and exchangeable error from O(d^2/N) to O(d/N). Argmax rounding also yields claimed subexponential disentanglers and separability algorithms.

papers.title: A Near-Linear Element-Kernel for d-Hitting Set
papers.authors: Zimo Sheng, Mingyu Xiao
papers.summary: For fixed d≥3, gives a randomized one-sided-error d-Hitting Set kernel with O_d(k log³k) elements, O_d(k^d log^(2d−2)k) sets and parameter O_d(k log³k), in expected polynomial time. Separately gives a deterministic O_d(k^(7/4) log^(3/2)k)-element kernel. Output elements re-encode assignments and need not be original elements.

papers.title: Autoregressive Distribution Learning and Universal Compression
papers.authors: Shuichi Hirahara, Mikito Nanashima
papers.classification_note: Distribution learning/evaluation equivalences are primary; universal compression is a major information-theory overlap.
papers.summary: Shows polynomial-time autoregressive distribution learning is equivalent to universal compression and entropy estimation of uniformly random prefixes. For prefix-closed distribution classes this is equivalent to evaluator learning and compression even without efficient decoding. The entropy estimator has completeness on the target class but soundness on every distribution; compression redundancy is m^(1-gamma) for fixed gamma>0. Additional generator-learning equivalence is for the full class of P/poly-samplable distributions.

papers.title: Expanding Codes with Polynomial Stretch
papers.authors: Isaac M Hair, Amit Sahai
papers.classification_note: Sparse code construction and adversarial-error recognition are primary; conditional cryptographic applications are secondary.
papers.summary: For fixed ε>0, samples binary sparse generator matrices with polynomial stretch, constant row weight O(ε⁻⁶) and(1−ε) neighbor expansion for every≤n^(1−ε) rows, yet efficiently recognizes all codewords with≤(1/2−ε) fraction adversarial errors against uniform. Gives a particular-expander XOR-MAJ distinguisher; PKE additionally assumes random-instance hardness and a new planting conjecture.

papers.title: Deterministic Fault-Tolerant Connectivity Oracles with Subqadratic Space
papers.authors: Merav Parter, Elad Tzailk
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Deterministic edge-failure connectivity encodings use Õ(n min{f^{2/5},n^{3/4}}) bits for simple undirected graphs, with exponential decoding; claimed lower bounds are Ω̃(n^{3/2}) and Ω̃(n f^{1/4}). Queries must list actual edges by endpoints, without edge labels. Polynomial preprocessing costs n^{o(1)} additional space. A separate Õ(n√f)-space construction has Õ(f) query time.

papers.title: Characterizing Quantum Advantage for Generalizations of the Boolean Hidden Matching Problem
papers.authors: Mark Bun, Joao F. Doriguello, John Kallaugher, Nadezhda Voronova
papers.summary: For every fixed predicate f of sign degree d≥2 and fixed block density α∈(0,1), f-Boolean Hidden Partition has randomized one-way communication Θ(n^(1−1/d)); quantum complexity is between Ω(n^(1−2/d)) and O(n^(1−1/ceil(d/2)) log n). Exactly sign degree two gives exponential quantum advantage; every d≥2 gives polynomial advantage. The quantum exponent gap for odd d remains.

papers.title: A Few Experts Suffice: Near-Optimal (Private) Online Learning with Limited Subscriptions
papers.authors: Hilal Asi, Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Tomer Koren, Mihir Singhal, Kunal Talwar
papers.classification_note: Nonprivate online learning theorem is primary, with a differential-privacy extension.
papers.summary: Against oblivious full-information expert losses, obtains near-optimal sqrt(T) regret up to polylogarithms using only polylog(N,T) distinct subscribed experts, while switches remain unrestricted. Gives pure-epsilon-DP regret O-tilde(sqrt(T)+1/epsilon), and the analogous optimal-up-to-logs rate for fixed-dimensional private online convex optimization.

papers.title: Dynamic Edge Orientation on Low-Arboricity Graphs: Breaking the log n Barrier
papers.authors: Sam Hiken, Nicole Wein
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: The Brodal–Fagerberg algorithm maintains an 11alpha-outdegree orientation of a fully dynamic loopless arboricity-alpha multigraph in O(alpha log log n) amortized time; an offline (5alpha-2)-orientation sequence with that many flips supplies the proof.

papers.title: A Complete Hierarchy of Local Lemmas
papers.authors: Dimitris Achlioptas, Konstantinos Kritharidis, Kostas Zampetakis
papers.classification_note: Classifying local lemma regimes supports counting; borderline combinatorics.
papers.summary: A finite-memory deletion-recursion hierarchy starts at asymmetric LLL and converges for every locally finite graph to the uniform Shearer threshold, with gap≤min(1/q,π²/(q+1)²), worst-case order tight. Effective finite presentations give certified threshold approximation; fixed periodic lattices require exp(O(ε^{-1/2})) time. Extends to positive deletion representations and zero-free polydiscs.

papers.title: Deterministic Approximate Nearest Neighbors in High Dimensions
papers.authors: Ying Feng, Piotr Piotr Indyk
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Fully deterministic Euclidean (1+ε)-ANN for n≥d uses n^{poly(1/ε)} preprocessing and space and O(d²+d poly(1/ε,log n)) query time. All queries are answered correctly. Bounds count arithmetic operations; the manuscript does not claim full bit complexity.

papers.title: Fully Dynamic Connectivity in $O(\log^3 n)$ Worst-Case Update Time
papers.authors: Valerie King, Quanquan Liu, Zeyu Nie
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Randomized fully dynamic connectivity on initially empty simple undirected graphs uses O(log³ n) worst-case insertion/deletion time, optimal O(log n/loglog n) query time, and O(n log² n) words. Correct throughout any fixed polynomial update horizon with high probability, including an adversary observing query answers only. An extra current-edge dictionary makes positive answers always correct and adds O(m) space.

papers.title: Polynomial-time Tensor Decomposition under the Kruskal Condition and the Lovitz--Petrov Generalization
papers.authors: Shiri Sivan
papers.summary: Randomized polynomial-arithmetic-time tensor decomposition under the Lovitz–Petrov uniqueness condition, hence under Kruskal’s condition, with probability one over continuous real randomness. Allows exact univariate root finding; also gives polynomial verification of the LP condition and uniqueness certification.

papers.title: The Necessity of Elias Codes in the Global Clock Model
papers.authors: Kuowen Chen, Shengquan Du, Tsvi Kopelowitz, Seth Pettie, Ben Plosk
papers.summary: Proves the checked summability lower bound for anonymous GlobalClock leader election with binary success/failure feedback and unknown n: attainable latency O(f(ceil log(n+1)) log(1/epsilon(n))) requires convergence of sum 1/f for nondecreasing f, nonincreasing error and log(1/epsilon)=O(n^(1-eta)). The claimed matching characterization, explicit monotone Elias-code upper bounds and adversarial contention efficiency approaching 1/e remain partly unaudited.

papers.title: Dynamic Steiner Tree under Edge Updates
papers.authors: Jeff Giliberti, Mohammad Taghi Hajiaghayi, Mohammad Mahdavi, Xinchen Yang
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Deterministic fully dynamic Oζ(1)-approximate Steiner tree for a fixed terminal set in connected undirected graphs with positive polynomial-range weights, soft-O(n^(1/2+ζ)) amortized updates, O(1) cost estimates and soft-O(n^(1+ζ)) explicit reporting, for fixed 0<ζ<1/2. Also a simpler randomized incremental tradeoff.

papers.title: Single-Exponential Algorithms for Directed Feedback Vertex Set on Planar Digraphs
papers.authors: Daniel Lokshtanov, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue
papers.summary: First single-exponential polynomial-space algorithms for planar Directed Feedback Vertex Set: randomized (2+sqrt(5))^k and deterministic approximately 8.03^k, based on an Euler alternation identity and a polynomial bimodal-completion routine.

papers.title: From One Hidden Subgraph to Dense Graph Partitions with Applications to Hardness of Clustering
papers.authors: Harman Agrawal, Pakapim Eua-anant, Bernhard Haeupler, Bundit Laekhanukit, Petar Mihov, Lazar Milenković, Rowan Santos, Zhijun Zhang
papers.summary: Graph-level transformation turns each hidden transversal induced subgraph into a partition of the target into its copies. Gives deterministic Almost-ETH 2-minus-epsilon hardness for metric min-sum clustering on{1,2}metrics and subpolynomial Densest-q-Partition hardness; also a weaker direct N^(1/4-epsilon) coloring hardness proof.

papers.title: Optimal Online Bin Covering across Stochastic Models
papers.authors: Nikhil Ayyadevara, Arindam Khan, Amit Kumar, K. V. N. Sreenivas
papers.summary: Asymptotic competitive ratio1 for deterministic random-order bin covering without horizon/OPT, hence unknown-distribution IID; also adversarial-order-with-sample and single-sample prophet variants.

papers.title: From smoothed analysis to backward error: The power of adaptive perturbations
papers.authors: Michał Dereziński, Michael W. Mahoney, Raphael Meyer, Christopher Musco
papers.summary: Obliviously perturbed general linear systems still require Ω(n) matrix-vector products for small forward error; deterministic small-backward-error solvers also need Ω(n), contrasting cited randomized O(log n/ε). Symmetric systems admit deterministic O(1/ε).

papers.title: A Tight FPT Approximation for Capacitated k-Median
papers.authors: Aditya Anand, Yichen Huang, Ragesh Jaiswal, Amit Kumar, Euiwoong Lee, Jatin Yadav
papers.summary: Deterministic (1+2/e+ε)-approximation for hard-capacitated metric k-median in f(k,ε)|I|^{O(1)} time, opening exactly k distinct facilities and respecting every capacity.

papers.title: Testing Fourier Sparsity Near Optimally
papers.authors: Arijit Ghosh, Manmatha Roy
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Nonadaptive Boolean Fourier-sparsity testing with O(s log³(2s)/ε) membership queries; distribution-free testing has the same query bound plus O(1/ε) samples from the unknown distribution. Guarantees concern query complexity.

papers.title: Potential Hessian Ascent IV: Sampling the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick Model at Beta < 1
papers.authors: Juspreet Singh Sandhu, Jonathan Shi, Holden Lee
papers.summary: For every fixed 0<β<1 and δ>0, polynomial-time o_n(1)-TVD sampling from zero-field SK Gibbs measure with probability ≥1−δ over GOE disorder. Uses stopped stochastic localization and path-space rejection.

papers.title: Random unitary circuits with constant spectral gap
papers.authors: Tim Baer, Jeongwan Haah
papers.summary: Claims constant spectral gaps, uniform in qubit count and all finite-dimensional representations, for random Pauli rotations and nearest-neighbor brickwork random unitary circuits; consequently O(nt) steps suffice for approximate t-designs. Includes orthogonal and Clifford analogues.

papers.title: Approximation and Even Arity Hardness for Boolean Constraint Satisfaction
papers.authors: Zhijie Zheng, Yucong He, Chengzhi Xie
papers.classification_note: Approximation algorithm is the leading result; even-arity hardness overlaps complexity.
papers.summary: Claims (k+1)/2^k−ε approximation for general weighted Boolean Max-k-CSP for fixed k≥5, matching known odd-arity hardness under the appropriate assumptions; also gives a strict rational improvement in even-arity UGC hardness. Randomized and deterministic precision costs differ.

papers.title: Hard Instances for Strong Semantic Proof Systems: CNFs for Depth-Four PC and Deep Instances for \(\mathsf{AC}^0[2]\)-Frege
papers.authors: Yaroslav Alekseev, Svyatoslav Gryaznov, Dmitry Itsykson, Toniann Pitassi, Robert Robere, Iddo Tzameret
papers.summary: Over F2, exponential semantic depth-3 polynomial-calculus size lower bounds for random 3-CNFs and functional/bit PHP; superpolynomial unrestricted-bottom-fan-in depth-4 bounds for lifted random logarithmic-width CNFs and weak unary PHP. For each fixed d>=2, depth-d input formulas need exp(Omega_d((log N)^(d/(d-1)))) semantic depth-d AC0[2]-Frege size but admit polynomial depth-(d+1) proofs.

papers.title: From Succinct Arguments to Proofs: Lower Bounds for Obfuscation and SNARGs
papers.authors: Abhishek Jain, Surya Mathialagan, Lawrence Roy
papers.summary: One-query nonuniform black-box reductions of iO/WE to falsifiable assumptions imply NP⊆coAM; multi-query uniform reductions, assuming NIZKs, imply public-key encryption and WE from OWFs. Analogous nonadaptive SNARG barriers allow long CRS and yield subexponential coAM/PKE consequences.

papers.title: Settling Nondeterministic Communication Complexity of Graph Connectivity
papers.authors: Zhijun Zhang
papers.summary: Optimal Ω(N log N) nondeterministic communication lower bound for graph connectivity; randomized Ω(N log min{1/ε,N}) and r-round Ω((N/r) log N) lower bounds. This does not settle unrestricted constant-error randomized complexity.

papers.title: The Binary Tree Mechanism is Optimal for Differentially Private Continual Counting
papers.authors: Konstantina Bairaktari, Markus Engelund Dahl, Kasper Green Larsen
papers.summary: Claims optimal expected ℓ∞ error Ω(log^(3/2)n) for approximate-DP continual counting at fixed suitable privacy parameters and Ω(log²n) for pure DP, even with offline access to the stream; derives a maximal discrepancy/privacy separation.

papers.title: The Harmonic Online k-Server Algorithm Is Poly(k)-Competitive
papers.authors: Yichen Huang
papers.summary: Claims that the memoryless Harmonic k-server algorithm is 2k^4-competitive on every metric against adaptive online adversaries, via a corrected electrical-energy assignment potential.

papers.title: unitaryQIP = unitaryPSPACE
papers.authors: Entong He, Fengning Ou, Mingnan Zhao
papers.summary: Proves unitaryQIP=unitaryPSPACE for worst-case unknown quantum inputs and arbitrarily inverse-polynomial synthesis error. Also obtains three-round protocols with polynomially many copies of the input, and EFI pairs imply BQP≠PSPACE.

papers.title: Non-Malleable Affine Extractors with Small Error and Complexity Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Yan Zhong, Xin Li
papers.summary: Constructs non-malleable affine extractors with linear output and exponentially small error at every fixed positive entropy rate, including a fixed number of affine tamperings. At entropy C n/log n obtains n^(1−η) output and error 2^−n^(1−η). Applications include exponential correlation bounds for weakly read-once linear branching programs and explicit near-maximal bounded-depth Res(⊕) lower bounds.

papers.title: A dichotomy theorem for approximating CSPs in random-order streams
papers.authors: Noah G. Singer, Madhur Tulsiani, Santhoshini Velusamy
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Streaming model and space dichotomy determine primary topic; CSP/LP approximation is the application.
papers.summary: For every finite-alphabet fixed-arity predicate family and gap beta<gamma, the basic LP characterizes single-pass random-order approximability: if LP solves the gap, O_epsilon(log^3 n) space solves the loosened gap; otherwise Omega_epsilon(n) space is needed even for O_epsilon(n) constraints at the tightened gap. Perfect completeness is retained when gamma=1.

papers.title: Finding a Shortest Vector and More in $2^{n/2+o(n)}$ Time using $q$-ary Coset Difference Tree
papers.authors: Minki Hhan
papers.summary: Claims randomized exact SVP on arbitrary n-dimensional lattices in worst-case time and space 2^(n/2+o(n)); also exact CVP for targets within approximately 1.039λ₁, with random-lattice/target consequences. Uses q-ary coset gradient aggregation and a difference tree.

papers.title: Beating the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound at Alphabet Size 42
papers.authors: Gil Cohen, Tomer Manket
papers.summary: Proves existence of nonlinear codes over alphabet 42 with rate at least 1−H₄₂(δ)+β for one uniform β>0 and every δ∈[.39,.48]. Alphabet restriction of AG codes, divisor-class averaging and expurgation improve the asymptotic Gilbert–Varshamov bound; no explicit construction is provided.

papers.title: An $O(n^{0.1537})$-Coloring Algorithm for $3$-Colorable Graphs
papers.authors: Kaisei Deguchi, Ken-ichi Kawarabayashi, Hirotaka Yoneda, Masataka Yoneda
papers.classification_note: Coloring approximation exponent determines primary topic, rather than structural graph theory.
papers.summary: Randomized polynomial-time O(n^0.1537)-coloring of every 3-colorable graph; a general vector-coloring independent-set framework first gives n^(1/6+o(1)), then band rounding and stronger constraints improve the exponent.

papers.title: Sharp universal death of entanglement threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Bobak Kiani
papers.summary: Determines the universal full-separability threshold for Pauli Hamiltonians with coefficient magnitudes ≤J and term-overlap degree Δ≥2: βJ≤arctanh(max_(0≤x≤1) x[(1−x)/(1+x)]^(Δ−1)). Gives commuting finite-tree entanglement witnesses above it, asymptotic constant 1/(2eΔ), and a classical product-state sampler a fixed distance below threshold.

papers.title: Matrix Spencer: Eight Standard Deviations Suffice and an Almost-Linear Time Algorithm for Dense Input
papers.authors: Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang
papers.summary: Claims Matrix Spencer discrepancy below 7.88 sqrt(n), a randomized below-11.51 sqrt(n) signing algorithm in n^(3+o(1)) arithmetic operations, and an asymptotic constant lower bound 2-o(1).

papers.title: Order-selection Prophet Inequality (Almost) Goes I.I.D.
papers.authors: Bo Peng, Zhihao Gavin Tang
papers.summary: An order-selection prophet algorithm for independent nonnegative values achieves .74500001, within .00045 of the optimal i.i.d. upper bound ≈.74544. Characterizes a local independent-arrival design class by uniform-marginal allocation kernels and certifies a perturbed kernel.

papers.title: Classical Oracle Separation of QMA from the QCMA Hierarchy and Quantum Cryptography Even When P = QCMA
papers.authors: Alper Cakan
papers.summary: Claims a classical oracle with P=BQP=QCMA=QCMAH strictly below QMA, together with several quantum cryptographic primitives despite that collapse.

papers.title: A Uniform Algorithm for Strict NP on Bounded-Treedepth Structures
papers.authors: Thomas Depian, Robert Ganian, Jakob Greilhuber, Marlene Gründel, Simon Wietheger
papers.classification_note: Uniform fixed-parameter decision/witness algorithms are primary; finite-model-theory machinery is secondary.
papers.summary: Uniformly decides every Strict NP sentence on a relational structure in f(|φ|,treedepth) times input size, with computable f. Constructs requested witness relations in the output-size-appropriate arity exponent; applications make stack/queue/track number and twin-width FPT in treedepth.

papers.title: Associativity of Multiplication Is Hard for Resolution
papers.authors: Vincent Liew
papers.summary: Claims exp(Omega((n/log n)^(1/4))) general-resolution lower bounds for associativity of n-bit multiplication under standard array and Wallace-tree encodings, with bounded-depth Frege extensions.

papers.title: Spectral gaps of Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run
papers.authors: Yunbum Kook, Santosh Vempala
papers.summary: For a bounded open convex body containing a unit ball, proves Hit-and-Run spectral gap Ω(1/(n² C_PI)) and coordinate Hit-and-Run gap Ω(1/(n³ C_PI)), retaining logarithmic dependence on initial χ² distance. Covariance-only consequences additionally invoke recent KLS results.

papers.title: SNARGs from any Witness Encryption, and More
papers.authors: Abhishek Jain, Zhengzhong Jin, Surya Mathialagan
papers.summary: Constructs transparent-CRS SNARGs for NP with non-adaptive soundness from LWE and any witness encryption, without an Extended Frege proof of correctness. A generic transformation supplies local cryptographic-EF correctness proofs; additional results concern designated-verifier arguments and succinct obfuscation.

papers.title: Improved Local Leakage Resilience of Shamir Secret Sharing and Worst-Case Optimal Polynomial Intersection
papers.authors: Yihang Sun, Mary Wootters
papers.classification_note: Central quantum polynomial-time coherent-oracle OPI algorithm and oracle separation, alongside a classical Shamir secret-sharing theorem.
papers.summary: Over prime fields and arbitrary distinct evaluation points, Shamir sharing of fixed rate R>1/2 tolerates any fixed b bits of local leakage; one-bit leakage is exponentially small for R>1/2-delta for an absolute delta>0, including arbitrary biases. For worst-case density-rho OPI lists supplied through coherent membership oracles, quantum poly(n,log p) time reaches SCL_rho(R)-epsilon and perfect satisfaction if R+rho>1. Separate existential discrepancy results extend beyond these algorithmic regimes; random evaluations require log p=n^Omega(1). An ordinary, unfolded OPI oracle separation uses vanishing 1/polylog(n) rate and quasipolynomial fields.

papers.title: Local Leakage Resilience of Multiplication-friendly Shamir Secret Sharing
papers.authors: Jihun Hwang, Hemanta K. Maji, Ilya D. Shkredov, Xiuyu Ye
papers.summary: For Shamir degree d=floor(cm), every fixed 0<c<1/2, proves near-optimal (2/π)^((1−o(1))d) worst-case one-bit-per-share leakage advantage for almost all public evaluation tuples over sufficiently large prime fields; m is a small c-dependent power of field bit length.

papers.title: Triangle-Freeness: Estimation Is as Easy as Testing
papers.authors: Asaf Shapira, Nick Kushnir
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Shows distance from triangle-freeness can be estimated with only a polynomial loss relative to its optimal testing query complexity: E_triangle(epsilon)<=poly(T_triangle(epsilon/8)).

papers.title: Quantum lower bounds for convex optimization and real matrix-vector query problems
papers.authors: Andrew Childs
papers.summary: Claims near-linear quantum query lower bounds for real matrix inversion and convex minimization, using Fourier witnesses vanishing on low-rank matrices; also treats trace and determinant.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Differentially Private Synthetic Graph Release with Nearly-Linear Additive Error
papers.authors: Marek Elias, Gautam Kamath, Janardhan Kulkarni, George Li, Jingcheng Liu, Sepideh Mahabadi, Pan Peng, Jakub Tarnawski, Hangyu Xu, Zongrui Zou
papers.summary: For nonnegative weighted graphs with public vertices and edge-weight l1 adjacency, gives polynomial-time (epsilon,delta)-edge-DP synthetic graph release with simultaneous cut error gamma times the true cut plus O(n/(gamma epsilon) log^7(n/(delta beta gamma epsilon))). Polynomiality is in an exact real RAM with Gaussian/Laplace draws, not bit complexity. Gives a nearly matching additive lower bound and applications including 1.387-approximate private correlation clustering with nearly linear additive error; that application additionally needs capped release and a private clustering baseline.

papers.title: Sampling from the Sherrington--Kirkpatrick Model up to Criticality
papers.authors: Hang Du, Brice Huang, Sidhanth Mohanty, Amit Rajaraman
papers.summary: For every fixed inverse temperature β<1, simulated annealing samples the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model to arbitrary inverse-polynomial total-variation error with high probability over GOE disorder; each temperature stage uses O(N log N) Glauber steps.

papers.title: Separating QMA from QCIP with a Classical Oracle, or, the Power of Quantum Proofs over Classical Interaction for Quantum Verifiers
papers.authors: Alper Cakan
papers.summary: Builds a classical oracle and unary language in QMA outside QCIP, allowing polynomially many classical-message interactions with a quantum verifier. Also constructs a sampleable gap and derives cryptographic black-box barriers; an IP-versus-MIP consequence uses an external relativized containment.

papers.title: Efficient Proper Agnostic Learning of Halfspaces
papers.authors: Anindya De, Elchanan Mossel, Shivam Nadimpalli, Joe Neeman
papers.summary: Gives a proper agnostic halfspace learner on the uniform Boolean cube with membership queries and runtime poly(n)+2^poly(1/ε), making the exponent of n independent of ε; also gives a slower sample-only proper learner.

papers.title: Fast Quantum Algorithms for Learning Linear Threshold Functions
papers.authors: Aleksandrs Krivcenko, Tuyen Nguyen, Ronald de Wolf
papers.summary: Gives optimal logarithmic real-membership queries for Gaussian LTF learning and optimal O(log k) Boolean queries to identify hidden equal-positive-weight majority support. With coherent Gaussian example preparation and its inverse, homogeneous LTF learning needs Theta(n^(1/4)/sqrt(epsilon)) queries, with efficient additional gates.

papers.title: An $\widetilde{O}(n^2)$-Time Sampler for Zero-Field Ferromagnetic Ising Models
papers.authors: Weiming Feng, Heng Guo, Yiyao Zhang
papers.summary: Gives a zero-field ferromagnetic Ising sampler on arbitrary multigraphs in O(m log² n+n)+O_β(n² log² n log²(n/ε)), for fixed β>1, using contraction sparsification and a new random-cluster mixing inequality.

papers.title: Second-Best Bilateral Trade is $1/2$ Efficient
papers.authors: Zhengyang Liu, Ying Qin, Zeyu Ren, Zihe Wang
papers.summary: Determines the worst-case second-best/first-best gains-from-trade ratio as exactly 1/2 for independent nonnegative bilateral-trade priors with finite first-best gains, under BIC, interim IR and ex-ante weak budget balance.

papers.title: Strong Selective and List-Decoding Direct Product Theorems for Quantum Query Complexity
papers.authors: Paul Beame, Niels Kornerup, Michael Whitmeyer
papers.summary: Proves strong selective direct products for every function, allowing algorithms to choose which k of m instances to answer, and strong list-decoding direct products for every partial Boolean-valued function. Gives multiplicative-adversary relational extensions and a general quantum matrix-mapping time-space application.

papers.title: A Nearly Quadratic Lower Bound for Linear Optimization over Convex Bodies in the Membership Oracle Model
papers.authors: Santosh Vempala
papers.classification_note: Linear-optimization membership-oracle lower bound is primary; sampling and volume consequences overlap counting_sampling.
papers.summary: Establishes Ω(n²/log² n) randomized membership-query lower bounds for constant-factor linear optimization, constant-TV uniform sampling and factor-two volume estimation, even for centrally symmetric parallelepipeds with polynomial radius ratio.

papers.title: Faster Minimum k-Cut II: Improved Randomized and Deterministic Algorithms for Weighted Graphs
papers.authors: Trevor Vaughn
papers.summary: For fixed k>=3, weighted Minimum k-Cut has randomized k^{O(k^2)} n^{k-1} log^2 n time and deterministic k^{O(k^2)} n^{k-1} polylog(n) time after O(m) parallel-edge aggregation. Assumes positive integer capacities with polynomially bounded total capacity; auxiliary weights have polynomial bit complexity. In particular weighted 3-cut becomes near-quadratic. Does not claim an unconditional matching lower bound.

papers.title: Explicit Reed-Solomon Subspace Designs: Optimal List and Line Decoding
papers.authors: Omar Alrabiah, Rohan Goyal, Venkatesan Guruswami
papers.summary: Constructs explicit Reed–Solomon codes over polynomial-size extension fields with capacity-approaching decoding and optimal-order constant list size, plus line-decoding/proximity-gap guarantees over the extension field.

papers.title: Three Standard Deviations Suffice While One Does Not
papers.authors: Victor Reis, Zhao Song
papers.summary: For every A in [-1,1]^{d by n}, there exists a signing x with infinity norm of Ax at most sqrt(3n arsinh(10d/n))+4; for d=n its asymptotic constant is about 2.99911. Separately, replacing a 2^-22 fraction of columns of a Hadamard matrix with independent signs gives, for sufficiently large power-of-two n, discrepancy exceeding (1+2^-22)sqrt(n) with high probability. The upper bound is existential, not a polynomial-time construction.

papers.title: Settling the Query Complexity of Weighted Stochastic Matching
papers.authors: Mahsa Derakhshan, Andisheh Ghasemi, Tao Yu
papers.classification_note: Static nonadaptive stochastic matching query algorithm, not arrival-based online matching; approximation is a secondary overlap.
papers.summary: Claims a (1−ε)-approximation in expected weight for nonadaptive stochastic matching using Oε(1/p) queries per vertex on general weighted graphs with independent nonuniform probabilities p_e≥p.

papers.title: Quantum circuit compilation with constant overhead
papers.authors: Chenyi Zhang, Xinyu Tan, Robin Kothari, David Gosset, Craig Gidney
papers.summary: Every G-gate circuit of arbitrary one-/two-qubit gates, including adaptive circuits with at most G gates on each branch, admits inverse-polynomial diamond-error compilation into an adaptive {H,T,CNOT} circuit with O(G) worst-case gates. The constant depends on the fixed error exponent. Dyadic rotations admit O(G+log(1/epsilon)) gates for arbitrary precision; an n-qubit phase-gradient state admits O(n) unitary gates at error 2^-n. Classical feedforward and ancillary resource states are allowed.

papers.title: Thin-shell stability and heat-adjoint hypercontractivity: logconcave sampling with sesteric complexity from a cold start
papers.authors: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala
papers.summary: For general logconcave densities given by a zeroth-order evaluation oracle and a standardized inner ball in a constant-measure ground set, constructs finite-q Renyi-warm starts in soft-O(n^{2.5}+sqrt(q)*n^2 min{R sqrt(L),R^{3/2} Lambda^{1/4}}) expected queries. Near-isotropic instances give soft-O(sqrt(q)*n^{2.5}). New Gaussian-tilt thin-shell stability and heat-adjoint hypercontractivity provide balanced Renyi warm-to-output guarantees. This is oracle-query complexity, not total bit complexity; centering/inner-ball assumptions matter.

papers.title: Sampling Matchings in Near-linear Time
papers.authors: Tianshun Miao, Yitong Yin
papers.summary: For the monomer–dimer model on any simple graph with fixed activity upper bound lambda_max and arbitrary positive edge activities, single-edge Glauber mixing is O_lambda(m log^2(n/epsilon)), with no maximum-degree restriction. Provides near-linear-work parallel sampling of depth soft-O_lambda(min{Delta,sqrt(nu(G))}) with high probability, and counting in soft-O_lambda(m+n+nu(G)^2/epsilon^2) work. Does not claim perfect-matching sampling or allow lambda_max to grow at no cost.

papers.title: The Optimizer's Windfall: Bounding Hindsight Gain under Random Restrictions
papers.authors: Xiaohui Bei, Wenhao Wu
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Dense-CSP sampling/query consequences motivate sublinear classification; general hindsight inequality overlaps optimization.
papers.summary: For fixed-degree multilinear optimization over products of compact unit-ball domains, independent nonnegative variable weights have hindsight gain bounded using only second moments. Uniform Bernoulli restriction at rate p has gain O_r(p^{r-1/2} sqrt(1-p) n^{(r-1)/2} ||A||_F), tight in the stated fixed-r,p regime. Consequences include optimal O(epsilon^-2) sampled vertices for dense fixed-alphabet Max-rCSP additive epsilon*n^r estimation, MaxCut query bounds, sharp percolation preservation condition p*e(G)/v(G)->infinity, and O(epsilon^-3) sampled particles for dense bounded-locality quantum energy.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Complexity Across the Computational Phase Transition
papers.authors: Zhe Ju, Jingcheng Liu, Yitong Yin
papers.classification_note: Mixing/counting transition is primary; fine-grained conditional reductions are a substantial complexity overlap.
papers.summary: Claims a near-critical hard-core mixing transition governed by exp(Theta(n delta^2/d)) times polynomial factors, with degree-uniform upper bounds and fixed-degree lower bounds. A robust SAT reduction transfers fixed power savings along specified inverse-polynomial distances above uniqueness; it is a conditional speedup implication, not an unconditional lower bound for all algorithms.

papers.title: The list size of random linear and LDPC codes at capacity
papers.authors: Shashwat Silas
papers.summary: For fixed prime power q and fixed radius 0<rho<1-1/q, sufficiently small fixed epsilon yields random-linear-code list size floor(h_q(rho)/epsilon) or one greater with high probability as block length grows. Outside an exponentially tiny fractional-part window it equals the ceiling. Also proves threshold-rate equivalence, up to arbitrary prescribed slack for sufficiently large fixed odd check size, between the Gallager-type LDPC ensemble and random linear codes for a precisely defined class of convex local properties. This is combinatorial list size, not efficient list decoding, and does not assert equality for every fixed small LDPC check size.

papers.title: A Deterministic O(log m)-Competitive Algorithm for Online Minimum Cost Bipartite Matching with Delays
papers.authors: Tung-Wei Kuo
papers.summary: Proves the existing deterministic VRM algorithm is O(log m)-competitive in every metric for online bipartite matching with delays, without knowing the metric or m: at γ=2 the bound is 24+18 ln m. A non-bipartite extension gives 28+24 ln m using minimum-weight matching to implement augmenting paths.

papers.title: Unconditional Unclonable Encryption
papers.authors: Prabhanjan Ananth, Seyoon Ragavan, Amit Sahai
papers.summary: Constructs efficient one-time private-key unclonable encryption of a single bit with perfect correctness and optimal-order information-theoretic advantage O(2^(-n/2)). Encrypts as a random eigenstate of a nonidentity n-qubit Pauli; encryption uses local Cliffords and decryption local Pauli measurements.

papers.title: Random Deletion for Circuits in Regular Matroids
papers.authors: Karthekeyan Chandrasekaran, Chandra Chekuri, Weihao Zhu
papers.classification_note: Near-minimum circuit count and random-deletion structure in regular matroids are primary; algorithmic enumeration/parallelism are consequences.
papers.summary: Proves m^{O(α)} α-near-minimum circuits in regular matroids, improving a quadratic exponent in α. Independent retention probability m^{−40/g} produces an independent set with high probability; conditioned on preserving a fixed α-short circuit, nullity is O(α log(α+2)). Gives randomized enumeration and parallel-algorithm consequences in the independence-oracle model.

papers.title: Spectral gap of Lee-Yang Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Chaithanya Rayudu, Jun Takahashi
papers.summary: For every 2-local n-qubit Lee–Yang Hamiltonian H satisfying the specified pairwise coupling inequality, adding a uniform field −h∑Z_i with h>0 gives a unique ground state and gap at least h/4. Polynomially bounded instances, including bipartite quantum Max-Cut, consequently admit inverse-polynomial-accuracy ground-energy estimation in BQP.

papers.title: A Near-Optimal Parallel Algorithm for Finding Matroid Bases
papers.authors: Aaron Putterman, Sanjeev Khanna, Junkai Song
papers.summary: Finds a basis of an arbitrary independence-oracle matroid in O(n^(1/3) log^(1/3)n) parallel rounds with polynomially many queries per round, matching the classical lower-bound exponent. Gives weighted-basis and related matroid consequences.

papers.title: Matrix Samplers and Quantum-Proof Extractors: Their Correspondence and Almost-Optimal Constructions
papers.authors: Kuan Cheng, Ruiyang Wu
papers.classification_note: Classical matrix-sampler/extractor construction is primary. Quantum side-information security is important but follows the shared rule for classical quantum-proof extractors.
papers.summary: Establishes a quantitative correspondence between D-dimensional matrix samplers and bounded-quantum-storage extractors. Constructs explicit strong matrix samplers with m+Oα(log(D/δ)) random bits and Oα(ε^(−2−α)log^(1+α)(D/δ)/log(ε^−1log(D/δ))) samples for δ≤ε; also gives strong conditional-min-entropy extractors with logarithmic seed, linear output and exponentially small error at every constant entropy rate.

papers.title: Counterexamples to Beyond-Johnson Proximity Gaps over Binary Fields
papers.authors: Quang Dao, Scott Kominers, Justin Thaler, Kai Zhe Zheng
papers.summary: Constructs binary-field additive-domain counterexamples to beyond-Johnson Reed–Solomon proximity gaps and polynomial list-size hopes at fixed rate. Gives explicit exceptional-challenge counts and reports Lean formalizations.

papers.title: A Walk from Free Probability to Matrix Discrepancy II: Weaver's Problem and the Kadison-Singer Problem
papers.authors: Tarun Kathuria
papers.summary: Gives a deterministic polynomial real-arithmetic algorithm for Weaver/Kadison–Singer signing with discrepancy below 58 sqrt(epsilon). Polynomial bit complexity is explicitly not claimed.

papers.title: High-dimensional expanders, the sparsest cut problem, and Steurer’s conjecture
papers.authors: Farzam Ebrahimnejad, Shayan Oveis Gharan
papers.classification_note: Structural counterexample to an expansion conjecture; approximation and mixing implications are secondary.
papers.summary: Refutes Steurer's low-correlation separated-sets conjecture using sparse high-dimensional expanders, even for nonnegative unit vectors satisfying squared triangle inequalities. Derives vertex expanders whose every symmetric stochastic reweighting has average L2 mixing time at least log^(5/4-o(1)) n.

papers.title: New Algorithms for Dynamic Maximal Matching and Edge Coloring
papers.authors: Julia Chuzhoy
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Fully dynamic explicit maximal matching against an adaptive adversary with worst-case update n^(4/5+o(1))log(1/p) and recourse soft-O(n^(4/5)), allowing a flagged per-update failure p. More generally the tradeoff is n^(1−δ/4+o(1)) update versus soft-O(n^δ) recourse for δ≤4/5. A deterministic variant has n^(20/21+o(1)) update and soft-O(n^(4/21)) recourse. Gives adaptive near-Δ edge-coloring primitives.

papers.title: Deterministic Connectivity Sketches Under Edge Deletions
papers.authors: Sanjeev Khanna, Aaron Putterman, Madhu Sudan
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Gives a deterministic one-way deletion-connectivity representation using about n^(7/4) bits and a lower bound about n^(3/2). Separates connectivity determination from surviving-edge recovery and extends to bounded-update-multiplicity dynamic streams.

papers.title: Constant-Overhead Injection into Quantum Codes
papers.authors: Louis Golowich, Venkatesan Guruswami
papers.summary: Constructs constant-rate quantum codes supporting fault-tolerant injection and ejection with constant quantum depth and linear qubit overhead under locally stochastic noise. Bare input/output qubits retain unavoidable constant error probability; error correction and encoded-state preparation have exponentially small failure.

papers.title: Sampling Colorings Close to the Maximum Degree: Non-Markovian Coupling and Local Uniformity
papers.authors: Vishesh Jain, Clayton Mizgerd, Eric Vigoda
papers.summary: For each fixed delta > 0, proves optimal O_delta(n log n) mixing of Metropolis Glauber dynamics for k >= (1+delta)Delta colors on graphs of girth at least seven and sufficiently large constant Delta. The degree threshold does not grow with n.

papers.title: The asymptotic spectrum of tensors is connected
papers.authors: Péter Vrana, Jeroen Zuiddam
papers.classification_note: Asymptotic tensor spectrum is an algebraic-complexity invariant; no fast arithmetic algorithm is the main result.
papers.summary: Proves path-connectedness of the asymptotic spectrum of complex tensors of each fixed order, so evaluation on any fixed tensor is a closed interval. Develops semiring interpolation and new spectral-point constructions.

papers.title: A general counting and sampling Lov\'asz local lemma
papers.authors: Vishesh Jain, Clayton Mizgerd, Huy Tuan Pham
papers.summary: For finite independent variables and general constraints satisfying p_a<=c x_a product_(b in N_(G^2)(a))(1-x_b), gives an FPRAS for satisfaction probability and an approximate conditional sampler in polynomial expected time, with polynomial degree independent of domain size, arity and dependency degree; c=1/100 suffices.

papers.title: The Sample Complexity of Multi-Class Omniprediction
papers.authors: Joey Rivkin, Princewill Okoroafor, Michael P. Kim
papers.summary: Characterizes multiclass Lipschitz omniprediction sample complexity up to logarithmic factors: epsilon^{-5/2} for three classes and epsilon^{-(K-1)} for K>=4, plus the hypothesis-complexity term. Shows that simultaneous omniprediction for all bounded proper losses is statistically unlearnable already with three labels and two affine benchmarks.

papers.title: Asymptotically Optimal Weighted Edge Colorings via Local Bin Packing
papers.authors: Rishikesh Gajjala, Arindam Khan
papers.classification_note: Weighted edge coloring via local bin packing is combinatorial optimization; structural extremal bounds overlap combinatorics_geometry.
papers.summary: Claims asymptotically optimal local-bin-packing bounds for simple weighted graphs, optimal leading weighted-degree bounds for bipartite/general multigraphs, and improved 1.62 and 1.999 local-packing factors for those multigraph classes. Includes a simple bipartite counterexample to the exact weighted-degree conjecture.

papers.title: $\mathsf{EQP}\subseteq\mathsf{IP}$ Does Not Relativize
papers.authors: Sinan Oral, Supartha Podder
papers.summary: Constructs a recursive oracle separating exact quantum polynomial time from both classical interactive proofs and the polynomial hierarchy. Uses exact Forrelation values +/-1/2, solved with three phase queries, plus repaired hard distributions supported on the exact promises.

papers.title: Nested Effective Resistance Partitions and Eulerian Sparsification
papers.authors: Richard Peng, Sushant Sachdeva, Paul Zhang, Yibin Zhao
papers.classification_note: Static graph sparsifier construction is primary; not a dynamic/streaming data structure.
papers.summary: Every Eulerian directed graph admits an O(n epsilon^-2)-edge reweighted Eulerian spectral sparsifier constructible in polynomial time. With polynomially bounded weight ratio, a nearly linear-time algorithm constructs O(n epsilon^-2 log n) edges with high probability.

papers.title: A computational phase diagram for the transverse field Ising model
papers.authors: Thuy-Duong (June) Vuong
papers.classification_note: The computational phase diagram concerns quantum transverse-field Hamiltonians, including quantum Gibbs preparation.
papers.summary: Gives a sharp spectral-width/temperature tractability boundary for transverse-field Ising partition functions and several observables, together with quantum Gibbs preparation and hardness beyond the boundary.

papers.title: A Faster Strongly Polynomial Time Algorithm for Submodular Function Minimization
papers.authors: Alina Ene, Huy Nguyen
papers.summary: For evaluation-oracle submodular minimization, returns an exact minimizer with O(n^2 log n) oracle calls and randomized O-tilde(n^2 EO+n^3) total time. A deterministic implementation has O-tilde(n^{omega+1}) overhead. The model assumes exact real arithmetic.

papers.title: Cutting Down the Tower: Single-Exponential Envy-Free Cake Cutting
papers.authors: Qilin Ye, Yannan Bai
papers.classification_note: Envy-free fair-division protocol is economics even without a strategic truthfulness guarantee.
papers.summary: Claims a deterministic Robertson–Webb protocol for complete envy-free cake cutting with polynomial(n)·2^n queries for general nonnegative nonatomic additive valuations; pieces may be disconnected.

papers.title: Polynomial Time Algorithms for the Kadison-Singer Problem
papers.authors: Zhao Song, Song Yue
papers.classification_note: Algorithmic discrepancy/Kadison–Singer theorem remains combinatorics_geometry under the shared structural/discrepancy rule.
papers.summary: Claims a deterministic polynomial-bit-time algorithm signing rational Hermitian rank-one matrices with operator norm at most 3.5 times the square root of their matrix-variance norm.

papers.title: NP-Hardness and Additive Inapproximability of Deterministic Communication Complexity
papers.authors: Serge Gaspers, Tao Zixu He, Simon Mackenzie
papers.summary: Given an explicit total Boolean truth table, computing deterministic communication complexity is NP-hard, and approximation within every fixed additive error remains NP-hard. Separate constructions cover unrestricted public-output protocols and strict bit-alternation, including Yao's original receiver-output convention.

papers.title: Worst-Case to Average-Case Reductions for Linear Algebra: Optimal, Simple, and General
papers.authors: Alexander Golovnev, Satyajeet Nagargoje, Igor Shinkar, Harsimran Singh, Noah Stephens-Davidowitz
papers.classification_note: Worst-case/average-case reductions are primary; the problems being reduced concern matrix arithmetic.
papers.summary: Gives optimal-dependence worst-case to average-case reductions for constant-degree matrix polynomials over prime fields, unconditional matrix inversion reductions, and triangle-parity and approximate-entry variants.

papers.title: Rapid mixing of quantum spin chains at any finite temperature
papers.authors: Leeseok Kim
papers.summary: For arbitrary bounded finite-range 1D quantum Hamiltonians, every fixed finite inverse temperature and local dimension admit a constant-block Petz heat-bath sampler mixing in O(log(n/epsilon)) time. The normalization gives each site rate one. A separate construction prepares Gibbs states in polylog(n/epsilon) depth with nearest-neighbor gates and ancillas.

papers.title: Parallelizable and addressable transversal non-Clifford gates on good quantum LDPC codes
papers.authors: Yiming Li, Zimu Li, Zhengyi Han, Zi-Wen Liu
papers.summary: For every fixed r≥3, constructs asymptotically good qLDPC codes, and good qLTCs with constant soundness, supporting Θ(N) parallelizable addressable transversal logical C^(r−1)Z gates; the gate family is not universal transversal computation.

papers.title: Quantum channel tomography: optimal bounds in the near-boundary regime
papers.authors: Kean Chen, Aadil Oufkir
papers.summary: Characterizes coherent channel-tomography query complexity near the dimension boundary: for Kraus rank at most r and dilation ratio tau=rd2/d1>1, diamond error epsilon already requires Theta(rd1d2/epsilon^2), while tau=1 permits Heisenberg scaling. Choi trace error has the gradual transition Theta(d1^2/epsilon + min{(tau-1)d1^2,(tau-1)^2d1^2d2^2}/epsilon^2). Upper bounds use parallel queries; lower bounds allow sequential adaptive coherent protocols. Exact lower-bound statements require sufficiently small universal epsilon; no efficient implementation is claimed.

papers.title: Non-Abelian sheaf quantum LDPC codes: good and magical
papers.authors: Zimu Li, Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Zi-Wen Liu
papers.summary: Claims constant-rate linear-distance non-Abelian qLDPC families by gauging sheaf codes, with additional almost-good code spaces exhibiting long-range magic and linearly many encoded magic states from gauging measurements.

papers.title: On Random Purifications of Isometries and Channels
papers.authors: Eli Goldin
papers.summary: Simulates forward access to a random unitary completion of an isometry with dimension-dependent error, while proving an exponential channel-query obstruction to simulating random dilations and even the quantum switch of a channel with itself.

papers.title: Counting Paths in Time $O^*(2^k)$, with Extensions to Counting Bounded Treewidth Graphs and Multilinear Monomials
papers.authors: Fahad Panolan, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue, Meirav Zehavi
papers.classification_note: Approximate counting of paths/patterns is primary, rather than decision/search graph algorithms.
papers.summary: Randomized relative approximation counts directed k-vertex paths in 2^k poly(k)(n+m) ε^−2 log(2/δ) arithmetic operations; extends to forests/bounded-treewidth patterns in (2+η)^k n^Oη(t) and multilinear coefficient sums of monotone circuits in 2^(ωk/2) poly(s,k). This is approximate, not exact counting.

papers.title: Optimal Multi-Item Auctions with I.I.D. Values
papers.authors: Boyu Liu, Zhengyang Liu, Zihe Wang
papers.summary: For additive buyers and i.i.d. two-point item values, gives an explicit deterministic DSIC ex-post-IR auction optimal even among randomized mechanisms for arbitrary buyer and item counts, with polynomially computable expected revenue. With support size part of the input, optimal revenue and construction become #P-hard already for one buyer or already for two items. These are separate hardness restrictions; n and m are unary and priors are rational.

papers.title: Parity Decision Trees of Depth $O(4^d \log \| \widehat f \|_1)$ for Boolean Functions $f$ of $\mathbb F_2$-Degree $d$
papers.authors: Shengyu Zhang
papers.summary: Proves deterministic parity decision-tree depth O(1+4^d log ||f̂||₁) for Boolean phases of F₂-degree d, extending the XOR log-rank conjecture to degree O(log log s), where s is Fourier sparsity.

papers.title: Depth-Independent Mergeable Arguments
papers.authors: Zvika Brakerski, Maya Farber Brodsky, Omer Paneth, Tomer Solomon
papers.summary: Constructs mergeable arguments with proof length independent of merge depth using LWE and unleveled FHE, with P, NP and trapdoor-language variants under different security and merge-tree restrictions.

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent
papers.authors: Yuhan Ye, Kaizhao Liu
papers.summary: For smooth convex objectives and any predetermined nonnegative gradient-descent stepsize schedule, proves worst-case error n^(-p_sil-o(1)), p_sil=log2(1+sqrt2), matching the silver exponent. Also matches the anytime exponent 2p_sil/(1+p_sil) up to o(1), meaning infinitely many bad horizons for a single infinite schedule. The hard objective and dimension may depend on the schedule; this is not a lower bound for adaptive stepsizes or accelerated methods.

papers.title: A Deterministic Polynomial Kernel for Odd Cycle Transversal
papers.authors: Tomohiro Koana, Soh Kumabe
papers.summary: Derandomizes the polynomial kernel for Odd Cycle Transversal, obtaining O(k^3 log^3 k) vertices through deterministic cut covering and almost multilinear representations of gammoids.

papers.title: Silver Rate Is (Almost) Optimal for Gradient Descent: The Strongly Convex Case
papers.authors: Kaizhao Liu, Yuhan Ye
papers.summary: For smooth strongly convex functions of condition number kappa and any predetermined nonnegative GD schedule, proves iteration complexity Omega(kappa^(1/p_sil-o(1))*log(1/epsilon)) for either squared distance or relative objective error. More explicitly the gap to silver is exp(O(sqrt(log kappa)))*log kappa. Schedules may depend on kappa and the finite horizon, but not on observed gradients; dimensions are unrestricted.

papers.title: Counting Hamiltonian Cycles in Bipartite Digraphs Deterministically in $O(1.9526^n)$ Time
papers.authors: Tomohiro Koana, Soh Kumabe
papers.classification_note: Exact counting of Hamiltonian cycles is primary; the weighted TSP consequence is secondary.
papers.summary: Counts directed Hamiltonian cycles in bipartite n-vertex graphs deterministically in O(1.9526^n) time. Also gives a pseudopolynomial weighted traveling-salesman consequence.

papers.title: Quantum Security of XOR of Permutations via Fourier Analysis
papers.authors: Wonseok Choi, Minki Hhan, Junyoung Jang
papers.summary: For fixed r≥2 and q≤2^n/57774, XOR of r independent private random permutations is quantum-indistinguishable from a random function with advantage O(min{q³/2^(rn),q^(3/2)/2^((r−1/2)n),2^−((r−3/2)n)}). Adversary queries the construction, not the constituent permutations; proposed matching attacks are heuristic.

papers.title: Distinguishability Threshold for Random Geometric Graphs
papers.authors: Zach Hunter, Aleksa Milojevic, Benny Sudakov
papers.classification_note: Statistical distinguishability of geometric versus independent random graphs is classified as learning/inference; probability/graph-geometry is a close alternative.
papers.summary: Obtains the conjectured spherical random-geometric-graph indistinguishability scale d of order n^3 p^3 log^3(1/p), up to epsilon-dependent constants, in a specified moderately sparse density range.

papers.title: Exhaustive Search Is Hard to Beat in Constant Depth for Hyperclique and Orthogonal Vectors
papers.authors: Nikolai Chukhin
papers.summary: Proves constant-depth De Morgan circuit gate lower bounds m^Omega(ell) for polynomial-size r-uniform hypercliques (ell<=m^(1/h-epsilon)), nearly exhaustive-search exponents for growing subpolynomial ell, and n^Omega(k) clique bounds through k<=n^(1/(h-1)-epsilon). Derives n^(k-epsilon) gates for fixed-k OV in sufficiently large polylogarithmic dimension and k-Dominating Set, plus Omega(n^2) wires for depth-three2-OV with dimension at least(1+eta)log n. These are restricted-circuit lower bounds, not unrestricted running-time conjectures.

papers.title: A Polynomial Erdős-Pósa bound for Eulerian digraphs
papers.authors: Esther Galby, Roohani Sharma, Bart van der Steenhoven
papers.summary: Proves an O(k^4) arc-disjoint-cycle Erdős–Pósa bound for Eulerian digraphs, together with an Omega(k log k) lower bound.

papers.title: Exact Euclidean k-Means: Faster in the Plane, Hard Beyond It
papers.authors: Tian Bai, Fedor Fomin, Xiaoyang Xu
papers.summary: Gives exact planar Euclidean k-means in n^{O(k/(log k)^{2/3})} time and parameterized lower bounds in dimensions at least three and for dimension with fixed k.

papers.title: Tree Covers for Directed Graphs: Distance Oracles, Routing Schemes and Spanners
papers.authors: Gur Lifshitz, Shiri Chechik
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Constructs directed k-strong tree covers of expected overlap O(k*n^(1/k)): for each ordered pair, a tree-pair gives distance(u,v)+(k-1)*roundtrip(u,v). Different directions may use different tree-pairs, yielding a(2k-1)-roundtrip spanner with O(k*n^(1+1/k)) edges. Provides path-reporting oracles and routing; O(log log k) query oracles use(2k-2)-strong stretch, not the base k-strong stretch. General k>=4 construction is expected soft-O(min(mn,n^2.5)).

papers.title: Constant-factor approximation of MinCostCSP with a conservative majority polymorphism
papers.authors: Marcin Kozik, Stanislav Živný
papers.summary: Classifies constant-factor approximability of MinCostCSP for finite structures admitting a conservative majority polymorphism, with a tractability-versus-cyclic-Unique-Games-deletion reduction criterion.

papers.title: Improved Separations between Quantum and Classical Communication Complexity of Total Functions
papers.authors: François Le Gall
papers.summary: Compresses the lookup construction converting partial communication problems into total functions, obtaining near-linear input overhead. Applications give polylogarithmic quantum communication versus randomized complexity near sqrt(n), or n^{1-epsilon} with more constant quantum messages.

papers.title: Solving One of Many Instances Is Almost as Hard as Solving One
papers.authors: Nikolai Chukhin, Alexander S. Kulikov, Ivan Mihajlin, Alexander V. Smal
papers.summary: Shows that choosing one of k distinct input pairs saves only O(log k+log n) deterministic communication for total Boolean functions, and gives corresponding formula-depth bounds, resolving the cited Dinur–Meir conjectures in polynomial and quasipolynomial arity regimes.

papers.title: A tight approximation for metric k-means via squared tapered rounding
papers.authors: Hao Zhu
papers.summary: Claims deterministic polynomial-time (1+8/e+epsilon)-approximation for general finite rational metric k-means with supplied candidate centers, matching its NP-hardness threshold for every fixed epsilon>0. Extends a recent k-median tapered-rounding framework by separating taper strength c=0.85 from potential coefficient kappa=8, with a new squared-cost comparison inequality certified by interval arithmetic plus a local zero-slack argument.

papers.title: Optimal Approximation for Constrained Correlation Clustering via Repulsion
papers.authors: Yixin Cao, Ying Xu
papers.summary: Gives a randomized(2+epsilon)-approximation for constrained correlation clustering and a vertex-cover reduction establishing matching factor-two hardness under UGC, including the cluster-deletion special case.

papers.title: Identity Testing of Markov Chains from a Single Trajectory
papers.authors: Jianhao Jia
papers.summary: Claims identity testing from one Markov-chain trajectory in O(n/epsilon) transitions for reversible reference kernels against arbitrary alternatives, and O(n log n/epsilon) for arbitrary finite kernels, from every initial state.

papers.title: Tight Coreset Bounds for $(k,z)$-Clustering in Euclidean and Doubling Metrics
papers.authors: Junqiu Hu, Lingxiao Huang, Jian Li, Baoduo Xu
papers.summary: Claims tight up to polylogarithms strong nonnegative-weighted subset coreset sizes: Euclidean unrestricted dimension min{k^{(2z+2)/(z+2)}ε^{-2},kε^{-z−2}} for fixedz≥1; doubling metrics kD·min{k^{1−2/z}ε^{-2},ε^{-z}} forz≥2, sufficiently smallε andD≥C_z log(2/ε). New doubling upper branch holds for allD≥1 andε∈(0,1).

papers.title: Adaptive Sparsifier Revisited: $(1 \pm \epsilon)$-Approximate, Fast, and Simple
papers.authors: Maximilian Probst Gutenberg, Yu-Cheng Yeh, Gernot Zöcklein
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Maintains a (1±ε) spectral sparsifier with near-linear size in a fully dynamic weighted graph against an adaptive adversary in polylogarithmic amortized update time (with polynomial dependence on ε^−1). Weights are polynomially bounded in the reduction. Core result is additive Laplacian error ηΔ in decremental unweighted multigraphs; the full spectral guarantee uses an external expander-decomposition reduction.

papers.title: Making Every Edit Count: Efficient Binary Edit Correction at the Gilbert–Varshamov Bound
papers.authors: Ryan Gabrys, Shubhransh Singhvi, Eitan Yaakobi
papers.summary: Constructs binary codes correcting any fixed total number t of insertions, deletions, and substitutions with redundancy 2t log2(n)+O_t(1), deterministic polynomial-time construction, encoding, and decoding.

papers.title: Precedence Constraint Scheduling on a Fixed Number of Machines
papers.authors: Klaus Jansen
papers.summary: Claims an exact polynomial-time algorithm for precedence-constrained unit jobs on every fixed number m of identical machines, including the classical three-machine case, using globally describable separator hierarchies.

papers.title: Incremental Open Addressing Has No Time-Space Tradeoff
papers.authors: Martin Farach-Colton, Andrew Krapivin, William Kuszmaul
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Claims incremental open addressing with O(1) worst-case expected insertion and positive/negative query time all the way to full occupancy, with reordering and no metadata beyond a count.

papers.title: A New Characterization of Streaming Decidability of Boolean CSPs Under Deletions
papers.authors: Aditya Bandekar, Amatya Sharma, Santhoshini Velusamy
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Characterizes one-pass strict-turnstile satisfiability of each fixed nontrivial Boolean constraint languageΓ by its integer capturing degreed: upperO_Γ(n^d polylogn) bits and lowerΩ_Γ(n^d/logn) for polynomial-length streams. Upper algorithm recovers active constraints preserving all solutions; upper bound extends to fixed larger domains.

papers.title: Competitive Equilibrium for Linear Chores is CLS-complete
papers.authors: Qian Liu, Shinuo Ma, Yixin Tao, Minji Yang, Weiqiang Zheng
papers.summary: Proves CLS-completeness of computing an exact competitive equilibrium in Fisher markets with divisible linear chores by encoding approximate quadratic KKT points into equilibrium prices.

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Algorithms for Nuclear Tensor Norms and Multipartite Quantum Separability
papers.authors: Martino Bernasconi, Giulio Malavolta
papers.summary: Gives deterministic d^{O_epsilon(k)} algorithms for constant-additive Frobenius weak membership in real tensor nuclear-norm balls and multipartite separable-state sets; also claims dimension-free quantum testing from copies.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for $(1+\epsilon)$-Approximation for Minimum Spanning Trees in Doubling Metrics
papers.authors: Jan Höckendorff, Felix Hommelsheim, Christian Sohler, Di Yue
papers.summary: Deterministic (1+ε)-MST construction in bounded-doubling metrics in 2^O(ddim)(n log n+min{n²,n ε^−1 log(1/ε)}) exact-distance real-RAM time, with matching expected randomized lower bound already at doubling dimension seven. Euclidean coordinate inputs admit a faster ε-dependent term via bichromatic closest pair.

papers.title: Near-linear-Time Sampling of the Ferromagnetic Ising Model at the Tree Uniqueness Threshold
papers.authors: Tianshun Miao
papers.summary: Zero-field ferromagnetic Ising on every simple graph of maximum degree Δ≥3 admits TV-ε sampling in expected O(n+m log³(n/ε)) work through β=Δ/(Δ−2). Also zero-field XY for Δ≥8 through its robust tree threshold in soft-O(m+n exp(O(sqrt(log(n/ε)))) real-arithmetic work, and integer Potts q≥3 in near-linear q^{O(1)}-weighted work for β−1≤.1(β_od−1).

papers.title: Dynamic $(\Delta+1)$-Coloring with Polylogarithmic Worst-Case Update Time
papers.authors: Maxime Flin, Mohsen Ghaffari
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Randomized fully dynamic algorithm explicitly maintains a proper (Δ+1)-coloring against an oblivious adversary, with polylog(n) worst-case time and recolorings per edge update with high probability. Smooth dynamic almost-clique decomposition plus staged coloring controls immediate repairs and deferred data maintenance.

papers.title: Rapid mixing of Gibbs samplers via quantum Dobrushin–Shlosman conditions
papers.authors: Cambyse Rouzé, Daniel Stilck França
papers.summary: Constructs QBP-dressed finite-block Gibbs-preserving KMS channels. Claims logarithmic trace-norm mixing for all fixed-temperature finite-range spin chains, uniform in on-site field norms and single-exponential in βJ_interaction; stability around interacting DS references; and weakly quartic-interacting Fermi–Hubbard systems at fixed hopping and effective-potential spread. Nearly linear gate preparation requires bounded local input terms.

papers.title: Edit Distance Approximation: Subquadratic Factor Three and Monge Approximation Schemes
papers.authors: Egor Gorbachev
papers.classification_note: Approximate edit-distance string algorithm; aligned with historical string-algorithm taxonomy.
papers.summary: Randomized factor-three edit-distance approximations in soft-O(N^(11/6)) unit-cost and soft-O(N^(40/21)) metric-weighted time; a Monge sparsification theorem with soft-O(n log W/√ε) core supports (1+ε) bounded/dynamic weighted algorithms. Nonmetric weights have fine-grained/query hardness even on small alphabets.

papers.title: Near-Logarithmic Inapproximability of Parameterized Set Cover
papers.authors: Bingkai Lin, Xin Zheng
papers.summary: W[1]-hardness of approximating k-Set Cover within Ω(log ρ/(k² log log ρ)) for n sets and universe at most ρ log n, k^{Ω(k²)}≤ρ≤n^{O(1)}. Gives randomized k-OV-based fine-grained hardness, a randomized Turing universe–gap equivalence in the specified parameter range, and primal/dual VC-dimension bounds.

papers.title: Beyond light cones: State preparation complexity in quantum spin glasses
papers.authors: Omar Al-Ghattas, David Gamarnik, Bobak T. Kiani
papers.summary: For dense Gaussian quantum p-spin Hamiltonians, a state family with effective weight-p Pauli-profile entropy O(n²) stays Ω(√n) below the optimum for sufficiently large fixed p (depending on the entropy constant). Subquadratic entropy gives o(√n) advantage over any conditioning benchmark, including product states. Implies Ω(n²/log n) arbitrary one/two-qubit gate lower bounds even with unlimited discardable ancillas; depth-width, MPS, magic-hierarchy and Clifford+T consequences have separate parameters.

papers.title: Sample Complexity of Multiclass Omniprediction
papers.authors: Lunjia Hu, Haipeng Luo, Jon Schneider, Kunhe Yang
papers.summary: For k≥3 and only two benchmark predictors, multiclass omniprediction has no uniform finite sample bound for all bounded proper losses, and exponential-in-k bounds for Lipschitz proper/GLM losses. Lipschitz pseudo-regret needs Ω((kεlog(1/ε))^−((k+2)/4)) samples in the stated small-ε range; batch loss-adaptive and online guarantees differ.

papers.title: A Noise Operator Approach to Quantum Query Complexity and Time-Space Tradeoff Lower Bounds
papers.authors: Paul Beame, Blake Holman, Niels Kornerup
papers.summary: A noise-operator framework proves quantum time-space lower bounds for almost every fixed strongly universal hash, removes the logarithmic loss for integer multiplication, and gives an unrestricted-output sorting lower bound.

papers.title: NP-Hardness of Bounded Distance Decoding for Reed-Solomon Codes and Variants, via Non-Archimedean Rings
papers.authors: Venkata Gandikota, Elena Grigorescu, S. Venkitesh
papers.summary: Deterministic NP-hardness for Reed-Solomon decoding with n^alpha agreement surplus beyond dimension, arbitrary fixed rate and subexponential field size; extends to folded codes with growing folding and shrinking capacity gap.

papers.title: Algorithmic Aspects of the Fermi--Hubbard Model
papers.authors: Ainesh Bakshi, Ankur Moitra, Xinyu Tan
papers.summary: Quantum Gibbs sampler for nearest-neighbor fixed-dimensional Fermi–Hubbard with beta<=c/(d³ t_max), mixing in O(log(n/epsilon)) from any physical even state, independently of on-site repulsion/chemical potential. General m-mode local fermionic systems need beta<=c4^-m(DL)^-3; qubits beta<=c(DL)^-3 independently of arbitrary fields. Exhibits efficiently preparable non-Gaussian-mixture fermionic Gibbs states and entangled qubit states; separability holds up to fields of order log(1/beta)/beta under suitable locality constants.

papers.title: Constant-Time Inverse Suffix Array Queries in Compact Space and Sublinear-Time Construction of Suffix Array Indexes
papers.authors: Dominik Kempa, Tomasz Kociumaka
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Constant-time inverse-suffix-array queries in O(n log sigma) bits, with deterministic O(n min{1,log(sigma)/sqrt(log n)}) packed-input construction. Also supplies two suffix-array time-space tradeoff families with the same construction bound.

papers.title: Obfuscation via Proofs of Equivalence and Polynomial-Time Reductions to Falsifiable Assumptions
papers.authors: Damiano Abram, Agni Datta, Archisman Dutta, Lawrence Roy
papers.summary: Polynomial-time obfuscation secure for equivalent circuit pairs possessing bounded-size Extended Frege proofs, with circuit/proof-size bounds public but proofs not supplied to the obfuscator. Assumes uniform logarithmic-input obfuscation, polynomial-security LWE at subexponential modulus/noise ratio, and a quantitative tunable discrete-log assumption.

papers.title: Kendall–tau Center Admits a PTAS
papers.authors: Diptarka Chakraborty, Debarati Das, Anish Mukherjee
papers.summary: Deterministic PTAS for Kendall–tau 1-center of arbitrarily many complete rankings on arbitrarily many candidates, time (nd+1)^O_epsilon(1). A constant-size input subset determines movement intervals containing one near-optimal ranking; discretized sorting keys, influential-variable fixing and joint LP optimization handle all maximum-distance constraints.

papers.title: On Robust Promise CSPs: A Boolean Dichotomy, Sharp Quantitative Bounds, and Soft-Equality Transfer
papers.authors: Shaowei Cai, Tao Jiang, Mengchuan Zou
