papers.summary: Claims a robust-solvability dichotomy for fixed signed symmetric Boolean promise templates, logarithm-free square-root robustness for mode/conservative-separable classes, and quantitative soft-equality transfer with a sharp universal exponent loss. Hardness statements retain UGC and the stated deterministic/randomized complexity assumptions.

papers.title: Synergies between Proof Complexity and Cryptography
papers.authors: Halley Goldberg, Mandar Juvekar, Valentine Kabanets
papers.classification_note: Principal conclusion is complexity hardness; cryptography supplies assumptions.
papers.summary: Combining subexponentially secure iO with no infinitely-often subexponentially optimal proof system yields almost-everywhere circuit hardness in quasipolynomial unambiguous classes, conditional UP intersection coUP hardness, and non-Levin NP-hardness of implicit gap MCSP.

papers.title: Uniform convergence at optimal rate and scale
papers.authors: Noga Alon, Steve Hanneke, Shay Moran, Tom Waknine
papers.summary: Obtains uniform convergence at the optimal fat-shattering scale: fat_gamma(F)=d gives deviation at most gamma+epsilon from O((d+log(1/delta))/epsilon^2) samples, with a matching worst-case lower bound. Approximate disambiguation of partial classes and a recentered chaining argument preserve the leading approximation constant.

papers.title: Agnostic Learning by Imitating
papers.authors: Sílvia Casacuberta, Parikshit Gopalan, Varun Kanade, Omer Reingold, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Pranay Tankala
papers.summary: Adaptive multiaccuracy-oracle access is computationally and statistically equivalent to agnostic learning for arbitrary model classes and fixed feature distributions, and supports stronger omniprediction/calibration objectives.

papers.title: Breaking the Quadratic Time Barrier for Flow Sparsifiers via Schur Complement Localization
papers.authors: Gramoz Goranci, Monika Henzinger, Ali Momeni Mohammadabadi, Harald Raecke, AR Sricharan
papers.summary: For undirected capacitated graphs with k prescribed terminals, constructs a flow sparsifier on exactly those terminals with quality O(log^(5/2) k) in randomized high-probability soft-O(m^(3/2) log U) time. Related Steiner oblivious-routing and multicut applications trade quality for faster construction.

papers.title: Faster Deterministic Distributed Matching: Breaking the Log-Squared Barrier
papers.authors: Mohsen Ghaffari, Christoph Grunau
papers.summary: Deterministic LOCAL matching rounding achieves roughly log^(3/2)(Delta) rounds, giving (1+epsilon) cardinality approximation, log^(6/5)(n) approximation and log^(8/5)(n) maximal matching bounds through existing frameworks.

papers.title: Fine-Grained Complexity of Approximating Vector Knapsack: A Faster Algorithm and Equivalence with $k$-SUM in 2D
papers.authors: Karl Bringmann, Ariel Kulik, Karol Wegrzycki
papers.summary: In the real-RAM model, gives a (1-epsilon)-approximation for fixed d-dimensional vector knapsack in n^((d-1)/(2epsilon)+O(d)) time up to parameter/polylog factors, a near-linear (2/3-delta)-approximation in 2D, and fine-grained equivalences with exact real kSUM with k tied to 1/epsilon.

papers.title: Dictators are most informative
papers.authors: Vu Khac Ky, Tuan Tran
papers.summary: Claims the full Courtade–Kumar most-informative-Boolean-function conjecture, including its equality cases, through entropy profiles, spectral transfer and certified scalar inequalities.

papers.title: Distributed LTL Synthesis under Arbitrary Message Adversaries
papers.authors: Benedikt Bollig, Patricia Bouyer-Decitre, Matthias Függer, Dhrubajyoti Ghosh, Thomas Nowak, Nathalie Sznajder
papers.summary: Characterizes decidability of two-process LTL synthesis under omega-regular lossy-link adversaries by nowhere density of the chromatic-subdivision image in the unit interval, equivalently repeated bounded-time consensus.

papers.title: Tight Depth Lower Bounds for Stretch Amplification
papers.authors: Oliver Korten
papers.summary: Establishes tight adaptivity-depth overhead for fully black-box PRG stretch amplification, yielding tight PRG-to-PRF depth lower bounds. Proves analogous range-avoidance limitations and an oracle separation between depth and unrestricted circuit-size hardness.

papers.title: Fast mixing of the SYK model at high temperatures
papers.authors: Yiyi Cai, Yongtao Zhan, Alexander Zlokapa
papers.summary: For the quartic SYK model with Gaussian coupling scale J, proves a constant spectral gap for a specified Gaussian-filtered KMS Gibbs sampler when βJ≤1/1000, with probability at least 1−2 exp(−N); gives trace-norm mixing O(N+log(1/ε)) and polynomial-time Gibbs preparation through an existing implementation theorem. This concerns an engineered Lindbladian at high temperature, not arbitrary thermal dynamics or low-temperature SYK.

papers.title: On the Power of Determinism in Multi-Item Auctions
papers.authors: Yiannis Giannakopoulos, Johannes Hahn
papers.summary: Improves the better-of-separate-selling-and-bundling guarantee to 2.5 for independent additive values, with a 2.19 lower bound, and determines the exact two-iid-item separate-selling ratio 1+W(1/e). A flexible capped-value master revenue inequality drives further independent and iid bounds.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for k-Median++ and Improved Bounds for k-Means++
papers.authors: David Naori, Haim Kaplan
papers.summary: Analyzes standard D-sampling and oversampling against the optimal k-clustering cost. Obtains the exact metric k-median++ factor 2B(k,Δ), where B is a coupon-process recurrence, and improves Euclidean k-means++ to (1+φ)B(k,Δ). Euclidean k-median tightness is established for Δ=0; for positive oversampling its stated lower and upper constants differ. The Euclidean k-means constant is not claimed tight.

papers.title: Agnostic Product Mixed State Tomography via Robust Statistics
papers.authors: Alvan Arulandu, Ilias Diakonikolas, Daniel M. Kane, Jerry Li
papers.summary: Gives polynomial-time, polynomial-copy semi-agnostic tomography of an arbitrary n-qubit state by a product mixed state with trace error O(opt log(1/opt))+ε, using adaptive single-copy single-qubit measurements. The reduction also yields improved robust learning of binary product distributions. A pure-product corollary is nonadaptive but has the weaker O(sqrt(opt log(1/opt)))+ε error. Statistical-query lower bounds are model-specific.

papers.title: Maximal Isolating Vertex Cuts and Shredders: Structure and Applications
papers.authors: Olivier Fischer, Sorrachai Yingchareonthawornchai
papers.summary: Computes maximal connected minimum isolating vertex shores in logarithmically many max-flow calls, and lists all global minimum vertex-cut shredders with complete component certificates in randomized m^(1+o(1)) time with high probability. Also constructs weighted Steiner element-connectivity hypercacti using O(log|T| log^3 n) max-flow calls on size O(m log|T|) graphs.

papers.title: Exponential quantum speedup for F_3^n-Subset-Sum? Or, rigorous classical algorithms for Binary-Error LWE
papers.authors: Robin Kothari, Tony Metger, Ryan O'Donnell, Noah Shutty, Kewen Wu
papers.classification_note: Quantum subset-sum algorithm is the headline theorem; classical LWE decoder is a major component.
papers.summary: For random vectors in F₃ⁿ, gives a quantum algorithm finding a nonempty zero-sum subset in polynomial time from m=εn² vectors for every fixed ε>0, and a broader sample/time tradeoff. Its key classical component is a deterministic binary-error LWE decoder with a pointwise success guarantee over the random matrix, for secrets and errors independent of that matrix. No classical lower bound or proved exponential quantum separation is established.

papers.title: Lower Bounds for Adaptive Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes via the Capped Horvitz--Thompson Estimator
papers.authors: Guy Goldberg, Tom Gur, Sidhant Saraogi
papers.summary: Extends the nearly tight relaxed-LDC blocklength lower bound to arbitrary nonlinear binary encodings and adaptive decoders with two-sided error. For constant decoding radius and every fixed ε>0 it proves n≥Ωε(q⁻²(k/log k)^(1+1/((2+ε)q))); for constant q this is k^(1+Ω(1/q)), and constant rate forces q=Ω(log k/log log k).

papers.title: Efficiently Learning SYK Hamiltonians
papers.authors: Anurag Anshu, Srinivasan Arunachalam, Sitan Chen, Yeongwoo Hwang
papers.summary: Learns quartic Gaussian SYK couplings from Gibbs states at every fixed known inverse temperature β>0 to arbitrary normalized squared error ε in poly(min{β,1}^(−1),2^(β²),n,ε^(−1),log(1/δ)) resources, for all but O_β(1/n) Hamiltonians. A separate fixed-time evolution algorithm learns coupling direction up to sign, with polynomial resources and total evolution time proportional to the supplied t*.

papers.title: Query-optimal quantum simulation of Lindblad evolution
papers.authors: Chunhao Wang, Christopher Ye
papers.summary: Simulates general time-independent Lindblad evolution in diamond norm with optimal block-encoding query dependence O(1+tau+log(1/epsilon)/log(e+log(1/epsilon)/tau)), tau=t(alpha_H+sum_j alpha_j^2). Requires controlled Hamiltonian/jump block encodings and adjoints. Gives near-optimal additional gate dependence with explicit jump/ancilla costs.

papers.title: Linear-length cycles in the supercritical percolated hypercube
papers.authors: Michael Anastos
papers.summary: For every sufficiently small fixed epsilon>0, bond percolation of Q_d at p=(1+epsilon)/d has, with high probability as d grows, a cycle of length Theta(epsilon^2 2^d), constructible in O(d^2 2^(2d)) time. Also estimates giant-component 2-core size as (2epsilon^2+O(epsilon^3))2^d. Epsilon is fixed, not an arbitrary shrinking critical-window parameter.

papers.title: Optimal stabilizer testing and learning with limited quantum memory
papers.authors: Srinivasan Arunachalam, Louis Schatzki
papers.summary: Claims optimal stabilizer-testing copy complexity Theta(n-k) away from the full-memory endpoint, and optimal nonadaptive learning Theta(n^2/k), with k coherent memory qubits between copies.

papers.title: Universality in random graphs via optimal linking systems: trees and beyond
papers.authors: Asaf Cohen Antonir, Lyuben Lichev, Maksim Zhukovskii
papers.summary: Proves an absolute C, independent of every fixed maximum degree Δ, such that G(n,C log n/n) contains all spanning Δ-bounded trees with high probability. Constructs spanning linking systems of optimal-order depth log n/log log n at this density, and establishes near-optimal girth conditions for universality of cycle factors over a sparse-density range.

papers.title: The Complexity of KKT Points of Quadratic Programs with Polynomially-Bounded Coefficients
papers.authors: Argyrios Deligkas, Michail Fasoulakis, Stavros Ioannidis
papers.summary: Computing an exact box-constrained KKT point of a quadratic polynomial remains CLS-complete with unary-encoded, polynomially bounded integer coefficients. In contrast, square-free quadratic polynomials with unary integer coefficients admit Boolean local search in polynomial time. This theorem does not claim hardness for inverse-polynomial approximation or constant coefficients.

papers.title: Rank-1-perturbed trickledown theorems: Mixing time of Glauber dynamics for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick model up to $\beta \le \tfrac{1}{2} + \eps$
papers.authors: Mathews Boban, Anqi Li, Shayan Oveis Gharan
papers.summary: Proves an inverse-linear spectral gap and quadratic-time Glauber mixing for the zero-field Sherrington–Kirkpatrick model up to inverse temperature 1/2+0.00005, with high probability over the random interaction matrix.

papers.title: Multiplicative and Additive Extractors for Low Entropy Samplable Sources Under Reduced Assumptions
papers.authors: Marshall Ball, Eshan Chattopadhyay, Mohit Gurumukhani, Ronen Shaltiel, Yunya Zhao
papers.summary: Under exponential nondeterministic-circuit hardness for E, constructs seedless extractors for polynomial-size samplable sources: one bit at constant error from O(log n) entropy, and almost all entropy with polynomially small error from n^α entropy for any fixed α>0, including a multiplicative guarantee. Under Σ₂-circuit hardness, obtains almost-all extraction at polylogarithmic entropy. The constructions extend to samplers with nondeterministic postselection.

papers.title: Optimal Approximation Algorithms For Satisfiable Ordering CSPs
papers.authors: Yury Makarychev
papers.summary: For every fixed finite ordering constraint language, characterizes the polynomial-time approximation threshold on completely satisfiable instances via transformations of solutions to both canonical left and right relaxations. The algorithm is unconditional; matching perfect-completeness hardness assumes the Rich 2-to-1 Games Conjecture. In particular it matches the 1/2 algorithm for satisfiable Betweenness.

papers.title: Approximate Polynomial Satisfiability is in the Counting Hierarchy
papers.authors: Nikhil Balaji, Mahsa Shirmohammadi, Sébastien Tavenas, James Worrell
papers.summary: Places approximate polynomial satisfiability over rational and finite-field coefficients in the counting hierarchy, improving PSPACE. The problem is origin membership in a polynomial image closure over the algebraic closure, not fixed-tolerance numerical feasibility.

papers.title: Small classes have linear neighbourhood complexity
papers.authors: John Sylvester, Viktor Zamaraev, Maksim Zhukovskii
papers.summary: Proves that every hereditary graph class of labelled speed at most n!cⁿ has linear neighbourhood complexity. Consequences include O(log²n)-bit adjacency labels, improving O(log³n), and known algorithmic consequences for this class. Linear distance-r neighbourhood complexity for every fixed r remains open.

papers.title: Faster Polynomial Factorization over Finite Fields via Batched Modular Composition
papers.authors: Zhenyu Xiong, Mingsheng Wang
papers.summary: Claims Las Vegas finite-field polynomial factorization in n^1.5532+o(1) log q field operations, uniformly in characteristic, via batched modular composition. Also extends the n^((ω+3)/4) single-composition exponent to arbitrary arguments modulo separable polynomials.

papers.title: High-Magnetization Sampling at Low Temperatures: Ising Models and Bayesian Sparse Linear Regression
papers.authors: Syamantak Kumar, Purnamrita Sarkar, Kevin Tian, Yusong Zhu
papers.summary: For each fixed inverse temperature β, samples high-magnetization SK slices k≤c_β d in polynomial time under arbitrary external fields. High-field SK sampling reaches within a constant factor of the asymptotic Almeida–Thouless line; reaching the asymptotically exact line additionally assumes the signs of the mean vector. Bayesian Gaussian spike-and-slab posterior sampling improves measurements from roughly k³ log³d to k^(3/2)log²d+k log³d, uniformly over signal-to-noise ratios.

papers.title: Even Coarse Matching Estimates Require Nearly Linear Streaming Space
papers.authors: Gillat Kol
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Proves nearly linear streaming space for even coarse maximum-matching size estimates, allowing both polynomial approximation factors and polynomially many passes. The hard graphs are simple bipartite graphs in vertex arrival with known bipartition.

papers.title: Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes from Product Expansion
papers.authors: Mitali Bafna, Anqi Li, Quynh T. Nguyen
papers.summary: Conditional explicit binary CSS qLTCs with constant rate, relative distance, soundness and check weight, assuming Conjecture 5.6 on product expansion of structured Reed–Solomon tuples over binary extension fields. This is not an unconditional construction of good qLTCs.

papers.title: Additive $\Omega(\log^* OPT)$ Gap for Bin Packing with Three Items per Bin
papers.authors: Ilan Doron-Arad
papers.summary: For every fixed epsilon>0, constructs bin-packing instances with all sizes in (1/3-epsilon,1/3+epsilon) intersect (1/4,1/2) exhibiting additive Omega(log* OPT) configuration-LP gaps and NP-hardness of additive o(log* OPT) approximation. Also transfers any instance I to such a three-item instance J with LP(J)=M=O((LP(I)+1)^4) and OPT(I)-LP(I)<=3+96(OPT(J)-LP(J)).

papers.title: The Exact Online Threshold for the Asymmetric Binary Perceptron
papers.authors: Sunghyeon Jo, Taekyun Lee
papers.summary: Exact online feasibility threshold alpha_on(kappa)=2/(pi E_*(kappa)) for the Gaussian asymmetric binary perceptron, with signs irrevocably chosen as columns arrive. E_* is a Brownian control problem with an essential-supremum-in-time L2 drift budget. Below threshold a deterministic O(MN)-arithmetic online algorithm succeeds with high probability; at zero margin certified bounds give 0.327479... <= alpha_on(0) < 0.366634....

papers.title: Multi-Party Error Resilience beyond $\frac{1}{n}$
papers.authors: Klim Efremenko, Gillat Kol, Raghuvansh Saxena, Zhijun Zhang
papers.summary: Characterizes adaptive information dissemination resilience as Θ(1/√n) in collision-as-silence radio broadcast, allowing receiver-specific corruptions. Crucial correctness condition: every receiver with at most 10δ local corruption must learn all n inputs; at least 90% qualify. It does not guarantee every receiver under a global δ budget. The protocol uses soft-O_η(n^(3/2+η)) rounds for one-bit inputs, not constant rate.

papers.title: Near-Linear Estimation of Network Unreliability
papers.authors: Mu-Xia Sun
papers.summary: Claims an unbiased relative approximation to all-terminal network unreliability in expected O(m log²n ε^−2 log(1/δ)) time for arbitrary independent edge-failure probabilities. A central structural result bounds simultaneous distinct-cut failures by O(u^3/2) for polynomially small unreliability u.

papers.title: Some algebraic and geometric computations in CH via Chow forms
papers.authors: Robert Andrews, Abhibhav Garg, Rafael Oliveira, Éric Schost
papers.summary: Places several Chow-form evaluation/support, equidimensional membership and approximate polynomial satisfiability decision problems in CH, and component degrees in FP^CH, via uniform constant-depth exponential-size threshold circuits. Main Q-input results use constant-free algebraic circuits. Image-closure Theorem 1.6 assumes an irreducible variety of dimension p-1 mapping to C^p; APS is separately extended to the listed finite/number/function fields.

papers.title: Finding full immersions is fixed-parameter tractable in labeled tour graphs
papers.authors: Hadas Barabash, Jim Geelen, Rose McCarty, Caleb McFarland, Paul Wollan
papers.summary: Claims fixed-parameter O_H(n^5) full-immersion testing for binary-vector-labelled 4-regular tour graphs, with vertex-minor consequences for apex circle graphs and an algorithmic rooted circuit-decomposition min–max theorem.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Sublinear Metric Steiner Tree
papers.authors: Sepideh Mahabadi, Mohammad Roghani, Jakub Tarnawski, Ali Vakilian
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: A randomized distance-oracle estimator for metric Steiner-tree optimum uses Õ(n^{3/2}) queries and time for some fixed factor 2−η0; every fixed improvement over 2 requires Ω(n^{3/2−ε}) queries for every ε>0. This estimates cost rather than constructing a tree.

papers.title: Post-Quantum Perfect Zero-Knowledge Arguments for NP From Any One-Way Permutation
papers.authors: Frédéric Dupuis, Rémi Ligez, Khaireddine Medhioub, Louis Salvail, Louis-Charles Thibodeau
papers.classification_note: Classical protocol but quantum-security recording theorem is central; assigned quantum, borderline cryptography.
papers.summary: From a post-quantum one-way permutation, proves security properties of NOVY commitments and constructs classical-communication post-quantum perfect zero-knowledge arguments for NP, with constant soundness 14/15 before amplification. A recording theorem permits polynomially many accepting answers per challenge without assuming collapsing.

papers.title: The One-and-a-Half Johnson Bound Is Tight for Proximity Gaps of General Linear Codes
papers.authors: Scott Duke Kominers, Justin Thaler, Kai Zhe Zheng
papers.summary: Proves that the one-and-a-half Johnson radius is the exact general-linear-code threshold for proximity gaps, constructing counterexamples at every relative distance and refuting a proposed unique-decoding-radius extension.

papers.title: Dynamic Approximate Text Indexing
papers.authors: Panagiotis Charalampopoulos, Jonas Ellert, Jakub Radoszewski
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: A dynamic approximate text index with polylogarithmic update overhead for constant mismatch/edit budget, matching static k-errata-tree tradeoffs up to logarithmic factors and supporting character insertions and deletions.

papers.title: Data-Dependent Probability Estimation via Sample Amplification
papers.authors: Vitaly Feldman, Satyen Kale, Mahbod Majid, Kunal Talwar
papers.summary: An efficient estimator answers an arbitrary event or bounded query chosen after seeing its entire sample, reaching constant mean squared error with soft-O(√d) samples on a d-point domain, without stability or symmetry assumptions.

papers.title: Packing Bins in the Euclidean Plane: An Almost-Optimal Approximation for Unsplittable Capacitated Vehicle Routing
papers.authors: Jannis Blauth, Fabrizio Grandoni, Bence Mátravölgyi, Ramin Mousavi, Kinter Ren, Mohammad R. Salavatipour
papers.summary: For unsplittable Euclidean planar CVRP with arbitrary binary integer capacity/demands, obtains a polynomial-time (3/2+ε)-approximation, meeting the bin-packing lower frontier; polynomially bounded capacity permits a PTAS.

papers.title: Optimal Dynamic Strings in Compressed Space
papers.authors: Anouk Duyster, Tomasz Kociumaka, Hanna Komlós
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Persistent dynamic strings with optimal logarithmic update time and compressed space measured by the current live collection, including reclamation after deletion and PILLAR queries.

papers.title: XOR Functions and Beyond in the Random Query Model
papers.authors: Sumegha Garg, Janani Sundaresan, Santhoshini Velusamy
papers.summary: Randomized bounded-error query algorithms for XOR functions g(x,y)=f(x⊕y) satisfy T(S+log T)=Ω(n sens(g)); a general degeneracy bound gives TS=soft-Ω(n dgn(f)). Gives nearly quadratic tradeoffs for low-influence examples and matching symmetric-function algorithms up to logarithms.

papers.title: A $(3+\epsilon)$-Approximation for Fair $k$-Means and a Matching Lower Bound
papers.authors: Kangke Cheng, Guanlin Mo, Shihong Song, Hu Ding
papers.summary: A drift-regularized convex relaxation plus a ρ-approximation for weighted k-means gives exactly fair fractional assignments within 2ρ+1+ε; fixed dimension yields 3+ε. Claims NP-hardness below 3 even on a line with overlapping groups. Integral rounding permits additive fairness violations, not exact integral fairness. Also improves k-sparse Wasserstein barycenters.

papers.title: Sampling Colorings on $G(n, d/n)$ via Glauber Dynamics
papers.authors: Leon Schiller
papers.summary: For every fixed 0<ε≤1/2, sufficiently large fixed d, and q≥d+d^{1/2+ε}, Glauber dynamics on G(n,d/n) mixes with high probability in O_{d,ε}(n^{2+ζ}(1+log(1/δ))), ζ=C_ε log(q)/d^ε. The almost-quadratic interpretation assumes q=O(d). Uses hub-containing disjoint tree/unicyclic blocks and a Bochner block-elimination argument.

papers.title: Mutual Correlated Agreement and List-Decoding: Improvements and Separations
papers.authors: Ignacio Manzur
papers.summary: Improves mutual correlated agreement bounds for polynomial generators, strengthens the finite-list list-decoding implication, and separates list-decoding from MCA for general linear codes.

papers.title: Near-Optimal One-Way Functions, Direct Product Hardness and Hash Functions from iO and NP versus coNP
papers.authors: Rahul Ilango, Alex Lombardi, Yaxin Tu
papers.summary: Assuming subexponentially secure iO and NP not contained infinitely often in coNP/poly, constructs one-way functions with inversion probability at most 2^(−n+n^ε) against polynomial-time adversaries, with near-optimal direct-product hardness and related hash constructions. The claim concerns very small success probabilities for polynomial-time adversaries, rather than near-exponential running-time hardness.

papers.title: Zero-Knowledge PCPs of Quasilinear Size via Locally Simulatable Sheaf Codes
papers.authors: Hadas Zeilberger, Jack O'Connor, Tom Gur, Nicholas Spooner
papers.classification_note: Classical zero-knowledge PCP construction; PCP/complexity primary, cryptography secondary.
papers.summary: Constructs constant-query perfect zero-knowledge PCPs for NTIME(T) of length soft-O(T+b²), secure against verifiers making b proof queries. Thus b up to roughly √T is compatible with quasilinear length. Locally simulatable sheaf codes replace the interactive proximity component of earlier constructions.

papers.title: Nash Equilibria, Variational Inequalities, and Fixed Points: Beating Brute Force via Smoothed Analysis
papers.authors: Idan Attias, Yuval Dagan, Constantinos Daskalakis, Rui Yao, Manolis Zampetakis
papers.summary: Under pointwise bounded-density and Lipschitz assumptions, a deterministic cover-refinement algorithm finds approximate fixed points with expected C^n P_v Vol(B_n) log(1/epsilon) evaluations; VI uses projection with separate boundary density. For m-player n-action games with deviation-payoff vector density at most M^(mn), expected (CmM)^(mn) log(m/epsilon) evaluations. A separate first-order homotopy theorem gives another smoothed bound under stronger joint derivative densities.

papers.title: Lossless Hardness Condensation in Deterministic Communication Complexity
papers.authors: Simon Mackenzie
papers.summary: Every finite total Boolean matrix of deterministic fixed-leaf-output communication complexity c≥4 contains an original 2^k-square with k≥(εc−4)/3 and complexity ≥(1−ε)(k+1). Gives a fixed-size c/3−O(log c) guarantee and doubly-exponential-parameter constructive extraction.

papers.title: Faster Solvers for Sparse Systems with Large Spectral Outliers
papers.authors: Yang P. Liu, Hoai-An Nguyen, Richard Peng, Junzhao Yang
papers.summary: For full-column-rank A with all but k largest eigenvalues of A^T A well-conditioned, claims randomized relative-error solve in subpolynomial factors times k^omega+(nnz(A)+k^{3/2}sqrt(d))log(1/epsilon) bit operations. Assumes O(log d)-bit input, n polynomial in d, known polynomial condition-number bound and inverse-polynomial accuracy. Same bound for least squares.

papers.title: An Efficient Minimax-Optimal Algorithm for Adversarial m-Set Bandits
papers.authors: Francesco Bacchiocchi, Tommaso Cesari, Roberto Colomboni
papers.summary: Claims a polynomial-time m-set aggregate-feedback bandit algorithm with high-probability regret O(√(dT log(binomial(d,m)/δ))) against adaptive non-anticipating adversaries, and a matching lower bound. For m=1 the lower bound claims to close the remaining √log K confidence-regret gap.

papers.title: d-DNNF is Not Polynomially Closed Under Negation
papers.authors: Marcelo Arenas, Oliver Broadrick, Vincent Liew, Guy Van den Broeck
papers.summary: There are n-variable functions with O(n)-size deterministic decomposable negation normal forms whose complements require 2^Ω(n)-size even nondeterministic DNNFs. Also gives a structured-case quasipolynomial separation and automata/grammar consequences.

papers.title: Online Beck--Fiala Down to Logarithmic Sparsity
papers.authors: Dylan Altschuler, Konstantin Tikhomirov
papers.summary: For obliviously fixed d-sparse vectors in [−1,1]^n, achieves Oη(√d) discrepancy simultaneously over all prefixes, with failure at most CηT exp(−cηd/log^(2+η)(ed)). Thus the optimal scale holds down to d≈log T·(log log T)^(2+η), and resolves the online Spencer regime.

papers.title: An Improved Streaming Algorithm for Exact Pattern Matching
papers.authors: Paweł Gawrychowski, Wojciech Janczewski, Ce Jin, Jelani Nelson
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Exact streaming pattern matching for m≤n≤2m in O(log n log log n) bits, with one-sided error at most 1/log n over all reported positions. Gives general length/error bounds and a similar-space smallest-period algorithm below any fixed fraction less than 1/2.

papers.title: Succinct arguments for QMA in Microcrypt
papers.authors: Baocheng Sun, Zihan Hu
papers.summary: Claims succinct arguments for QMA in the plain model from succinct quantum-state commitments, with quantum verifier/communication, O(log(1/ε)) rounds and O(λ log n log(1/ε)) communication. This avoids assuming quantum PCP or post-quantum one-way functions, using direct witness extraction and an auxiliary outer collector.

papers.title: Balanced Fair Division
papers.authors: Benjamin Cookson, Jakob de Raaij, Max Dupre la Tour, Nisarg Shah
papers.summary: Balanced EF[1,1] exists for arbitrary identical valuations and any number of agents, and arbitrary heterogeneous valuations when the number is a prime power. For equal bundle size q, t-swapEF always exists for q<=2t, but may fail for q>=2t+1 for sufficiently many agents, even identical strictly monotone submodular valuations. Also derives sharp balanced density partitions.

papers.title: Shannon Rate Seeded Codes from Indistinguishability Obfuscation
papers.authors: Jesko Dujmovic, George Lu, Jad Silbak, Daniel Wichs
papers.summary: Binary public-seeded deterministic codes attain rate1−H(p)−epsilon against polynomial-time errors: list decoding for p<1/2 assuming iO and strongly robust public-key PRCs; unique decoding for p<1/4 additionally needs subexponential LWE, DDH, QR or DCR. Standard-model guarantee is selective in message; adaptive message choice is obtained in ROM. Robust PRCs are instantiated under noisy-McEliece variants.

papers.title: Anchored Extra-Proximal Methods: Optimal Higher-Order Methods for Monotone Inclusion Problems
papers.authors: Ruichen Jiang, TaeHo Yoon
papers.summary: For monotone F with Lp-Lipschitz (p−1)st derivative and maximal monotone H, anchored extra-proximal methods attain tangent residual ε in soft-O((Lp R^p/ε)^(2/(3p−1))) pth-order oracle calls. Matching deterministic lower bounds allow dimension at least 2N+1; nonexpansive fixed-point complexity is the minimum of this rate and R/ε. Taylor-model inclusion solves are additional work, not bounded general arithmetic operations.

papers.title: The Quartic Gap Between Quantum and Dequantized Algorithms for Linear Algebra Is Tight
papers.authors: Shouvanik Chakrabarti, Dylan Herman, Junhyung Lyle Kim, Guneykan Ozgul
papers.summary: Dense linear systems with any prescribed constant condition bound κ0>1 require Ω(ρ⁴/log ρ) classical sampling/query accesses but Θ(ρ) coherent accesses to sample their solutions within sufficiently small constant TV error, where ρ=||A||F/||A||. Extends to several positive-definite and matrix-function tasks.

papers.title: Sharp detection thresholds for random geometric graphs with polynomial average degrees
papers.authors: Hang Du, Cheng Mao, Nike Sun, Yihong Wu, Jiaming Xu
papers.classification_note: Statistical distinguishability is the main question; random graph geometry is secondary.
papers.summary: For hard-threshold spherical random geometric graphs with p→0 and np≥n^δ for fixed δ>0, KL divergence from G(n,p) vanishes when d≫(np log(1/p))³.

papers.title: Improved Algorithms in the Random-Order Model: Knapsack, GAP, and Beyond
papers.authors: Saksham Agrawal, Arindam Khan, Akash Pareek
papers.summary: For known n and uniformly random order of an adversarially fixed instance, claims 0.2564-competitive integral knapsack/GAP against integral optimum. A deterministic remaining-capacity-scaled prefix-LP algorithm is 1/e-competitive for fractional GAP against fractional optimum, extended to resource-deletion/scaling packing assignment. No small-item assumption; integral and fractional benchmarks differ.

papers.title: Metric TSP in Sublinear Time: Breaking Two Approximation
papers.authors: Amir Azarmehr, Soheil Behnezhad
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: For some absolute ε,δ,γ>0, estimates metric TSP value within factor 2−δ using O(n^(2−ε)) distance queries and O(n^(2−γ)) time, with probability at least 2/3. No MST is supplied.

papers.title: Non-signaling PCPs as Algebraic Proofs, and Total Coefficients Lower Bounds for Sherali–Adams
papers.authors: Liyan Chen, Zhengzhong Jin
papers.summary: Characterizes suitably locally computable non-signaling PCPs with Extended-Frege completeness by low-norm averaging extended Sherali–Adams refutations, with a 2^O(k) loss in one direction. Without extension variables proves exponential total-coefficient lower bounds and refutes the specified AND-code low-norm conjecture.

papers.title: Four-Message Arguments for NP \circ batchQMA and Six-Message Arguments for QMA from LWE
papers.authors: Rishab Goyal, Venkata Koppula
papers.summary: Obtains four-message all-short arguments for NP composed with batchQMA and six-message arguments for general QMA from post-quantum LWE. The structured batch statement is not a coQMA verifier, and fixed preprocessing is excluded from the online succinctness bound.

papers.title: Exponential memory/query-complexity tradeoffs in high-accuracy feasibility problems
papers.authors: Jialin Yu, Moïse Blanchard
papers.summary: Proves exponential memory/query tradeoffs for high-accuracy separation-oracle feasibility. Memory d^(1+delta) log(1/epsilon) entails at least (d log(1/epsilon)) raised to a soft-Omega(d^((1−delta)/8)) query lower bound. Randomized lower bounds permit adaptive oracles; deterministic algorithms admit a nonadaptive hard oracle.

papers.title: Dimension-Independent Anti-Concentration Certificates for Log-Concave Distributions
papers.authors: Stefan Tiegel
papers.summary: Every isotropic log-concave distribution admits dimension-independent SoS anti-concentration certificates of degree exp(O(1/δ)); κ-strongly log-concave distributions have degree O(κ^-1δ^-2+δ^-30). Includes empirical certificates for sufficiently many samples.

papers.title: Optimistic Hedge in General-Sum Games: Fundamental Limits and Regret Bounds via Temporal Approximation
papers.authors: Liad Erez, Nadav Eisen, Tomer Koren, Yuval Dagan
papers.summary: Fixed-rate Optimistic Hedge from uniform initialization has O(n log n) horizon-independent regret in all two-player general-sum games at η=c/n, but some three-player n-action games force exponential-in-n regret for every sufficiently small fixed rate, and linear-in-T regret when η≥Cn2^(-n/8).

papers.title: Constructive Arboricity in Almost-Linear Time for Dense Graphs
papers.authors: Iman Gholami, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Alireza Kaviani, Soheil Mohammadkhani, Amir Mohammad Shahrezaei
papers.summary: Constructs an optimal forest partition of a simple undirected graph in min(n^(2+o(1)),m^(4/3+o(1))) time and an additive-one partition in m^(1+o(1)). Exact dense-graph arboricity thus becomes almost-linear in input size.

papers.title: Finding Gaussian Structure in Bosonic States
papers.authors: Alvan Arulandu, Sitan Chen, Ziyun Chen, Jerry Li, Eric Ma
papers.summary: Agnostically learns the closest pure bosonic Gaussian state in infidelity: polynomial time at sufficiently high fidelity and n^poly(1/epsilon) in the general regime, with mild log-log energy dependence. Gives tolerant Gaussianity testing and separates Gaussian from non-Gaussian measurements.

papers.title: A Deterministic Approximation Scheme for Counting Read-Twice CNF Assignments
papers.authors: Yucong He
papers.summary: A deterministic bit-polynomial FPTAS for unweighted Boolean CNF with at most two total literal occurrences per variable, arbitrary signs and widths; polynomial exponent is universal. Three occurrences are NP-hard even with width two or three.

papers.title: Conservative Modular Counting at Every Odd Prime
papers.authors: Chengzhi Xie
papers.summary: Classifies fixed finite conservative CSP templates modulo every odd prime: Mal’tsev polymorphism is the FP criterion for p=3,5, while exact integer strong balance is the criterion for p≥7; otherwise #pP-complete under polynomial-time Turing reductions.

papers.title: Tight Bounds for Conservative Pointer Jumping
papers.authors: Atul Mantri
papers.summary: Determines conservative pointer-jumping communication with many players: beyond roughly log-star n, maximum messages scale as 1+n/k² and total communication as n/k+sqrt(n). Gives an optimal universal one-bit selector and improvements in general one-way and myopic models.

papers.title: Efficient Equilibrium Computation in Colonel Blotto Games
papers.authors: Martin Bichler, Abheek Ghosh
papers.summary: An FPTAS for continuous two-player Colonel Blotto with arbitrary rational budgets and common nonuniform battlefield values, nearly linear in input length for fixed ε; exact linear-time real-RAM equilibrium sampling when max_i v_i≤b/2.

papers.title: A Low-Diameter Nash-Williams--Tutte Theorem
papers.authors: Pin-Hsian Lee, Peng-Ting Lin, Meng-Tsung Tsai, Ting-An Wu
papers.classification_note: Structural low-diameter spanning-tree packing theorem with algorithmic corollary.
papers.summary: Strengthens Nash–Williams–Tutte for simple graphs: whenever k edge-disjoint spanning trees exist, they can simultaneously have diameter O(n/delta) and O((n/delta)log(delta+1)) internal vertices, with absolute constants independent of k. Gives an expected soft-O(n^5) construction.

papers.title: Memory--Sample Tradeoffs in High--Dimensional Statistics
papers.authors: Ankit Pensia, Devansh Gupta, Kabir Aladin Verchand, Vatsal Sharan, Atreya Vedantam
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.classification_note: Memory/sample tradeoff in streaming model; statistics is secondary.
papers.summary: Establishes single-pass memory/sample tradeoffs for moment-matched non-Gaussian component analysis, yielding superlinear memory barriers for Gaussian mixtures, robust estimation and related tasks. Typical bound is Omega(d²/N^(2/m)); sparse variants use dk instead of d².

papers.title: On Global Joint Lower Bounds in Zeroth-Order Nonconvex Optimization
papers.authors: Yuxuan Xia, Xiao-Tong Yuan
papers.summary: Global zeroth-order stationarity lower bound Ω(d L0² min{ΔH,L0²}/ε⁴) against adaptive randomized algorithms with unrestricted exact scalar queries, sample-label reuse and outputs, under ε²≤c min{ΔH,L0²} and d≥C(B/ε²)log(2+BL0²/ε⁴). Includes Goldstein and noiseless variants plus gap amplification.

papers.title: A Dichotomy Theorem for CSP-Based Ideal Membership
papers.authors: Akbar Rafiey, Ashkan Soleymani, Patrick Jaillet
papers.summary: For each fixed finite rational domain, constraint language Γ and degree d, gives a P/coNP-complete dichotomy for deciding polynomial identities on all CSP solutions. Tractability is exactly whether the identity endomorphism’s degree-d evaluation vector lies in the span of Taylor-covered endomorphisms.

papers.title: Leakage-Resilient Computation via Matrix Refreshing
papers.authors: Stefan Dziembowski, Sebastian Faust
papers.summary: Uniform invertible-matrix refresh of two inner-product shares tolerates continual local leakage with statistical error O(T2^(6λ−n/9)); a stateful Boolean compiler has O(S2^(18λ−n/27)) error and efficient simulation. Uses only-computation-leaks, private communication and erasures.

papers.title: High Confidence Yields Outlier Robustness: Consequences in Computational Hardness, Privacy, and Replicability
papers.authors: Varun Narayanan, Jasper C.H. Lee, Ankit Pensia
papers.summary: High-confidence estimators imply efficient oblivious-contamination robustness under a mild Lipschitz extension to a neighborhood of the distribution class. A different, generally inefficient construction gives adaptive robustness using twice the samples and failure √β for contamination O(log(1/β)/n). User-level reductions give optimal-parameter high-confidence-to-replicability testing.

papers.title: Nearly Exact Length Bounds for Directed Steiner Tree and Forest in Planar Graphs
papers.authors: Mirmahdi Rahgoshay, Maryam Mahboub
papers.summary: Polynomial-time bicriteria algorithms for length-constrained planar directed Steiner tree and forest preserve path lengths within 1+ε, with polylogarithmic cost approximation. The rooted integral-reference bound is O(ε⁻¹ log² k); the forest bound is O(ε⁻² log⁷ q).

papers.title: Quantum Advantage has Few Complexity Implications
papers.authors: Eli Goldin, Alex Lombardi, Tomoyuki Morimae
papers.summary: Constructs a classical oracle with P=NP and BQP=PSPACE yet polynomial-round public-coin proofs of quantumness secure against P/poly; separately a unitary oracle with BQP=QCMA and quantum-verifier oblivious state preparation.

papers.title: Learning Mixtures with Unknown Scales: Sharp Dependence on Separation
papers.authors: Shihao Wang, Xueru Zhang
papers.summary: Polynomial-time global parameter recovery for known regular radial profiles with component-specific unknown full scale matrices. Laplace rates gamma^(-7)epsilon^(-2) unrestricted weights and gamma^(-3)epsilon^(-2) equal weights, with matching fixed-1D lower bounds; epsilon<=gamma/8 and polynomial factors in supplied conditioning bounds.

papers.title: Shallow Quantum Circuits for Geometrically Local Lindblad Dynamics
papers.authors: Zheyu Shen, Yusen Wu, Xiao Yuan, Yukun Zhang
papers.summary: Simulates static finite-range Lindblad dynamics on a fixed-dimensional lattice in diamond error ε using O(nT polylog(nT/ε)) gates and O(T polylog(nT/ε)) nearest-neighbor depth, with matching leading Ω(nT) gate and Ω(T) depth lower bounds under specified models.

papers.title: Vertex Deletion on $H$-Induced-Minor-Free Graphs: Subexponential FPT Algorithms and Approximation Schemes
papers.authors: Daniel Lokshtanov, Fahad Panolan, Saket Saurabh, Jie Xue, Meirav Zehavi
papers.summary: For fixed H,t and MSO formula ϕ, deleting k vertices to treewidth≤t and ϕ on H-induced-minor-free graphs takes 2^(k^(2/3) log^O(1)k)n^O(1); hereditary targets also admit a QPTAS. Includes string-graph applications through excluded induced subdivisions.

papers.title: Forgetting Alternation and Blossoms
papers.authors: Taisuke Izumi, Naoki Kitamura, Yutaro Yamaguchi
papers.classification_note: General matching structural reduction with static, distributed and streaming consequences; graph algorithms primary.
papers.summary: Reduces maximal disjoint shortest augmenting paths in general graphs to alternation-free double paths in a DAG with O(m log n) overhead. Gives deterministic O(m√n log n) exact matching, randomized soft-O(ε^−4) CONGEST approximation and deterministic O(ε^−4) semi-streaming passes.

papers.title: Three-Round Catalytic Communication: Lower Bounds and Applications
papers.authors: Weiqiang Yuan, Jiaqing Zhu
papers.summary: Three-round catalytic communication for the explicit N×N Boolean Paley matrix requires Ω(log²N/s) catalytic bits for 1≤s=o(log N), even with average-case error≤1/3 and exact restoration on every state. Derives fixed-field Ω(log²N) rank rigidity under any fixed <1/2 corruption fraction and quasipolynomial two-probe error-correcting storage lower bounds.

papers.title: A Sharp Barrier of Consistent Submodular Maximization: Any Improvement over 2 − √2 Entails Exponential Queries or Linear Recourse
papers.authors: Shi Fu, Qixin Zhang, Dacheng Tao
papers.classification_note: Online arrivals/recourse guarantee; classified online rather than static optimization.
papers.summary: For monotone cardinality-constrained consistent maximization, proves the sharp polynomial-query/constant-worst-case-recourse threshold 2−√2: expected approximation β−ε at each fixed time with O(ε^−2) recourse; any improvement needs exponential pre-final queries or Ω(k) final changes. Coverage attains 1−1/e−ε with O(ε^−1) recourse, and bounded curvature has a matching interpolated threshold.

papers.title: Decoding Expander Walk Codes up to the Johnson Bound in Near-Linear Time
papers.authors: Silas Richelson, Sourya Roy, Madhur Tulsiani
papers.summary: List-decodes Ta-Shma expander-walk binary linear codes of bias ε and rate Ω(ε^(2+β)) at correlationρ≥2√ε in soft-O(N)(1/ε)^cβ time, cβ=(1/β)^O(1/β), for fixed0<β≤1/2.

papers.title: Sensitivity Oracles for Matroid Packing, Matroid Covering, and Matching Problems with Applications
papers.authors: Keerti Choudhary, Amit Kumar, Lakshay Saggi
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Monte Carlo sensitivity oracles support arbitrary f updates across sparse-linear-matroid packing/covering/parity and derived graph problems. Examples include exact(s,t) flow with O((fn)²) space and soft-O(f⁴) query time, and perfect matching with O(n²log n) space and O(f^ω) query time. Susceptible-set variants remove density/packing dependence.

papers.title: Low Soundness Linearity Testing on Subsets of the Hypercube
papers.authors: Yunus Aydin, Haakon Larsen, Tushant Mittal, Silas Richelson, Sourya Roy
papers.topic_label: Data structures, streaming and sublinear algorithms
papers.summary: Low-soundness linearity tests on approximate additive bases use2k+1 queries. For fixed0<p≤1/2, even-weight pn slices and p-biased cubes admit optimal1+ceil(1/p)-query parity tests; constant-weight slices admit constant queries, but growing sublinear weights do not.
